The European Parliament adopted by 477 v: The European Parliament rejected a decision to authorize genetically modified soybean MON 87708 × MON 89788 × A5547-127 for market placement due to concerns about increased herbicide use and potential residue levels.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament approved a resolution advocating for a stronger Banking Union and Capital Markets Union to enhance economic stability. They expressed concerns about remaining challenges in some financial institutions and called for intergovernmental negotiations on budgetary instruments, ensuring parliament's active participation and adherence to the Union's legal order. The resolution also acknowledged the need to address low profitability levels in the banking sector amidst a deteriorating macroeconomic environment exacerbated by COVID-19.
The European Parliament adopted by 568 v: The European Parliament approved, by 568 votes to 109, a resolution consenting to the Status Agreement between the EU and Montenegro for EU Border and Coast Guard operations. This agreement aims to provide a legal framework for EU border team deployments, outlining their tasks, powers, and respect for fundamental rights.
The European Parliament adopted by 616 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 616 votes in favor, requesting the Commission to propose by June 15, 2020, a Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) contingency plan. This plan is intended to ensure continuity for EU program beneficiaries if the MFF 2021-2027 isn't adopted in time due to delays and differences in positions between institutions. The plan will be based on relevant legal bases for each expenditure program and Article 312(4) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution advocating collective EU action against COVID-19, emphasizing unity, solidarity, and open borders for essential supplies within the Union.

The European Parliament approved a resolution on competition policy, emphasizing its role in global markets. Key points include promoting fair competition for SMEs, strengthening international cooperation with major economies, improving FDI monitoring, ensuring reciprocity in public procurement, and maintaining fair competition post-Brexit.
The European Parliament adopted by 569 v: The European Parliament approved, by 569 votes to 109, a resolution consenting to the Status Agreement between the EU and Serbia regarding actions of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency in Serbia. This agreement aims to provide a legal framework for the operation, liability rules, tasks, and powers of deployed border guard teams, ensuring respect for fundamental rights and establishing complaint mechanisms.
The European Parliament adopted by 676 v: The European Parliament approved a decision to allow cabotage transport in border regions between Germany and Switzerland, passing with 676 votes in favor, 1 against, and 13 abstentions. This move aims to enhance coach and bus services between the two countries without discrimination or competition distortion. The authorized regions are Freiburg, Tübingen (Baden-Württemberg) and Swabia (Bavaria) in Germany.
The European Parliament adopted by 634 v: The European Parliament approved a visa facilitation agreement with Belarus, passing it by 634 votes to 48. The agreement aims to simplify visa issuance for stays up to 90 days within a 180-day period for citizens of both parties. The agreement emphasizes respect for human rights and democratic principles.
The European Parliament adopted by 667 v: The European Parliament approved, by a large margin, a resolution to update the Atlantic Tunas conservation protocol, aiming to improve shark fishery management and modernize decision-making processes within the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas (ICCAT).
The European Parliament adopted by 560 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to consent to a readmission agreement with Belarus, aimed at efficient and orderly return of unauthorized residents between Belarus and EU states. The agreement was signed in January 2020, based on complete reciprocity.
The European Parliament adopted by 671 v: The European Parliament approved, by a large margin, the renewal of the Agreement on cooperation in science and technology between the EU and Ukraine for another five years. The Council's draft was endorsed, extending the partnership until 2024.
The European Parliament adopted by 575 v: The European Parliament approved an extension of the Fisheries Partnership Agreement with Mauritania, passing by 575 votes to 58. This agreement concerns fishing opportunities and financial contributions, set to expire on November 15, 2019. The extension was agreed upon in a letter exchange between the EU and Mauritania.
The European Parliament adopted by 663 v: The European Parliament approved, by a large majority, the renewal of the scientific and technological cooperation agreement between the EU and India for another five years (from May 2020 to May 2025).
The European Parliament decided by 568 v: The European Parliament approved, by 568 votes to 85, the discharge of its President for the implementation of the 2018 budget. The resolution highlighted issues in parliamentary budget management, including high rigidity in four main expenditure areas and a decrease in revenue compared to 2017.
On the basis of the report by the Commit: The European Parliament rejected a proposal allowing the UK to participate in an automated fingerprint data exchange system under the Prüm Decision, with 329 votes against and 4 abstentions. This decision aimed to facilitate cross-border criminal investigations among EU member states.
The European Parliament decided by 499 v: The European Parliament approved the Commission's implementation of the EU's 2018 budget by a vote of 499 to 136, with 56 abstentions. The Parliament acknowledged the reliability of the accounts but expressed concern over persistent errors in payments due to partially functioning supervisory systems. The Court of Auditors identified higher risk areas, particularly research expenditure and the 'Economic, social and territorial cohesion' section of the Multiannual Financial Framework.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Clean Sky 2 Joint Undertaking's budget for 2018 and closed its accounts, with 625 votes in favor, 62 against, and 6 abstentions. The joint undertaking's annual accounts were considered accurate by the Court of Auditors.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of EIOPA for the financial year 2018, and endorsed the closure of its accounts. The vote was passed with 604 votes in favor, 64 against, and 25 abstentions. The Authority's financial statements were deemed reliable and legal by the Court of Auditors.

European Parliament approved the discharge for the Fuel Cells and Hydrogen (FCH 2) Joint Undertaking's 2018 budget, with 629 votes in favor, 58 against, and 6 abstentions. The Court of Auditors confirmed the accuracy of the joint undertaking's accounts for that year. The Union contributed EUR 318.8 million to FCH2 from Horizon 2020, with additional contributions from members totaling EUR 649.4 million.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of the Bio-based Industries Joint Undertaking's budget for 2018 and closed its accounts, with a majority vote of 629 to 59. The Court of Auditors confirmed the accuracy of the joint undertaking's financial position and operations in 2018.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the IMI 2 Joint Undertaking's budget for 2018, allowing for the closure of its accounts. The decision was supported by 633 votes, with 22 votes against and 38 abstentions. The Court of Auditors confirmed the accuracy of the joint undertaking's financial position and operations for the same year.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Electronic Components and Systems for European Leadership (ECSEL) Joint Undertaking's budget for 2018 and closed its accounts, following a favorable audit report from the Court of Auditors. The vote passed with 626 in favor, 55 against, and 12 abstentions.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of the European Environment Agency (EEA) for the financial year 2018, endorsing their reliable and legal annual accounts. The final budget for EEA in 2018 was €65.8 million, with a budget implementation rate of 99.96%. Other observations were made regarding performance, staff, procurement, and internal controls.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of EMSA for 2018, endorsing their reliable annual accounts. The final budget for EMSA in 2018 was €106.7 million, with a budget implementation rate of 99.02%. Other observations were made regarding performance, staff policy, procurement, and internal controls.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of the GNSS Agency for 2018, endorsing their reliable financial statements worth €32.2 million. The budget implementation rate was 100%, with an execution rate of payment appropriations at 83.7%.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Shift2Rail Joint Undertaking's 2018 budget and accounts, passing with a majority vote. The decision includes recommendations for budget management improvements, performance enhancements, and internal control adjustments.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the European Union Agency for Railways' Executive Director for the 2018 budget implementation and accounts closure. The Court of Auditors confirmed the reliability and legality of the agency's financial statements for 2018, leading to a resolution with recommendations on the agency's financial management. The final budget for 2018 was €28,793,243, with a budget implementation rate of 99.98% and a payment appropriations execution rate increase of 1.66% compared to 2017.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Director of EMCDDA for the financial year 2018, endorsing reliable annual accounts. Recommendations were made on budget management, performance, staff, procurement, and internal controls, with a final budget of €16,174,200.21, representing a 2.18% increase from 2017.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of EASA for financial year 2018, endorsing their reliable and legal annual accounts. The final budget for 2018 was €197.87 million, with a budget implementation rate of 98.31%. Other observations were made regarding performance, staff policy, procurement, and internal controls.
The European Parliament decided by 677 v: The European Parliament granted discharge to the Secretary-General of the Court of Auditors for the 2018 budget, passing with a majority of 677 votes and 3 abstentions. However, concerns were raised about persistent overbudgeting in expenditure on buildings, furniture, equipment, and miscellaneous operating costs.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of EASO for the 2018 budget, closing the accounts for that year. However, a qualified opinion was issued regarding the legality and regularity of payments in the financial years 2016 and 2017.
The European Parliament decided by 665 v: The European Parliament approved the discharge of the European Ombudsman's 2018 budget by a large margin, with sound financial management commended. The Court of Auditors found no significant issues in human resources and public procurement for the year.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Translation Centre for EU Bodies' Director for financial year 2018, endorsing the closure of accounts. The Court of Auditors confirmed the reliability and legality of the Centre's annual accounts for 2018. The Parliament adopted a resolution with recommendations on the Centre's financial statements, budget management, and other observations.
The European Parliament decided by 626 v: The European Parliament approved, by a majority of 626 votes to 56, the discharge of the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS) for their 2018 budget implementation. The Parliament commended the EDPS for prudent financial management, particularly in the establishment of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB).
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of the European Fisheries Control Agency for the financial year 2018, endorsing the closure of accounts. The Court of Auditors confirmed the reliability and legality of the agency's annual accounts for 2018.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of the EU Cybersecurity Agency for 2018, endorsing reliable financial statements with a budget increase of 2.67%. Recommendations were made on budget management, performance, staff policy, procurement, and internal controls.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of Eurojust's Administrative Director for the financial year 2018, endorsing their reliable annual accounts. The final budget for Eurojust in 2018 was €38,606,737, a decrease of 20.71% compared to 2017, primarily due to reduced administrative expenses.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Director of the European Training Foundation for the financial year 2018, endorsing their reliable and legal annual accounts. Recommendations were made regarding budget management and performance, with a high implementation rate of 99.99%.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the SESAR Joint Undertaking's budget for 2018, closing its accounts. The decision was supported by 605 votes, with 84 votes against and 4 abstentions. The resolution noted the Union's contribution for the deployment phase of SESAR 2020, expected to be around €1.6 billion from various sources.

The European Parliament approved the discharge for the Director of the Fusion Energy Joint Undertaking, allowing closure of accounts for 2018. The decision includes observations on the ITER project timeline shift from 2020 to 2025 and potential impacts of UK's Euratom withdrawal post-2020.

The European Parliament approved the discharge for the Director of BEREC's Agency budget for 2018 and closed the accounts, following assurances from the Court of Auditors about the reliability and legality of the transactions. A resolution with recommendations was adopted, addressing concerns over staff turnover affecting the implementation of BEREC's work program.
The European Parliament decided by 597 v: The European Parliament approved, by a majority of 597 votes to 97, the discharge of the High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy regarding the 2018 budget of the European External Action Service (EEAS). The resolution emphasized the need for increased audit focus on operational expenditure and critical areas like cybersecurity. The total budget was €678.5 million, with an implementation rate of 99.9% for commitments and 84.8% for payments.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge for the Executive Director of CEDEFOP, allowing closure of accounts for the 2018 financial year. This decision follows assurances from the Court of Auditors about the reliability and legality of the center's annual accounts in 2017. The Parliament adopted a resolution with recommendations on CEDEFOP's financial statements, budget management, and other observations related to performance, procurement, and staff policy.

The European Parliament approved the reliable financial statements of Eurofound for 2018, granting discharge and closing accounts. Recommendations were made on budget management, procurement, staff policy, and internal controls, with a final budget of €20,760,000 for 2018.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Director of ACER for the financial year 2018, endorsing reliable annual accounts. Recommendations were made on budget management and other areas, with a budget increase of 2.18% compared to 2017 and a high implementation rate of 99.26%. Other observations included procurement, staff policy, and internal controls.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Director of the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT) for the financial year 2018, endorsing the closure of accounts. The resolution contained recommendations for improving the EIT's financial statement and management, with a focus on increasing budget efficiency.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Euratom Supply Agency's Director-General for 2018 and closed the agency's accounts, with a majority vote. Recommendations were made to improve budget management, addressing high cancellation rates of appropriations carried over from 2017.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of eu-LISA for the financial year 2018 and closed the accounts, following assurances from the Court of Auditors about the reliability and legality of the agency's annual accounts. A resolution with recommendations was adopted, addressing the Agency's financial statements and budget management for the year. The final budget increased by 32%, and despite a low budget implementation rate of 75.18%, the payment appropriations execution rate was 94.08%.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Director of the European Institute for Gender Equality (EIGE) for the financial year 2018, endorsing their reliable annual accounts. The final budget for EIGE in 2018 was €7,981,001.45, with a budget implementation rate of 99.38% and a payment appropriations execution rate of 81.15%. Other observations were made regarding performance, staff policy, procurement, and internal controls.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of ESMA for the financial year 2018, and endorsed the closure of its accounts. The decision includes recommendations on the reliability and legality of the Authority's financial statements, with a budget increase of 5.02% compared to 2017.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of the European Banking Authority for 2018, and endorsed the closure of its accounts. The vote passed with 607 in favor, 81 against, and 5 abstentions. The final budget for 2018 was €42,584,409, an increase due to the relocation process to Paris. The Authority's financial statements were deemed reliable by the Court of Auditors.
The European Parliament decided by 454 v: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Commission for the implementation of the budgets of the Eighth to Eleventh European Development Funds (EDFs) in 2018, with a vote of 454 to 210. The Parliament noted that commitments and payments exceeded targets, while encouraging continued efforts on old contracts and prioritizing closure of operations for the eighth and ninth EDFs.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) for the financial year 2018, endorsing their reliable annual accounts. The final budget for EFSA in 2018 was €79,183,814.25, with a budget implementation rate of 100% and a payment appropriations execution rate of 91.31%. Other observations were made regarding performance, staff policy, procurement, and internal controls.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of CEPOL for the financial year 2018, endorsing the closure of accounts. The Court of Auditors confirmed the reliability and legality of the agency's annual accounts for this period.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) for the financial year 2018, endorsing the closure of the accounts. The Court of Auditors confirmed the reliability and legality of the agency's annual accounts for the same period.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Director of the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) for the 2018 financial year, with a resolution containing recommendations on the ECDC's financial statements and management. The final budget for 2018 was €58 million, primarily funded by the Union budget, despite some expenses incurred in Swedish krona due to the Centre's location outside the Eurozone.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Director of the European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights for 2017, and endorsed the closure of its accounts. The Parliament adopted a resolution with recommendations for the agency's financial management in 2018, following assurances from the Court of Auditors that the accounts are reliable and legal.
The European Parliament decided by 486 v: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Secretary-General of the Committee of the Regions for their 2018 budget implementation by a vote of 486 to 90, with 15 abstentions. The Parliament commended the Committee's prudent financial management in 2018, noting high commitment and payment rates.
The European Parliament adopted by 542 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to set the budget for 2021 at €2,090,467,628, an increase of 2.54% over the 2020 budget. Members emphasized the need for cost-effective use of resources, careful planning, and transparency in public procurement to enhance legislative effectiveness and citizen engagement.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency for 2018, with a resolution containing recommendations on their financial statements and management. The final budget for 2018 was €288 million, with a budget implementation rate of 98.37%. Concerns were raised about the low payment appropriations execution rate (69.69%).

The European Parliament approved the financial discharge for Europol's 2018 operations and closed the year's accounts, following assurances from the Court of Auditors about the reliability and legality of the transactions. A resolution with recommendations on budget management and other aspects was adopted.
The European Parliament adopted by 505 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution (505-119) to prioritize citizens in the new multiannual financial framework. They called for a €2 trillion recovery fund, financed by long-term bonds, to support SMEs, Green Deal, and digital agenda, with funds administered by the Commission and subject to parliamentary scrutiny.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge of the European Medicines Agency's Executive Director for the financial year 2018, endorsing the closure of accounts. The Court of Auditors confirmed the reliability and legality of the agency's annual accounts for 2018.
The European Parliament decided by 605 v: The European Parliament voted to establish a committee investigating alleged violations in enforcing animal protection laws during transport within and outside the EU, passing with 605 votes in favor, 53 against, and 31 abstentions. The committee will focus on the effectiveness of enforcement by the Commission and Member States regarding regulations on animal transport, including vehicle approvals, watering, feeding, temperature controls, and more. The committee will submit its final report within a year.
The European Parliament adopted by 603 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, 603-84, regarding the performance, financial management, and control of EU agencies' 2018 budget. The resolution includes cross-agency observations for each EU agency influencing policy development in areas like safety, security, health, research, economics, and justice.
The European Parliament decided by 574 v: The European Parliament approved the establishment of a special committee on AI in the digital age, aiming to analyze its impact on various sectors, investigate challenges, and define EU objectives over the medium- and long-term. The committee will use several Commission communications as a starting point.
The European Parliament adopted by 532 v: The European Parliament approved a recommendation, by 532 votes to 70 with 63 abstentions, emphasizing the importance of integrating Western Balkan countries into the EU for regional stability and peace. The Parliament urged strengthening the accession process to promote rule of law, democratic transformation, and good neighborly relations.
The European Parliament decided by 605 v: The European Parliament approved, by 605 votes to 76, the budget implementation for the Court of Justice of the EU in 2018, acknowledging effective financial management and prudence shown by the court.
The European Parliament decided by 548 v: The European Parliament passed a vote (548-83) to establish a special committee investigating foreign interference in EU democratic processes, including disinformation. The committee will analyze breaches of electoral rules, enhance countermeasures, assess methods for restricting political funding, and suggest EU-level actions against hybrid threats.
The European Parliament adopted by 448 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (448-115) for the 2021 budget, focusing on mitigating COVID-19 impacts, supporting recovery, and prioritizing the European Green Deal and digital transformation. The budget aims to rebuild the EU economy, ensuring resilience and inclusion while addressing health risks and creating jobs, particularly in sectors like tourism and strategic areas such as healthcare.
The European Parliament decided by 669 v: The European Parliament postponed its approval of the budget for the European Economic and Social Committee for 2018, following allegations of harassment against a committee member. The Parliament requested the committee to address OLAF's recommendations on this matter by September 2020.
The European Parliament adopted the reso: The European Parliament approved a resolution for the post-2020 European Disability Strategy, aiming to ensure equal rights and opportunities for people with disabilities in education, employment, and society. The strategy addresses the underrepresentation of over 100 million individuals with disabilities in the EU, particularly women and children. It aligns with the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD).
The European Parliament decided by 643 v: The European Parliament postponed a decision on discharging funds to the Council for 2018 budget implementation, voting 643-37 with 11 abstentions. The Parliament praised the Council's sound financial management but expressed concern about budget over-estimates and called for improvements.
The European Parliament adopted by 528 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 528 votes in favor, to initiate the Conference on the Future of Europe as soon as possible in autumn 2020. The resolution emphasizes the need for EU reform amidst the COVID-19 crisis and calls for swift negotiations between the Council and Commission to establish the conference before summer.
The European Parliament adopted by 520 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (520 votes, 86 against) urging a swift return to a fully operational Schengen area, emphasizing the need for targeted restrictions instead of internal border controls during the COVID-19 pandemic. They also called for improved communication and minimum health checks among Member States to preserve freedom of movement and aid economic recovery.
The European Parliament adopted a legisl: The European Parliament approved a resolution to amend EU banking rules in response to COVID-19, providing temporary relief for banks to increase lending. Measures include adjusting accounting standards, extending preferential treatment for guaranteed loans, delaying the leverage ratio buffer application, and bringing forward certain capital relief measures.
The European Parliament adopted by 565 v: The European Parliament condemned China's national security law for Hong Kong, viewing it as a threat to the city's autonomy and fundamental freedoms. The resolution passed with 565 votes in favor, 34 against, and 62 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 587 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 587 votes in favor, calling for swift support for the tourism and transport sectors post-COVID-19. The aim is to modernize, sustain, and make these sectors more accessible to people with disabilities. Support for tourist areas is emphasized, contingent on health regulations and uniform assessment criteria across the EU.
The European Parliament adopted by 653 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation for smooth transition between the current and future EU agricultural policy, allowing continued payments from the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF) and the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) in 2021 and 2022. New commitments can have a longer than three-year period as decided by Member States.
The European Parliament adopted by 593 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (593 votes, 34 against, 38 abstentions) to protect cross-border and seasonal workers affected by COVID-19. The resolution urges Member States to lift travel restrictions and discriminatory measures for these workers, ensuring their health and safety while preventing labor shortages in key sectors.
The European Parliament adopted by 510 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 510 votes in favor and 53 against, urging an investigation into potential misuse of EU funds and conflicts of interest by the Czech Prime Minister. The resolution was initiated by multiple groups, including EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens/EFA, ECR, and GUE/NGL, due to the PM's involvement in EU budget implementation while leading Agrofert Group, a conglomerate with over 34,000 employees. The resolution specifically addressed the 'Stork Nest' project, where Agrofert artificially created a company to obtain funds for small businesses. The criminal investigation into this matter was recently reopened by the Czech Prosecutor General.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament approved additional funding for biomedical research on Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME/CFS), a debilitating chronic disease affecting millions globally, including around 2 million in the EU. The aim is to coordinate research efforts and improve understanding of this complex condition through initiatives like Euromene.
The European Parliament adopted by 437 v: The European Parliament approved an agreement on Euro-Mediterranean aviation with Israel by 437 votes to 102, with 147 abstentions. The agreement, signed in 2013, aims to align Israeli aviation regulations closely with the EU's and includes safeguards for fair competition, labor standards, passenger rights, and environmental cooperation.
The European Parliament adopted by 609 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to allocate €345,000 from the EU budget for technical assistance under the European Globalisation Adjustment Fund (EGF) in 2020. This aims to support workers affected by globalization and economic crises, with a focus on monitoring and data gathering related to COVID-19 challenges.
The European Parliament adopted by 572 v: The European Parliament approved a recommendation for negotiations with the UK on a new partnership, passing by 572 votes to 34, with 91 abstentions. Despite four rounds of talks, significant differences remain, and the Parliament expressed concern over the UK's limited future partnership scope and fragmented approach. The Parliament also emphasized that the UK's proposals do not meet its commitments under the Withdrawal Agreement, particularly regarding security and defense matters. The Parliament reiterated the need for progress in all areas of negotiation, and supports a comprehensive draft treaty over separate agreements.
The European Parliament adopted by 682 v: The European Parliament approved an agreement with Switzerland to modify their WTO concessions on seasoned meat, following a dispute over increased customs duties. The Council authorized negotiations for compensation, which includes increasing a WTO tariff rate quota for beef by 1200 tonnes.
The European Parliament adopted by 510 v: The European Parliament approved a Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreement with Cape Verde, focusing on sustainable fishing and good governance. The agreement provides fishing opportunities for tuna vessels and allocates €750,000 annually.
The European Parliament adopted by 636 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to allocate the 2019 EU budget surplus of €3.2 billion, primarily from competition fines and interest on fines, for immediate aid to regions and businesses impacted by COVID-19.
The European Parliament adopted by 537 v: The European Parliament approved a new Fisheries Partnership Agreement with Guinea-Bissau, allowing Union vessels to fish in their waters from 2019-2024. The agreement was consented with 537 votes in favor, 64 against, and 87 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 680 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to provide financial aid from the EU Solidarity Fund to Portugal, Spain, Italy, and Austria affected by natural disasters in 2019. The funds allocated were €8.2 million for Portugal, €56.7 million for Spain, €211.7 million for Italy, and €2.3 million for Austria. The Parliament emphasized the need for a reform of the Fund to address climate change and called for a preventive policy in line with the Paris Agreement and Green Deal.
The European Parliament adopted by 589 v: The European Parliament approved a new Fisheries Partnership Agreement with São Tomé and Príncipe, allowing EU vessels to fish in their waters. The agreement aims to promote responsible fishing and support the development of São Tomé and Príncipe's fisheries sector.
The European Parliament adopted by 680 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to provide assistance to Portugal, Spain, Italy, and Austria following 2019's natural disasters, increasing the budget for disaster aid by €272 million.
The European Parliament adopted by 655 v: The European Parliament approved, with minor exceptions, a protocol adjusting the aviation agreement between the EU, its members, and Moldova, to include Croatia post-EU accession in 2013. This protocol does not significantly alter the existing agreement establishing a common aviation area.
The European Parliament adopted by 654 v: The European Parliament approved, with minor exceptions, an agreement establishing a Common Aviation Area between the EU and Moldova, enhancing air travel between the two regions. This agreement, part of the EU's Neighborhood Policy, covers various air transport issues including rights, management, regulation, competition, and social aspects.
The European Parliament decided by 651 v: The European Parliament passed a vote (651-28, 8 abstentions) to establish a special committee focused on combating cancer. The committee will address prevention, diagnosis, treatment, life as a cancer survivor, and palliative care, with a focus on EU competence and linking to the future Horizon Europe program. Responsibilities include setting strategies, assessing EU empowerment, examining screening programs, and exploring non-profit clinical trials.
The European Parliament decided by 613 v: The European Parliament approved a new Subcommittee on Fiscal Affairs within the Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs, with 613 votes in favor, 67 against, and 8 abstentions. This subcommittee of 30 members will focus on combating tax fraud, evasion, and avoidance, as well as promoting financial transparency for tax purposes.
The European\n Parliament adopted a leg: The European Parliament approved a protocol amending the Euro-Mediterranean Aviation Agreement between the EU and Morocco, accounting for Bulgaria and Romania's EU accession.
The European Parliament adopted by 415 v: The European Parliament rejected a draft Commission regulation extending approval periods for several agricultural chemicals, citing exceeding implementing powers and disregard for the precautionary principle, particularly in the case of flumioxazine due to its toxicity to aquatic life and lack of evidence for safe use.
The European Parliament adopted by 493 v: European Parliament strongly condemns racism and calls for action against it, particularly following George Floyd's death. They urge US authorities to combat racism and address structural inequalities, while denouncing disproportionate force by law enforcement.
The European Parliament adopted by 507 v: The European Parliament approved a recommendation, with 507 votes in favor, 119 against, and 37 abstentions, for strengthening the Eastern Partnership policy beyond 2020. This partnership aims to deepen relations between Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova, Ukraine, and the EU, focusing on shared values like democracy, human rights, and economic development. The June 2020 summit should outline a clear strategy and long-term vision for the partnership's future.
The European Parliament adopted by 645 v: The European Parliament approved, with minor dissents, an agreement to enhance civil aviation safety cooperation between the EU and China. The accord aims to streamline certification and surveillance of aeronautical products, improve safety, and facilitate trade. It includes mutual trust in each other's systems, acceptance of compliance findings, and ongoing collaboration for audits and inspections.
The European Parliament adopted by 421 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to combat fraud against EU finances, noting a 25% decrease in reported irregularities but an increase in fraudulent cases involving cohesion policy expenditure. The Parliament urged improved methods for estimating fraud scale, stronger anti-organized crime legislation among Member States, and closer cooperation on information exchange. They also condemned misuse of EU funds by high-level officials in several countries.
The European Parliament adopted by 531 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, with 531 votes in favor, 80 against, and 80 abstentions, regarding the EIB's financial activities in 2018. The EIB provided over €64 billion in financing for 854 projects, with Greece, Cyprus, Portugal, Croatia, and Poland receiving the majority of investments. Parliament urged alignment of investment priorities with updated EU policy objectives and called for a balanced geographical distribution of investments. Additionally, they emphasized the need for the EIB to prioritize climate-friendly infrastructure projects.
The European Parliament adopted a\n leg: The European Parliament approved the Euro-Mediterranean Aviation Agreement between the EU and Jordan. Consent was granted for the agreement's ratification.
The European Parliament adopted by 527 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, 527-67, emphasizing the need for the European Investment Bank (EIB) to increase investments in climate change, digital revolution, and public services. The EIB was praised for its climate-focused initiatives, including being the world's largest green bond issuer, and was urged to expand these efforts while establishing common standards for transparency and verification.
The European Parliament adopted a legisl: The European Parliament approved the Common Aviation Area Agreement between the EU and Georgia.
The European Parliament adopted by 438 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to initiate negotiations with New Zealand on exchanging personal data between Europol and New Zealand authorities, focusing on serious crime and terrorism. The agreement should ensure data protection equivalent to EU law standards, with exceptions for sensitive data transfers, clear safeguards for individuals' rights, and an explicit list of future provisions.
The European Parliament adopted by 485 v: The European Parliament approved a 3-month postponement (from Jan 2021 to Apr 2021) for the VAT application on e-commerce, aiming to prevent revenue loss and fraud during the COVID-19 crisis. They emphasized that any further delay could lead to significant financial losses for Member States.
The European Parliament adopted by 557 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to allocate €557 million for humanitarian support to refugees and host communities in Jordan, Lebanon, and Turkey, primarily focusing on education, livelihoods, health services, and social protection. The vote was 557 to 72 with 59 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 534 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen efforts against money laundering and terrorist financing, with 534 votes in favor, 25 against, and 122 abstentions. The resolution highlighted the need for improved implementation of anti-money laundering rules due to an estimated 1% of the Union's GDP being involved in suspicious financial activities.
The European Parliament adopted by 548 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to revise guidelines for trans-European energy infrastructure, aiming to align with updated energy and climate policy objectives, including the 1.5°C temperature increase target. The Commission is expected to propose revisions by the end of 2020.
The European Parliament adopted by 487 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 487 votes in favor and 119 against, addressing the humanitarian crisis in Venezuela and the ensuing migration and refugee crisis. The text was proposed by the EPP, S&D, and Renew groups. The EU has provided over €319 million in aid to Venezuelans, both within and outside their country. The ongoing crisis, exacerbated by the pandemic, is causing the largest population displacement in the region, with around 5 million Venezuelans fleeing and an expected total of over 6.5 million by year-end.
The European Parliament adopted by 579 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution for a Sustainable Chemicals Strategy aimed at reducing human and environmental exposure to hazardous chemicals, boosting industry competitiveness, and addressing pollution from synthetic chemicals. Current efforts fall short of SDG goals regarding chemical management and health impacts.
The European Parliament adopted by 550 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to revise employment policies in response to COVID-19, emphasizing immediate action to protect businesses and workers. Guidelines include boosting labor demand through public investment, wage subsidies, income support, extended unemployment benefits, sick leave, and telework arrangements.
The European Parliament adopted by 526 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (526-105) calling for stronger cooperation among EU institutions and member states in health emergencies, particularly for equitable access to future COVID-19 vaccines and treatments, stress tests on healthcare systems, and a directive on minimum standards for quality healthcare.
The European Parliament adopted by 686 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (686 votes to 1, with 8 abstentions) on February 19, 2020, expressing concern over Japan's handling of international parental child abduction cases involving EU citizens. The resolution highlights Japan's poor record in enforcing the 1980 Hague Convention and the lack of means to enforce visiting rights, potentially harming children and their relationships with left-behind parents.
The European Parliament adopted by 682 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (682-3, 10 abstentions) addressing the disproportionate impact of COVID-19 on individuals with intellectual disabilities and their families. The resolution emphasizes the need for greater flexibility in confinement measures and equal medical treatment for these individuals during the pandemic, along with accessible public health communications.
The European Parliament adopted by 494 v: The European Parliament approved a 3-month delay in implementing the VAT package for e-commerce due to COVID-19, aiming to prevent revenue loss and combat fraud. A longer delay was deemed risky, potentially causing losses of up to €3.5 billion for Member States.
The European Parliament adopted by 650 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to increase funding for the Youth Employment Initiative by €28.3 million, passing with 650 votes in favor and 19 against. This amendment adjusts the resources for economic cohesion from 2014-2020, allocating €4.17 billion to the initiative, with member states able to transfer up to 50% of additional funds to the European Social Fund.
The European Parliament adopted by 465 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution (465-150) on the July 2020 EU recovery fund, welcoming the move but regretting reduced grants and lack of parliamentary role. Parliament also criticized proposed cuts to various programs in the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), and expressed dissatisfaction with the repayment plan for the recovery instrument, threatening to withhold consent for the MFF until a satisfactory agreement is reached.
The European Parliament adopted by 552 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, with 552 votes in favor, 61 against, and 78 abstentions, supporting the implementation of the EU Association Agreement with Georgia. The resolution emphasizes continued support for Georgia's European integration, ongoing reforms under the agreement, and condemnation of Russia's occupation of Abkhazia and Tskhinvali/South Ossetia. Additionally, it highlights Georgia's role as a significant partner in EU and NATO missions. The resolution also acknowledges the increasing number of visa-free visits by Georgian citizens to Schengen countries.
The European Parliament adopted by 553 v: The European Parliament approved, by 553 votes to 106 with 29 abstentions, a resolution to mobilize €481,572,239 from the Contingency Margin in 2020 for continued humanitarian support to refugees in Turkey. This decision involves reallocating funds from headings 5 (Administration) and 2 (Sustainable growth: natural resources) of the multiannual financial framework.
The European Parliament adopted by 556 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 556 votes in favor, urging Member States to maximize energy storage potential. They called for a comprehensive strategy on energy storage from the Commission, focusing on various technologies and removing regulatory barriers to boost competitiveness. Key requests include an anti-double taxation system for energy storage projects, common grid connection requirements, and TEN-E Regulation revision to facilitate integration of storage into electricity markets.
The European Parliament adopted by 427 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 427-128, emphasizing the need for integrated security, development, and humanitarian intervention in the Sahel, West Africa, and Horn of Africa. The EU was called upon to coordinate its strategies with the African Union and African states, aiming for independent African ownership in security and defense affairs. The resolution also highlighted the need to improve crisis response speed and effectiveness, strengthen CSDP missions, and enhance overall communication and strategic planning policy.
The European Parliament adopted by 371 v: The European Parliament approved a legislative resolution aimed at improving the single market for road transport by adapting Regulation (EC) 1071/2009 and 1072/2009. The proposal includes light commercial vehicles within the scope of the regulation, but excludes very light vehicles and certain national transport operations. Non-profit road carriage is also considered as non-commercial.
The European Parliament adopted by 394 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 394-236, to amend driving time and rest regulations for vehicles over 2.4 tonnes in international transport. The aim is to ensure fair competition and worker rights in road transport. The amended proposal expands the scope and introduces changes to weekly rest periods for drivers.
The European Parliament adopted by 543 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen EU actions against global deforestation. The resolution calls for higher environmental standards, comprehensive anti-deforestation policies, binding targets for forest protection, and inclusion of primary forests in the future EU Forest Strategy.
The European Parliament adopted by 341 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on arms exports, aiming to enhance EU's strategic autonomy by prioritizing European products in defense equipment programs. Despite progress in annual reports, concerns remain about incomplete data submissions from some Member States.
The European Parliament adopted by 520 v: The European Parliament approved amendments to strengthen the EU MRV Regulation for maritime CO2 emissions, including the potential inclusion of larger ships in the EU Emissions Trading Scheme (EU ETS) and adopting key elements of the International Maritime Organization's strategy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The revised regulation was referred back for further negotiations.
The European Parliament adopted by 317 v: The European Parliament passed a directive aimed at enhancing enforcement and combating illegal practices in the road transport sector. The measure focuses on ensuring compliance with work and rest time provisions to improve road safety and protect driver's rights, while also targeting undeclared work through letterbox companies.
The European Parliament adopted by 513 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, expressing concerns over Poland's rule of law, including its legislative system, judiciary independence, and protection of fundamental rights. They called on the Council to resume Article 7 proceedings against Poland due to overwhelming evidence, urging immediate action under EU Treaty Article 7.
The European Parliament adopted by 545 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution calling for the development of a 'Romani mainstreaming policy' to integrate Roma into mainstream policies, programs, and projects. The Commission is invited to present a legislative proposal for Roma equality, inclusion, and participation, addressing housing, health, employment, and education inequalities.
The European Parliament adopted by 566 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to integrate environmental protection and sustainability into Erasmus+, Creative Europe, and the European Solidarity Corps programs. The Parliament emphasized the importance of these programs in promoting cooperation and innovation, and called for flexibility to help them resume post-pandemic in a sustainable manner. The Commission is invited to propose specific indicators to measure their environmental impact.
The European Parliament adopted by 671 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to address pharmaceutical pollution, focusing on improving control measures and raising awareness about the responsible use of pharmaceuticals. The resolution emphasizes the need for a holistic approach to combat pollution, encourages the use of extended producer responsibility, and calls for Member States to share best practices and promote training on prudent medicine usage.
The European Parliament adopted by 593 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to establish a new strategy for greener cities, aiming to integrate climate and environmental perspectives into urban policies, adopt an adaptation strategy for climate-vulnerable cities, and promote nature-based solutions for biodiversity conservation.
The European Parliament adopted by 617 v: The European Parliament passed an amendment to strengthen disaster resilience in the EU, focusing on prevention and preparedness. Key changes include developing transnational early warning systems, providing training for local communities, and improving national disaster risk management plans with cross-border collaboration.
The European Parliament adopted by 672 v: The European Parliament approved a proposal to authorize Portugal to apply reduced excise duties on certain alcoholic products from Madeira and Azores regions. The decision passed with 672 votes in favor, 7 against, and 8 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 526 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to boost energy efficiency in EU buildings, aiming for a 'renovation wave' to meet zero net emissions by 2050. This could create up to 2 million jobs and contribute significantly to the COVID-19 recovery. The focus is on neighborhoods and communities, with energy districts, local authorities, SMEs, and citizens playing key roles in renovations. One-stop-shops for building renovation are proposed as advisory tools.
The European Parliament adopted by 455 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on the EU's own resource system, increasing credibility and sustainability for the Next Generation EU recovery plan. New resources, aligned with strategic objectives, will be introduced from 2021, supporting the Green Deal, single market, tax efficiency, and anti-fraud efforts.
The European Parliament adopted by 574 v: The European Parliament, by 574 votes to 37 with 82 abstentions, rejected the official results of the August 2020 presidential election in Belarus due to violations of international standards. They also strongly condemned the violent repression of peaceful protests and called for free and fair elections, supporting a transition of power through national dialogue.
The European Parliament adopted by 601 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (601 votes for, 57 against, 36 abstentions) condemning Turkey's illegal actions in the Eastern Mediterranean, particularly in Greece and Cyprus' Exclusive Economic Zones. They urged Turkey to halt all further exploration and drilling activities, respect territorial integrity, and engage in diplomatic means for a peaceful solution.
The European Parliament adopted by 485 v: The European Parliament approved, by 485 votes to 169, amendments to emissions regulations for light vehicles (Euro 5 and Euro 6). The changes introduce a compliance factor to address uncertainties in real-world emission measurements, with this factor applicable during a transitional period.
The European Parliament adopted by 532 v: The European Parliament strongly condemned the poisoning of Alexei Navalny using a military-grade nerve agent, calling it a reprehensible crime under the Chemical Weapons Convention. The resolution urged an international investigation into the case and sanctions against Russia for non-cooperation.
The European Parliament adopted by 595 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (595 votes in favor, 50 against) on COVID-19 coordination for health assessments and risk classification, emphasizing the need for unified health management to combat the pandemic. The resolution calls for a swift return to a fully functional Schengen area, urging Member States to collaborate with Parliament, Council, and Commission on a recovery plan for Schengen.
The European Parliament adopted by 663 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (663-23) addressing the worsening shortage of medicines in the EU during COVID-19. To combat this issue, they proposed a pharmaceutical industrial strategy for health sovereignty and better coordination among EU countries. The plan includes securing supply, reducing dependence on third countries, and prioritizing patient safety.
The European Parliament adopted by 616 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 616 votes in favor, urging action against Islamist rebellion in northern Mozambique. The text was jointly proposed by multiple groups, expressing concern over the violence committed by Al-Shabab, which has displaced thousands and left many in need of assistance. Parliament called on Mozambican authorities to prevent further unrest, warning of potential regional instability if the rebellion is not contained.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament unanimously supports Dr. Denis Mukwege, expressing concern over threats against him and his hospital staff in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). They urge the DRC government to investigate these threats promptly and improve human rights protection in eastern DRC.
The European Parliament adopted by 626 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 626 votes in favor and 7 against, expressing deep concern over human rights violations in the Philippines under President Duterte, particularly the 'war on drugs'. They also condemned threats against journalists, including Maria Ressa, and called for all charges against her to be dropped.
The European Parliament adopted by 372 v: The European Parliament rejected a draft Commission Regulation, voting 372 to 275 with 39 abstentions, due to incompatibility with pesticide regulations. The rejection was primarily based on concerns about the insecticide flonicamid, which has potential risks for visceral malformations and pollinators.
The European Parliament adopted by 598 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (598-42, 46 abstentions) to support the cultural sector during the COVID-19 pandemic. They called for at least 2% of the Recovery and Resilience Facility to be allocated to cultural and creative sectors, recognizing their strategic importance (7.8 million jobs, 4% GDP).
The European Parliament adopted by 417 v: The European Parliament passed an amendment to establish the Just Transition Fund with a budget increase, aiming to support regions facing economic challenges from climate transition. The scope of investments was broadened to include microenterprises, social infrastructure, sustainable mobility, and research.

The European Parliament passed a resolution to advance Capital Markets Union (CMU), focusing on improving financing for SMEs and retail investor participation. The aim is to offer more attractive, stable, and sustainable financing options while safeguarding economic stability and protecting investors' interests. To aid COVID-19 recovery, barriers are called to be removed, legislation simplified, and funding sources diversified, particularly for SMEs. The Commission was invited to address obstacles in supervisory, tax, or insolvency legislation to integrate EU capital markets effectively.
The European Parliament adopted by 462 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to promote sustainable forest management, recognizing the importance of forests for climate benefits and ecosystem services. Member States were urged to protect forest ecosystems and develop guidelines for non-timber products, while the Commission was invited to explore incentives for climate, biodiversity, and other ecological benefits.
The European Parliament adopted by 542 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 542 votes to 63, emphasizing the importance of integrating digital finance into the Capital Markets Union for increased financing options. They called for a review of digital finance regulations, particularly in light of COVID-19, and expressed concern over unresolved issues related to money laundering and criminal activity associated with crypto-assets. The Parliament welcomed the Digital Finance Package but urged the Commission to address these concerns and coordinate internationally on digital finance standards.
The European Parliament adopted by 521 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 521 votes in favor and 152 against, establishing an EU Mechanism to uphold democracy, rule of law, and fundamental rights due to persistent violations in some Member States. This comes amid concerns over autocratic tendencies exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, economic recession, corruption, disinformation, and state capture. The Union lacks effective tools to ensure these criteria are met post-membership.
The European Parliament adopted by 358 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 358 votes in favor, 277 against, and 56 abstentions, expressing concern over corruption and rule of law issues in Bulgaria. The resolution highlighted increasing corruption perceptions and misuse of Union funds, and called for Bulgarian authorities to respect democratic values, ensure media freedom, and hold the executive accountable.
The European Parliament adopted by 431 v: The European Parliament endorsed a resolution affirming its commitment to a rules-based, value-driven global trading system. The EU reported a surplus of €84.6 billion in goods trade with partners in 2018, emphasizing the importance of exports for over 36 million jobs. In response to new challenges, the Parliament called for an EU trade strategy that promotes interests and values, boosts industry competitiveness, and aligns with the European Green Deal objectives. To strengthen its global position, the EU should pursue a multilateral, plurilateral, and bilateral agenda, aiming for a functional WTO dispute settlement system and ambitious EU-led reforms, as well as fair trade agreements ensuring reciprocity and adherence to European rules and standards.
The European Parliament adopted by 574 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen the Youth Guarantee, aiming for a binding instrument across all Member States. The enhanced scheme seeks to provide quality jobs for young people aged 15-30, addressing shortcomings in employability and incorporating a gender dimension. A differentiated approach is proposed for long-term NEETs facing socio-economic disadvantages.
The European Parliament adopted by 681 v: The European Parliament approved a decision to allow Spanish authorities to provide tax exemptions for locally manufactured products in the Canary Islands until 2027. The proposal aims to support local producers by reducing competition with external products due to higher production costs on the islands. The eligible product categories are listed in Annex I, and the Spanish authorities will determine specific products and exemption levels within limits.
The European Parliament adopted by 680 v: The European Parliament approved a proposal to allow France to reduce taxes on traditional rum produced in Guadeloupe, French Guiana, Martinique, and Réunion, justifying it due to economic difficulties in these regions. The proposal was adopted without amendment.
The European Parliament adopted by 634 v: The European Parliament approved, with 634 votes in favor and 39 against, a regulation adjusting the decommitment procedure for funds under the Asylum, Migration, and Integration Fund (AMIF) and Internal Security Fund (ISF). This move aims to provide Member States more flexibility to utilize funds during the COVID-19 pandemic, allowing them to use the N+2 rule fully until December 31, 2023.
The European Parliament adopted by 491 v: The European Parliament approved, by a majority of 491 votes to 159, the addition of Ukraine to countries with equivalence for field inspections and seed production of cereal crops, updating Council Decision 2003/17/EC. The decision aligns Ukrainian regulations with EU standards.
The European Parliament adopted by 680 v: The European Parliament approved an extension of dock dues exemption in French outermost regions for six months, from January 1st, 2021 to June 30th, 2021, due to the Coronavirus epidemic hindering impact assessments.
The European Parliament adopted by 443 v: The European Parliament voted against the draft Commission Regulation on Titanium Dioxide (E171), a food additive, due to potential health risks and insufficient data for risk assessment.
The European Parliament adopted by 584 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to update the revenue side of the EU budget for 2020, reflecting recent economic forecasts amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. Adjustments include revising estimates for traditional own resources, VAT, GNI, and UK correction, as well as accounting for fines, penalties, and exchange rate differences.
The European Parliament adopted by 439 v: The European Parliament rejected a draft Commission Regulation aimed at setting maximum levels of acrylamide in specific foodstuffs for infants and young children. This decision was based on concerns about the regulation's compatibility with existing food contaminant regulations. Acrylamide, a potentially carcinogenic chemical found in various foods, is particularly concerning in this age group due to its toxicity.
The European Parliament adopted by 609 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 609 votes in favor and 21 against, condemning Nicaragua's proposed 'Foreign Agents' Law. This law, modeled on Russia's 2012 foreign agents law, would restrict civil and political rights of individuals and organizations receiving funds from abroad, potentially impacting EU cooperation and interests in Nicaragua.
The European Parliament adopted by 413 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 413 votes in favor, condemning the mistreatment of Ethiopian migrants in detention centers in Saudi Arabia. The resolution calls for the immediate release of all detainees, particularly women and children, amid reports of over 30,000 Ethiopians being arbitrarily detained following forced expulsion from Yemen.
The European Parliament adopted by 663 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution calling for the immediate release of imprisoned journalist Dawit Isaak and other detained journalists in Eritrea. They also demanded information on Isaak's whereabouts, improved prison conditions due to COVID-19, and access to EU representatives.
The European Parliament adopted by 641 v: The European Parliament approved, by a large margin, a recommendation for nuclear arms control and disarmament options ahead of the 2020 Non-Proliferation Treaty review. This comes amidst ongoing challenges in denuclearizing the Korean peninsula, Iran's JCPOA withdrawal, the collapse of the INF Treaty, and stalemate in new START Treaty negotiations between Russia and the US.
The European Parliament adopted by 477 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution advocating for gender equality in EU foreign and security policy, aiming to integrate the gender perspective into various policies and allocate 85% of development aid to programs promoting gender equality.
The European Parliament adopted by 466 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on strengthening employment and social policies in the euro area, aiming to address economic recession and rising poverty due to COVID-19. Members called for a new policy strategy that integrates the European Green Deal, Social Rights Pillar, and long-term goals for a sustainable economy and society, aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals.
The European Parliament adopted by 392 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation to establish a framework for achieving climate neutrality by 2050, with all member states included. Support will be provided at various levels to ensure this goal is met fairly and sustainably, considering marine and terrestrial biodiversity. The parliament also approved measures for negative emissions.
Parliament adopted by 554 votes to 70, w: The European Parliament approved a resolution, with 554 votes in favor, 70 against, and 65 abstentions, supporting the implementation of the EU Association Agreement with Moldova. The agreement aims to promote political association and economic integration, with financial aid contingent on respect for European values like rule of law, human rights, and democratic principles. Parliament emphasized the need for progress in areas such as public institution independence, anti-corruption measures, judicial reform, and improving citizens' living conditions.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament approved a resolution (571 votes for, 26 against, 94 abstentions) supporting the Commission's plan to regulate digital services. The proposal aims to balance Single Market functioning, consumer protection, and equal treatment of online and offline activities while respecting fundamental rights.
The European Parliament adopted by 559 v: The European Parliament approved a call for a comprehensive ethical framework for AI, robotics, and related technologies. The aim is to establish Union-wide standards for high-risk tech, balancing innovation with the protection of Union values through human-centric AI systems. The proposed regulation will be based on principles such as human-centric, human-made, and human-controlled AI.
The European Parliament adopted by 464 v: The European Parliament approved a recommendation to advance a common EU defense policy, known as PESCO. This move aims to strengthen Member States' solidarity in response to armed aggression and enhance the EU's role as an international security provider. The Council and Vice-President of the Commission were urged to prioritize conflict resolution and implement measures to bolster the Union's defense capacity.
The European Parliament adopted by 602 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (602 votes, 44 abstentions) urging non-recognition of Belarus' fraudulent election results and not acknowledging Aliaksandr Lukashenko as the legitimate president post-November 2020. They also recognized Sviatlana Tsikhanukhaya's Coordinating Council as the legitimate representative for democratic change in Belarus, condemning their persecution, and calling for their release and dropped charges. Additionally, they expressed support for the Belarusian people's demands for new free and fair elections.
The European Parliament adopted by 377 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution urging mandatory measures to halt deforestation driven by palm oil, meat, soy, cocoa, etc., due to their impact on climate change and human rights violations. The resolution emphasizes the need for stronger regulations to prevent deforestation products from entering the EU market.
The European Parliament adopted by 637 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution calling for a Digital Services Act, urging the Commission to propose regulations for online platforms. The act should include standards for content moderation, transparent rules, and accessible judicial redress. The proposed regulation will apply to platforms hosting public content within the Union, regardless of their location.
The European Parliament adopted by 612 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to emphasize the need for protecting Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) in the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. The EU was encouraged to establish an efficient IPR system to safeguard innovative developers and ensure long-term use of AI by consumers.
The European Parliament adopted by 677 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to extend the sale of Euro 4 motorbikes (L-category vehicles) beyond January 2021, due to COVID-19 disruptions, allowing for their use as end-of-series vehicles until December 2021.
The European Parliament adopted by 593 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution on the impact of COVID-19 on European education, highlighting the exacerbation of digital and social inequalities due to the shift to online learning.
The European Parliament adopted by 645 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to allocate €2,054,400 from the European Globalisation Adjustment Fund to support 960 workers affected by redundancies in Spanish shipbuilding ancillary sectors in Galicia. The funds are intended to help businesses impacted by economic globalization.
The European Parliament adopted by 626 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, calling for the Commission to propose regulations on civil liability claims for artificial intelligence (AI) operators. The aim is to balance citizen protection and technological innovation while ensuring legal certainty throughout the liability chain.
The European Parliament adopted by 566 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (566 votes for, 45 against, 80 abstentions) emphasizing the importance of fundamental rights in digital services policy. They urged a tailored approach to regulate online and offline differences, with stricter measures for illegal content, swift removal of such content while safeguarding freedom of expression, and application only to illegally defined content.
The European Parliament adopted by 597 v: The European Parliament approved a six-year Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreement between the EU and Seychelles, aimed at promoting sustainable fishing and granting catch opportunities to EU vessels in Seychelles waters. The agreement follows recommendations from the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission for a balanced share of marine resources.
The European Parliament adopted by 463 v: The European Parliament approved amendments to agricultural market regulations, aiming for a more sustainable and 'greener' Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). The focus is on boosting modernization and sustainability, reducing food waste, promoting healthy eating habits, and producing healthier food. The matter was referred back for further inter-institutional negotiations.
The European Parliament adopted by 471 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to finance the Green Deal, aiming for at least €662 billion annual investment. They endorsed the Commission's recovery plan, emphasizing alignment with EU taxonomy and National Energy & Climate Plans (NECPs). Members raised concerns about mobilizing €100 billion by 2030 due to COVID-19 economic impacts.
The European Parliament adopted by 496 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (496 votes, 138 against) addressing the impact of COVID-19 on democracy, rule of law, and fundamental rights. It urged Member States to align emergency measures with international recommendations, avoid unrelated legislation, and limit restrictions on democratic institutions.
The European Parliament adopted by 627 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to extend the European network of Public Employment Services (PES) until December 2027. The aim is to modernize and strengthen PES for improved service quality, effectiveness, and efficiency. The network will promote cooperation, information exchange, and innovative job placement services, aligning with the European Green Deal, Social Rights Pillar, and UN Sustainable Development Goals.
The European Parliament adopted by 587 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to limit fishing capacity for Eastern Baltic cod, Western Baltic cod, and Western Baltic herring. The measure aims to provide financial support to affected fishermen to permanently decommission their vessels. The decision was made during the first reading of the ordinary legislative procedure.
The European Parliament adopted by 476 v: The European Parliament rejected a decision to authorize genetically modified soybean SYHT0H2 for market entry. Critics raised concerns about insufficient analysis of herbicide residues, potential health risks, and incomplete environmental risk assessment data.
The European Parliament adopted by 483 v: The European Parliament rejected a resolution to authorize genetically modified maize products by Monsanto, with 483 votes against, 178 for, and 25 abstentions. Critics raised concerns about insufficient analysis of glyphosate residues, potential interactions between genetic traits, and lack of data for unauthorized sub-combinations.
The European Parliament adopted by 604 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 604-43 (with 49 abstentions), to extend until December 2025 the exceptional trade measures for Western Balkan countries linked to the EU's Stabilisation and Association process. The move aims to strengthen the Union's commitment to trade integration in the region, with the current system of autonomous trade measures seen as beneficial for Balkan economies. The resolution requires beneficiary entities to engage in economic reforms and regional cooperation for eligibility.
The European Parliament adopted by 526 v: The European Parliament rejected a resolution, with 526 votes against and 142 in favor, to authorize the sale of genetically modified maize due to concerns about potential environmental interactions, unresolved safety questions, and the use of an antimicrobial resistant gene. Additionally, the applicant failed to provide data for certain sub-combinations of the maize.
The European Parliament adopted by 434 v: The European Parliament approved changes to the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) financing, with a vote of 434 to 185. The amendments emphasize maintaining CAP funds at current levels, designating national authorities for accreditation oversight, and focusing on core activities.
The European Parliament adopted by 471 v: The European Parliament approved a budget for 2021 with an increase of €15 billion, focusing on climate change, energy, digital, transport, space, SMEs, tourism, security, migration, fundamental rights, and external action. New own resources are expected to finance the budget from 2021, while emphasizing the role of the budgetary authority in the EU recovery plan.
The European Parliament adopted by 612 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation for the EU Health Programme (2021-2027) aimed at improving health, addressing cross-border threats, enhancing preparedness, and promoting data sharing. The amendments focus on objectives like health promotion, disease prevention, pharmaceutical independence, and resilient health systems.
Parliament adopted by 425 votes to 212,: The European Parliament passed a vote (425-212) to amend rules for agricultural support under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), focusing on improving environmental performance and promoting sustainable development. The amendments emphasize climate and environmental requirements, aiming to develop a competitive agricultural sector while preserving family farming and ensuring long-term food security.
The European Parliament adopted by 633 v: The European Parliament approved a cooperation agreement on Geographical Indications (GIs) between the EU and China, providing higher protection than WTO TRIPS for 200 each from both sides. Members called for monitoring implementation, swift expansion, and continued dialogue with China regarding export restrictions on some EU GIs.
The European Parliament adopted by 583 v: The European Parliament approved a five-year fishing partnership with Senegal, providing access for EU vessels and a yearly contribution of €3,050,750. The aim is to sustainably manage fisheries resources and protect marine biodiversity. Members emphasized the need to address by-catches of sensitive species and strengthen ecosystem protection measures.
The European Parliament adopted by 524 v: The European Parliament approved a five-year sustainable fisheries partnership with Senegal, providing fishing opportunities for EU vessels. The agreement includes an annual financial contribution of €3,050,750.
The European Parliament adopted by 504 v: The European Parliament approved a new six-year Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreement (SFPA) between the EU and Seychelles, focusing on tuna fishing. The agreement grants rights to 40 purse seiners and 8 surface longliners, with an increase in longliners compared to the previous protocol.
