The European Parliament adopted by 641 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to amend VAT rules for identifying taxable persons in Northern Ireland, ensuring proper functioning of the EU VAT system and avoiding a hard border with Ireland. The proposal was adopted without amendment.
The European Parliament adopted by 645 v: The European Parliament approved an agreement to protect famous EU Geographical Indications (GIs) in China, providing initial protection for 100 EU and 100 Chinese GIs upon entry into force, with potential expansion to additional product classes and GI names within four years.
The European Parliament adopted by 688 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution emphasizing the importance of product safety in the single market, particularly for medical and protective equipment, online and offline products, and imports. The resolution calls for harmonized market surveillance rules for all products and encourages the Commission to address AI challenges in its review of the General Product Safety Directive.
The European Parliament adopted by 553 v: European Parliament reinforced measures to protect media freedom, journalistic safety, combat hate speech, and address disinformation. Members called for support to fund independent journalism, develop a protective framework, and strengthen tools like the Media Pluralism Monitoring Instrument.
The European Parliament adopted by 331 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to enhance development effectiveness and aid efficiency, aiming to achieve Sustainable Development Goals while avoiding fragmentation and misuse of funds. As the world's largest donor of official development assistance, the EU is committed to addressing new global challenges like climate change and COVID-19.
The European Parliament adopted by 468 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (468-194) celebrating increased voter turnout in 2019 elections, particularly among young people. They emphasized the need to strengthen connections between voters and candidates, improve gender balance, and address barriers for minorities and disabled citizens. Parliament also called on Member States to ensure all eligible voters can exercise their right to vote.
The European Parliament adopted by 395 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution titled 'Towards a more sustainable single market for business and consumers'. The focus is on establishing eco-friendly production and consumption patterns, prioritizing resource efficiency to address global limits and support resilient business models post-COVID. The parliament calls for a research-based strategy to increase product sustainability, generate growth, and ensure consumer protection. They urge the Commission to demonstrate strong political ambition in proposals aimed at empowering consumers in the green transition and implementing a sustainable product policy aligned with EU's climate and environmental objectives.
The European Parliament adopted by 638 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to eliminate tariffs on lobsters and crawfish, subject to US reciprocity in reducing duties on certain products and avoiding measures against the EU that contradict the August 2020 Joint Statement.
The European Parliament adopted by 619 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (619-45, 28 abstentions) emphasizing the importance of restoring a fully functional Schengen area amid COVID-19. They urged coordination between Member States and EU institutions to avoid long-term border controls and stressed the need for contingency plans in case of future pandemic peaks. The Commission was called upon to address cross-border obstacles.
The European Parliament adopted by 686 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to manage tariff and import quotas for goods entering the EU post-Brexit, excluding Northern Ireland. The regulation will take effect from January 1, 2021.
The European Parliament adopted by 682 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to provide assistance to Croatia, Poland, and several other countries affected by natural disasters and the COVID-19 pandemic. Funding amounts include €8,462,280 for Croatia, among others.
The European Parliament adopted by 615 v: The European Parliament approved an amended proposal for the InvestEU Programme, aiming to establish the InvestEU Fund to support EU investment projects aligned with priorities like the Green Deal and digital transition. The fund will mobilize €91.77 billion through a €38.7 billion EU guarantee, with 40% provisioned. The amendments focus on strategic sector investments and resilience against economic shocks.
The European Parliament adopted by 647 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution aiming to end homelessness in the EU by 2030, expressing concern over the rising numbers of homeless individuals and the potential impact of COVID-19 on this issue. Member States and the Commission were urged to take stronger action, use existing resources, and develop new strategies for employment opportunities and social integration for jobless households.
The European Parliament adopted by 682 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to mobilize the EU Solidarity Fund for natural disaster aid in Croatia and Poland, and for advance payments to seven Member States affected by COVID-19. The budget was amended to provide additional funds for disaster relief and public health emergencies.
The European Parliament adopted by 593 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (593 votes for, 50 against, 50 abstentions) on the EU Trade Policy Review, emphasizing the need for 'open strategic autonomy' and wider use of the euro in international trade due to COVID-19 disruptions and global economic shifts.
The European Parliament adopted by 631 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (631-3, 59 abstentions) condemning Turkey's illegal activities in Varosha, an abandoned town in Cyprus. The resolution calls for the resumption of talks, urges mutual trust, and advocates for diplomacy to resolve the conflict. It also encourages the European Council to maintain a firm stance against unilateral Turkish actions and impose sanctions. Turkey is urged to cease its illegal activities in Varosha.
The European Parliament adopted by 330 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (330-298) emphasizing the need to protect fundamental rights in the EU for 2018-2019, highlighting concerns over child poverty, gender and disability inequalities, and violations against vulnerable groups.
The European Parliament adopted by 361 v: The European Parliament passed an amendment (361 votes, 156 against) to ease requirements under MIFID II for economic recovery post-COVID-19. Key changes include reducing red tape, temporary exceptions, and considering retail investor debt in suitability assessments. The parliament also clarified quantitative tests for ancillary trading activities.
The European Parliament adopted by 455 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (455 votes to 145) condemning Poland's de facto ban on abortion rights, expressing concern over restrictive access to contraceptives and family planning services. The resolution called out the risk to women's health and lives due to the Constitutional Tribunal's ruling declaring the existing law unconstitutional.
The European Parliament adopted by 425 v: The European Parliament rejected a Commission Implementing Regulation to extend approval periods for several pesticides, including chlorotoluron, due to concerns it violates the precautionary principle and is not aligned with safety criteria. Chlorotoluron, classified as very toxic to aquatic life and potentially harmful to human health, was identified as a substance of concern in the regulation.
The European Parliament adopted by 458 v: The European Parliament rejected the draft Commission regulation that aimed to approve carbendazim as an active substance in biocidal products (film preservatives and masonry preservatives) due to concerns over its hazardous properties, environmental impact, lack of risk management measures, insufficient data on alternatives, and inconsistencies with EU law.
The European Parliament adopted by 486 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (486-109, 102 abstentions) for a new industrial strategy focusing on climate neutrality by 2050, supporting dual ecological and digital transition, and creating quality jobs. The strategy aims to foster long-term growth, mobilize resources, realize the European Green Deal, strengthen global leadership, and reduce EU dependence. It consists of two phases: one for job consolidation, production reactivation, and adaptation post-COVID; another for industry rebuilding and transformation. The Next Generation EU initiative is seen as the cornerstone of the first phase.
The European Parliament adopted by 467 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 467 votes in favor, 80 against, and 148 abstentions, emphasizing the need for a unified foreign policy response to the COVID-19 pandemic. They welcomed collaborative initiatives like 'Team Europe' and the Global Coronavirus Response Initiative but criticized the lack of global leadership and rising authoritarianism during the crisis. The resolution also highlighted the worsening global socio-economic inequalities and called for a review of the 2016 global strategy.
The European Parliament adopted by 643 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 643 votes in favor and 5 against, urging an end to the armed conflict in Ethiopia between the federal government and Tigray regional administration. The resolution also expressed concern over violence and human rights violations, and called for both parties to respect fundamental human rights.
The European Parliament adopted by 613 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 613 votes in favor and 41 against, condemning human rights violations in Belarus, particularly the murder of Raman Bandarenka. The resolution also demanded investigations into his death and other protest-related deaths. The Parliament called for stronger sanctions against the Belarusian authorities.
The European Parliament adopted by 669 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, by 669 votes to 3 with 22 abstentions, condemning Algeria's escalating human rights violations, particularly against journalist Khaled Drareni. They called for the immediate release of Drareni and other detained activists, and an end to media censorship and political arrests.
The European Parliament adopted by 533 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to update the strategy for supporting Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), recognizing their crucial role in the EU economy. The new strategy aims to address the challenges faced by SMEs during the pandemic, focusing on a resilient society and competitive economy. The plan includes an action plan with clear objectives, regular monitoring, and improvements to the business environment.
The European Parliament adopted by 512 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 512 votes to 134, urging the Commission to regularly evaluate the implementation of the Return Directive, emphasizing the importance of a common, evidence-based approach for coherent policy making and informed public discourse. Members also highlighted concerns about the decrease in enforced return decisions since 2015, stressing the need for an effective return policy as part of a well-functioning European asylum and migration policy. The resolution emphasized the importance of measuring the effectiveness of the Return Directive by considering the return rate, sustainability of returns, implementation of fundamental rights safeguards, respect for procedural guarantees, and effectiveness of voluntary return.
The European Parliament adopted by 448 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution aimed at improving the Dublin III Regulation, which governs asylum applications within the EU. The resolution highlighted an increase in asylum seekers from 2012-2019, with children accounting for nearly half of all applications. Recognizing the current system's failure to ensure fair distribution of responsibility among Member States, the Parliament advocates for a sustainable solidarity mechanism and additional resources to uphold asylum seekers' rights.
The European Parliament adopted by 380 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution for a social Europe governance framework, aiming to adopt a key program at the Porto Social Summit. This program will outline a sustainable, fair, and inclusive social Europe by 2030, based on integrating the European Pillar of Social Rights into treaties and adopting a Sustainable Development and Social Progress Pact. More social policy areas will fall under qualified majority decision-making, including non-discrimination, worker protection, and terms for third-country nationals.
The European Parliament approved by 347: The European Parliament passed a resolution on sustainable corporate governance, emphasizing the need for directors to prioritize long-term company interests and incorporate sustainability considerations (including human rights and environmental protection) in corporate decision-making. The Parliament also supported strengthening non-financial reporting obligations, particularly regarding climate and environmental data disclosure.
The European Parliament adopted by 429 v: The European Parliament approved changes to control mechanisms for the Commission's implementing powers, primarily focusing on referrals to the Appeal Committee in specific cases, especially in genetically modified organisms, food, and feed. In cases where no opinion is delivered by the Appeal Committee, a new meeting at a high political level may be organized for a political debate.
The European Parliament adopted by 684 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to establish a European Year of Rail, emphasizing rail's crucial role during the COVID-19 crisis. The year aims to promote rail as a sustainable, safe, and affordable mode of transport, highlighting its potential in achieving climate neutrality by 2050 and ensuring essential services even during crises.
The European Parliament adopted by 689 v: The European Parliament approved an extension for the European Capitals of Culture 2020-2021, acknowledging challenges posed by COVID-19. The decision allows Rijeka (Croatia) and Galway (Ireland) to extend their tenure due to pandemic disruptions.
The European Parliament adopted by 619 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, with 619 votes in favor and 11 against, aiming to enhance the Petitions Committee's role in defending citizens' rights and increasing public awareness of EU policy areas through a permanent information campaign.
The European Parliament adopted by 663 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to update management, conservation, and control measures for tropical tuna fishing in the Inter-American Tropical Tuna Convention area. The proposal covers measures related to tuna stocks, other species caught by tuna vessels, and species within the same ecosystem. It applies to EU vessels fishing in the IATTC area, addressing aspects such as purse-seine vessels, data buoys, Fish Aggregating Devices, transhipment rules, etc.
The European Parliament decided, by 598: The European Parliament voted to amend its Rules of Procedure to adapt to extraordinary circumstances, such as the COVID-19 pandemic. The changes aim to ensure the continuity of parliamentary activities and accommodate members with disabilities in exceptional situations. A new Title XIIIa titled 'Extraordinary circumstances' was introduced, including Rule 237a for such situations.
The European Parliament adopted by 663 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to allocate €47.5 billion in additional funds under REACT-EU, aimed at mitigating COVID-19 pandemic's economic impact. These funds will be distributed from 2021 to 2023, with €37.5 billion allocated for 2021 and €10 billion for 2022. The funds can be used until the end of 2023, with operations eligible from February 2020.
The European Parliament approved by 678: The European Parliament approved the Agreement on civil aviation safety between the EU and Japan, enhancing air safety and boosting competitiveness for European aviation industry. The agreement was signed in June 2020 and received parliamentary consent.
The European Parliament adopted by 524 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (524-67, with 103 abstentions) to strengthen minority rights in Europe, emphasizing the EU's commitment to diversity. The Commission is invited to develop a common framework for protecting minority rights, while Member States are urged to uphold these rights and respect linguistic rights in multilingual communities.
The European Parliament approved by 570: The European Parliament approved an extension of the Fisheries Agreement between the EU and Mauritania, allowing continued cooperation for sustainable fishing. The aim is to extend the current protocol for one year, pending renewal negotiations.
The European Parliament adopted by 616 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to modernize and upgrade vocational education and training (VET) for sustainable competitiveness, social fairness, and resilience. The resolution emphasizes the need for more inclusive, accessible, and attractive VET policies, and calls for equal priority between VET and formal education. In response to COVID-19 disruptions, the Parliament urges providing financial resources, technical assistance, and digital devices for VET providers and learners.
The European Parliament adopted by 505 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (505-146) advocating for a dedicated Council on gender equality, recognizing the need for an intersectional approach to combat discrimination against women and men. The resolution aims to accelerate progress towards gender equality, as current rates suggest it will take over 60 years to achieve.
The European Parliament approved by 639: The European Parliament approved an agreement with the Cook Islands to continue sustainable fisheries cooperation, allowing Union vessels to fish in their waters. The agreement provides fishing opportunities for four tuna seiners, with annual financial contributions of €735,000 (first and second years) and €700,000 (third and fourth years).
The European Parliament adopted by 550 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen the EU's strategy on climate change adaptation, focusing on integrating it into the European Green Deal and global resilience efforts. The strategy should include binding goals, priority areas, regular reviews, and scientific data-based assessments for effective spending on sustainable projects.
The European Parliament adopted by 622 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to enhance water quality, emphasizing the need for timely adoption of future River Basin Management Plans and addressing issues such as insufficient funding, slow implementation, weak enforcement, and overuse of exemptions. The resolution also rejected treating water as a commodity.
The European Parliament adopted by 652 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to increase the European Investment Fund's capital by €2.87 billion, aiming to bolster the EU's response to the COVID-19 crisis through the implementation of the InvestEU programme.
The European Parliament adopted by 594 v: The European Parliament approved an increase of €1.569 billion in the Draft amending budget No 10/2020, aimed at addressing the COVID-19 crisis. Funds will be allocated to support SMEs, farmers, and agri-businesses affected by the pandemic.
The European Parliament adopted by 496 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on the Multiannual Financial Framework (2021-2027), Recovery Instrument, and Rule of Law Regulation. Starting from January 1, 2021, the rule of law cross compliance will apply to all EU budget commitments and payments. The Parliament argued that the European Council's conclusions on this matter are unnecessary as the regulation's applicability, purpose, and scope are already defined in the legal text.
The European Parliament adopted by 543 v:
The European Parliament approved a resolution on the EU Security Union Strategy, emphasizing the need for monitoring and addressing shortcomings in the existing regulatory framework. They also called for an impact assessment of new legislative proposals regarding fundamental rights and discrimination.

The Parliament focused on fighting terrorism, urging the Commission to implement the EU Counter-Terrorism Directive 2017/541 across all Member States and welcoming the new EU Counter-Terrorism Programme. They stressed the importance of a comprehensive approach to preventing radicalization, including security, education, social, cultural, and anti-discrimination policies, and the rapid removal of terrorist content online with appropriate safeguards for fundamental rights.
The European Parliament adopted by 472 v: The European Parliament rejected a resolution to authorize genetically modified soybean MON 87751 × MON 87701 × MON 87708 × MON 89788 for market placement, due to concerns about unanswered safety questions, lack of analysis on glyphosate residues, and insufficient testing for potential synergistic or antagonistic effects.
The European Parliament adopted by 604 v: The European Parliament strongly condemned forced labor and exploitation of Uyghur minorities in Xinjiang, expressing concern over human rights violations. They called on China to end detentions without trial, close internment camps, and stop supplying European brands with forced labor.
The European Parliament approved by 550: The European Parliament approved an Interinstitutional Agreement on budgetary discipline, cooperation, and new resources by a vote of 550 to 72. This agreement outlines the implementation of the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) for 2021-2027, including a roadmap towards establishing new resources. The agreement also includes provisions for interinstitutional cooperation, sound financial management, and data quality.
The European Parliament adopted by 488 v: The European Parliament rejected a decision to authorize genetically modified maize products for market, citing concerns over glyphosate residues, unanswered safety questions, and potential long-term effects on reproduction and development.
The European Parliament adopted by 614 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 614 votes in favor, condemning the detention and sentencing of human rights defender Nasrin Sotoudeh, urging Iran to release her immediately and provide necessary healthcare. They also strongly condemned recent executions and called for diplomatic actions against unfair trials and prison visits in Iran.
The European Parliament adopted by 490 v: The European Parliament rejected a resolution to renew the authorization for genetically modified maize MON 89034, with 490 votes against 184 and 22 abstentions. Concerns included potential impacts on wild teosinte plants in Europe, deficiencies in monitoring reports, and doubts about safety studies.
The European Parliament adopted by 434 v: The European Parliament condemned escalating repression in Egypt, particularly against activists from the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR). A joint resolution was passed, expressing concern over recent arrests of EIPR activists and urging authorities to drop charges, end harassment, and ensure detainees' rights. The resolution also criticized the use of anti-terrorism laws against human rights defenders. Egyptian authorities were called upon to end intimidation of human rights organizations.
The European Parliament adopted by 489 v: The European Parliament rejected a proposal to renew the authorization for genetically modified maize MON 88017, with concerns over insufficient studies, monitoring issues, and potential risks to non-target organisms. Additionally, there were concerns about the use of complementary herbicides and lack of residue analysis.

The European Parliament rejected a resolution to renew the authorization for genetically modified maize MIR604 (SYN-IR6Ø4-5) in the market, citing concerns over insufficient safety evidence, non-compliance with monitoring methods, and international responsibilities regarding biological diversity.
The European Parliament adopted by 540 v: The European Parliament approved the 2021 EU budget, marking the first annual budget under the new Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF). The budget allocation stands at €164.25 billion in commitments and €166.06 billion in payments, with a surplus of €778.8 million and €2.001.4 million respectively, allowing for flexibility within the MFF limits. Additionally, Parliament endorsed five statements addressing child poverty and COVID-19 impact on sectors like tourism.
The European Parliament adopted by 352 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 352 votes in favor, aiming to ensure access to affordable housing for all EU citizens. The resolution emphasizes the need to address rising rents and homelessness, particularly during the COVID-19 crisis.
The European Parliament adopted by 657 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to revise Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) guidelines, aiming to complete the network by 2030 and prioritizing the elimination of bottlenecks. The focus is on making the network sustainable, supporting the EU's single market, Single European Transport Area, and global competitiveness, while also developing interconnections in rural and peripheral regions. The resolution emphasizes the importance of deploying alternative fuels for all modes of transport within the TEN-T framework.
The European Parliament adopted by 472 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 472-126, advocating for the "right to disconnect" as a fundamental worker's right in the digital age, addressing concerns over work-life balance and health issues exacerbated by remote work.
The European Parliament adopted by 548 v: The European Parliament approves a long-term budget (MFF) worth €1.074 trillion for 2021-2027, focusing on a green and digital future. Funding increases of €15 billion are allocated to flagship programs, primarily from EU fines and unallocated margins.
The European Parliament adopted by 504 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on rule of law monitoring and annual reports, welcoming Commission's reports for 2017-2019 as valuable tools. Concerns were raised about the increase in infringement proceedings launched by the Commission in 2019 compared to previous years, particularly in the environment policy area.
The European Parliament adopted by 444 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to strengthen and improve the European Arrest Warrant, aimed at combating cross-border crime more effectively. Issues addressed include detention conditions, proportionality, procedural safeguards, training, rule of law, custodial sentences, time limits, and in absentia decisions.
The European Parliament adopted by 459 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 459-62, emphasizing democracy and human rights as priorities in EU foreign policy. Members advocated integrating human rights, democracy, rule of law, and impunity fight into all external policies. Key actions include countering states withdrawing from international human rights framework, improving Council voting, adding human rights clauses in agreements, increasing budget for democracy/human rights promotion, making the EUSR a permanent post, and strengthening response to human rights issues.
The European Parliament adopted by 364 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on AI, calling for a common EU framework with harmonized definitions and ethical principles. This includes AI for military purposes being accountable, fair, traceable, reliable, and governable. AI should not violate fundamental rights or the rule of law, and judicial authorities should provide reasons when using AI-derived evidence. The Parliament also emphasized the importance of international law in regulating AI's military uses.
The European Parliament adopted by 340 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 340-100, emphasizing the need for a stronger, more autonomous foreign policy in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The EU was urged to position itself as a 'partner of choice' and defend a rules-based international order, promoting its values worldwide. Strategic cooperation with third countries, enhanced partnerships with UN, NATO, and a focus on regional approaches were emphasized for addressing global security challenges.
The European Parliament adopted by 464 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on the EU gender equality strategy (2020-2025), calling for a clearer roadmap with timelines, targets, and monitoring tools. They also urged the Commission to incorporate a gender perspective into COVID-19 response and promote women's decision-making participation, as well as address violence against women. Member States were asked to implement anti-discrimination directives and eradicate multiple forms of discrimination.
The European Parliament adopted by 644 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen cultural heritage, recognizing its value for shared memory, diversity, and unity. They urged the Commission and Member States to protect, enhance, and promote linguistic diversity, include minorities in heritage discussions, and support traditional cultural events. Education was emphasized, with a call to incorporate various art forms into curricula.
The European Parliament adopted by 526 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to develop an EU Global Connectivity Strategy, aiming to tap into untapped economic potential between Europe, Asia, and other continents. The strategy emphasizes sustainable cooperation for fiscally, economically, socially, and environmentally sound connectivity. All European countries are invited to join, including EFTA, Western Balkans, European Neighborhood, and the UK.
The European Parliament adopted 649 vote: The European Parliament passed a resolution to amend Regulation (EU) No 223/2014 (Fund for European Aid to the Most Deprived) to address COVID-19's impact on the most vulnerable. The amendment allows Member States to use additional funds for post-COVID recovery in 2021 and 2022, potentially increasing aid for food and basic necessities.
The European Parliament adopted by 653 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to expand Regulation (EU) No 654/2014, aimed at protecting EU interests in disputes under the World Trade Organisation Agreement. The amendment broadens the scope to include services and intellectual property rights, enhancing the regulation's credibility and deterrent effect.
The European Parliament adopted by 387 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (387 votes to 180) emphasizing the need for a stronger Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP). The focus is on achieving strategic autonomy, preserving stability in the EU's immediate neighborhood, and addressing potential flashpoints like the Indo-Pacific region. The Parliament also reiterated condemnation of Russia's actions in Crimea and Moldova.
The European Parliament adopted by 587 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 587 votes in favor and 50 against, aiming to strengthen the EU's list of tax havens for increased transparency and consistency, targeting jurisdictions responsible for less than 2% of global tax revenue losses. The reform is expected to be completed by the end of 2021, with a focus on formalizing the process via a legally binding instrument. The Council was urged to delegate the assessment of third jurisdictions and proposal creation to the Commission, ensuring public scrutiny and democratic accountability.
The European Parliament adopted by 689 v: The European Parliament approved, with minor exceptions, an extension of the Bonn Agreement aimed at combating pollution in the North Sea, including air pollution from ships, and Spain's accession to this accord.
The European Parliament adopted by 362 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to improve fisheries management, aiming to end overfishing by 2025. Measures include strengthening scientific coverage and improving data collection on recreational fisheries. The Commission was called upon to present proposals for Total Allowable Catches (TACs) as per the Common Fisheries Policy Regulation.
The European Parliament adopted by 592 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 592 votes in favor and 32 against, condemning the escalating human rights violations in Vietnam, particularly the imprisonment of journalists Pham Chi Dung, Nguyen Tuong Thuy, and Le Huu Minh Tuan. The resolution calls on Vietnam to immediately release these journalists and others, and urges all parties to use EU-Vietnam agreements to improve human rights in the country.
The European Parliament adopted by 391 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 391 votes in favor, 114 against, and 177 abstentions, recognizing the National Assembly elected in December 2015 and its president Juan Guaidó as Venezuela's legitimate democratic representative. It condemned illegal elections, political prisoner detention, and media censorship in Venezuela, and requested the release of political prisoners. The resolution also extended targeted sanctions to 11 additional individuals.
The European Parliament adopted by 592 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation amendment aimed at establishing a unified approach for handling the discontinuation of critical benchmarks like LIBOR. The new rules grant the Commission authority to designate a legal replacement rate, reducing uncertainty and potential risks to financial stability.
The European Parliament adopted by 462 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen the single market for services, aiming to remove national barriers and boost competitiveness by up to €297 billion. They urged Member States to ease restrictions on service movement amidst COVID-19, but regretted the lack of specific funding in the recovery plan.
The European Parliament adopted by 590 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 590 votes in favor and 16 against, condemning Turkey's treatment of Selahattin Demirtaş and calling for his immediate release from detention. The text was tabled by multiple political groups.
The European Parliament adopted by 540 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation for a technical support instrument aimed at promoting economic, social, and territorial cohesion across EU member states. The resolution supports reforms to boost investment, competitiveness, and sustainable convergence, while also strengthening institutional capacity for green and digital transitions aligned with climate change goals, UN Sustainable Development Goals, and the European Pillar of Social Rights. The instrument will assist national authorities in designing, developing, and implementing recovery plans.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 581: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 581 votes in favor and 50 against, urging Russia to immediately release Alexei Navalny and end harassment of dissident voices. The resolution also condemned Russia's use of chemical agents against its citizens and deemed its actions inappropriate for a member of the Council of Europe.
The European Parliament adopted by 597 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 597 votes in favor and 17 against, condemning the crackdown on democratic opposition in Hong Kong. The resolution calls for the immediate release of arrested opposition figures and the preservation of Hong Kong's autonomy under the 'One Country, Two Systems' principle.
The European Parliament adopted by 598 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to boost women's participation in the digital economy, addressing persistent gender disparities in the sector. They urged the Commission to implement measures promoting women in tech, fund STEM programs for girls, and establish entrepreneurship programs for female-led tech projects.
The European Parliament adopted by 677 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 677 votes in favor and 5 against, offering support to Croatia following devastating earthquakes. The resolution, tabled by multiple groups, provides €683.7 million from the EU Solidarity Fund and calls for extended absorption time for future funding due to the severity of the situation.
The European Parliament adopted by 365 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution aimed at reducing in-work poverty, with a focus on addressing gender inequality. Measures include strengthening collective bargaining systems, promoting affordable services, supporting SMEs, and enhancing education and training.
The European Parliament adopted by 571 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 571 votes in favor, 61 against, and 59 abstentions, to strengthen efforts against human trafficking. They called for analysis of digital technologies and social media in recruitment, empowering law enforcement, adopting liability rules for tech companies, improving legal instruments, and promoting information exchange.
The European Parliament adopted by 574 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 574 votes in favor, 22 against, and 95 abstentions, supporting a new circular economy action plan. The plan calls for binding EU targets by 2030 to reduce raw material and consumption footprints, and introduces a framework for sustainable products, emphasizing durability, safety, and non-toxicity as the norm in the EU market. The Commission is invited to propose legislation on sustainable products and expand the Ecodesign Directive to include non-energy related products by 2021.
The European Parliament adopted by 592 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (592 votes, 42 nays, 57 abstentions) addressing the impact of COVID-19 on youth and sport. The resolution emphasizes the need to preserve structures and ensure diversity in both sectors due to pandemic-induced risks. For youth, it highlights increased unemployment and poverty among NEETs and vulnerable groups, urging the Commission and Member States to counteract these effects through targeted policies.
The European Parliament adopted by 585 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, passing by a majority of 585 votes to 50, to amend Regulation (EU) 2017/1129, creating the EU Recovery Prospectus for quick financing access during COVID-19 recovery. The new prospectus aims to be easy for issuers, investors, and authorities. Companies admitted to trading on regulated markets for at least 18 months can opt for the simplified regime.
The European Parliament adopted by 505 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 505 votes to 124, urging Member States to report on the implementation of border procedures under the Asylum Procedures Directive, highlighting existing issues and gaps. This is not a full assessment or replacement for the Commission's report on the directive's implementation.

The European Parliament passed a resolution on women's rights in Europe, highlighting concerns about unmet targets from the Beijing Declaration and the disproportionate impact of COVID-19 on women. The Commission and Member States are called upon to develop plans and funding for addressing women and poverty.
The European Parliament adopted by 606 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to advance the European Skills Agenda, focusing on sustainable competitiveness, social fairness, and resilience. The agenda emphasizes quality training and lifelong learning for all by 2025, with a strong focus on apprenticeships and vocational education and training (VET). Parliament encourages the Commission and Member States to promote VET and create paid internships and apprenticeship programs for students. Modernizing VET systems is highlighted as crucial, particularly in post-COVID recovery.
The European Parliament adopted by 667 v: The European Parliament strongly condemned the military takeover in Myanmar and called for the immediate reinstatement of the civilian government. The resolution urged the release of President Win Myint, Aung San Suu Kyi, and others illegally arrested, and advocated for a free and fair process to draft a new constitution with the people of Myanmar.
The European Parliament adopted by 533 v:
The European Parliament approved a resolution on the ECB's annual report 2020 (533 votes to 94, with 63 abstentions). They welcomed the ECB's role in maintaining euro stability but emphasized that monetary policy should also support general economic policies for sustainable development.

The Parliament acknowledged the quick ECB response to the COVID-19 crisis but stressed that monetary policy alone wouldn't ensure a sustainable recovery, and reforms are needed for growth. They highlighted potential side effects of accommodative monetary policy and warned against underestimating future interest rate increases.
The European Parliament adopted by 526 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (526-79) supporting the EU Association Agreement with Ukraine, emphasizing its role as a reform blueprint. Members urged continued focus despite COVID-19 challenges, stressed conditionality for Ukrainian reforms, and called for updates to the agreement and stronger monitoring mechanisms. They also praised the 2019 elections' assessment by OSCE/ODIHR and the adoption of a new Electoral Code, urging alignment with international standards. Suggestions were made for institutional reform implementation in close cooperation.
The European Parliament adopted by 638 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (638-12, 44 abstentions) condemning the ongoing violence in Yemen, calling it the world's worst humanitarian crisis. They urged additional resources to address the situation, including an economic rescue package and foreign exchange injections. The parliament also called for facilitating vaccine access in Yemen during the COVID-19 pandemic and proposed a ban on arms exports to coalition members like Saudi Arabia and UAE due to human rights violations.
The European Parliament adopted by 676 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 675 votes in favor and 14 against (1 abstention), emphasizing the importance of public access to EU documents. The body expressed concern over limited information provided by the Commission on EU legislation implementation and called for increased transparency in comitology procedures and the establishment of a common database for legislative files.
The European Parliament adopted by 601 v: The European Parliament passed a law (601 votes to 77, with 14 abstentions) that codifies existing rules on weapon control within the EU. The new law sets categories for firearms possession and requires marking and registration of firearms manufactured or imported after September 2018.
The European Parliament adopted by 598 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 598 votes in favor and 43 against, condemning human rights violations in Kazakhstan. The joint resolution was tabled by multiple groups, urging Kazakhstan to respect human rights, drop politically motivated charges, and release political prisoners.
The European Parliament adopted by 659 v: The European Parliament condemned the treatment of human rights defender Paul Rusesabagina, including enforced disappearance and illegal rendition, and urged Rwanda to ensure a fair trial with family contact. The resolution passed overwhelmingly.
The European Parliament adopted by 642 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution expressing concern over the Ostrovets nuclear power plant in Belarus, located near EU borders. They are concerned about its geopolitical nature, non-compliance with safety standards, and lack of transparency. Members urged Belarus to respect international safety standards and cooperate transparently with authorities.
The European Parliament adopted by 632 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 632 votes in favor and 15 against, condemning the lack of democracy and transparency in Uganda's January 2021 election. The resolution also criticized excessive force by police and armed forces, prohibition of international observers, and violence against opposition leaders, civil society, human rights defenders, and media.
The European Parliament adopted by 545 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (545 votes, 24 nays) emphasizing the need for an improved EU Strategy on children's rights, addressing the impact of COVID-19 on children and advocating for gender-balanced policies to empower girls.
The European Parliament adopted by 578 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 578-65, to strengthen equal employment opportunities for individuals with disabilities in line with the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD). Efforts are urged to reduce disparities in employment rates and create an inclusive labor market.
The European Parliament adopted by 576 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution endorsing the activities of the European Ombudsman in 2019. The Ombudsman handled over 16,000 cases, primarily addressing issues with the Commission and EPSO, focusing on requests for information, service culture, language usage, procedural rights, administrative management, recruitment, and respect for fundamental rights.
The European Parliament adopted by 508 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (508-121) focusing on improving employment and social aspects within the annual strategy for sustainable growth 2021. They emphasized the need for equal importance of fairness and social rights in the socio-economic model, linking it to the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF). The Parliament also urged the Commission to incorporate social indicators into the European Semester Social Scoreboard.
The European Parliament adopted by 492 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (492-141) declaring the EU an LGBTIQ Freedom Zone, condemning discrimination against individuals based on their sexual orientation or gender identity. The resolution also addressed concerns in Poland and Hungary regarding intolerance towards LGBTIQ people.
The European Parliament adopted by 444 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution for a WTO-compatible Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), aimed at reducing the EU's global carbon footprint. This mechanism will monitor and potentially reduce GHG emissions from imports, while ensuring compatibility with WTO rules and free trade agreements. The CBAM is part of a broader plan to decrease greenhouse gas emissions through energy efficiency improvements and renewable energy deployment.
The European Parliament adopted 504 vote: The European Parliament passed a resolution urging the Commission to propose a directive for mandatory supply chain due diligence, aiming to require large businesses and listed SMEs to identify, prevent, and address adverse impacts on human rights, environment, and governance in their value chains.
The European Parliament adopted by 400 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on COVID-19 recovery and resilience, focusing on the European Semester and Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF). The aim is to ensure the recovery generates European added value, improves competitiveness, supports sustainable growth, and addresses ecological, digital, and social rights transitions. Parliament also called for accelerated RRF implementation and welcomed Next Generation EU for crisis response and recovery.
The European Parliament adopted by 472 v: The European Parliament rejected Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/52, which extends the approval period of certain plant protection substances, including dimoxystrobin, due to concerns about its safety and urgent need in food production. The European Parliament adopted by 495 v: The European Parliament rejected a decision to authorize genetically modified maize MZIR098 for market entry, citing concerns about insufficient data from field trials and inadequate risk assessments.
The European Parliament adopted by 686 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to revise the Construction Products Regulation (CPR), aimed at reducing trade barriers in construction products within the EU. Common technical language, including standards, is defined by harmonized European standards.
The European Parliament adopted by 568 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to amend taxation cooperation rules, accelerating the exchange of digital platform income data among Member States. The proposal also includes provisions for joint audits, group requests, and clarifying foreseeable relevance. Parliament approved the Commission's proposal with amendments, requiring faster information exchange (within 3 months) and a pre-2023 report on costs, benefits, and processing times.
The European Parliament adopted by 491 v: The European Parliament rejected a resolution, with 491 votes against and 184 in favor, regarding the approval of genetically modified cotton GHB614 × T304-40 × GHB119 for use in food, feed, and non-cultivation products. The decision was based on concerns about insufficient data, lack of consideration for herbicide residues and metabolites, an inadequate environmental monitoring plan, and unrelated monitoring activities to protection goals.
The European Parliament adopted by 669 v: The European Parliament strongly condemned the assassination of Italian Ambassador Luca Attanasio and his entourage in Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). A resolution was passed, calling for an independent investigation into the murders and urging DRC authorities to address security force officers implicated in human rights violations.
The European Parliament adopted by 610 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (610-43) condemning human rights violations in Cambodia, including violence against protesters and arrests of opposition members, journalists, and activists. The resolution calls for an end to harassment, immediate release of detainees, repeal of repressive laws, and refrain from excessive force against peaceful protests.
The European Parliament adopted by 401 v: The European Parliament approved amendments to fisheries control regulations, focusing on mandatory CCTV systems for high-risk vessels and training for inspectors. The amendments suggest equipping certain large fishing vessels with CCTV for improved compliance with the landing obligation, and incentives may be offered for voluntary implementation. Inspectors are proposed to undergo additional training.
The European Parliament adopted by 568 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 568 votes in favor, expressing deep concern over the ongoing Syrian conflict and its impact on civilians. They called for a greater political response from the EU to address the persistent political deadlock, rising humanitarian needs, and escalating food insecurity. Normalization of diplomatic relations with Syria was opposed until there's significant progress on the ground, and they strongly condemned human rights violations.
The European Parliament adopted by 633 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 633 votes in favor and 11 against, expressing concern over the deteriorating human rights situation in Bahrain. The resolution strongly condemned the death sentences of Mohammed Ramadan and Husain Ali Moosa, urging an immediate halt to their execution and a retrial complying with international fair trial standards. The Parliament also called for an immediate moratorium on the use of the death penalty in Bahrain.

The European Parliament approved a resolution supporting Kosovo's commitment to EU integration, emphasizing the need for political will and administrative capacity enhancement. They also expressed concerns over freedom of expression in the Serbian community, political instability post-elections, and urged Council to adopt a visa-free regime for Kosovo citizens.

Progress towards democracy and rule of law was acknowledged, but efforts against corruption and organized crime were highlighted as areas requiring improvement, with a call for stronger institutions.
The European Parliament adopted by 460 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution for a revitalized EU-Africa strategy, aiming to foster sustainable and inclusive development. The EU is encouraged to collaborate with countries committed to Africa's long-term prosperity, prioritizing regional integration and tailored country-specific approaches. A call for updating regional policies towards African sub-regions was also made, with a focus on funding for success.
The European Parliament adopted by 581 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution supporting Albania's EU integration efforts and the launch of accession negotiations upon meeting Council conditions. The parliament also emphasized the importance of free and fair elections in April 2021 for democratic renewal, transparency in public institutions, and regular communication with civil society and media. Additionally, they suggested involving Albania and other Western Balkan countries in the Conference on the Future of Europe.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament approved a resolution, with 538 votes in favor, 69 against, and 79 abstentions, encouraging Serbia to commit clearly to EU membership requirements. The European Parliament adopted by 558 v: The European Parliament approved, with 558 votes in favor and 70 against, a resolution endorsing Northern Macedonia's progress on EU reforms, particularly in rule of law, anti-corruption, and democratic institutions. Parliament emphasized the need for EU Member States to expedite Council approval for negotiations and hold the first Intergovernmental Conference as soon as possible. The Parliament also highlighted the importance of maintaining the rule of law through ongoing efforts against organized crime and corruption, financial investigations, and appropriate sanctions.
The European Parliament adopted by 470 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to enhance implementation and enforcement of defense package directives, aiming to streamline the internal market for defense products. Despite support, concerns remain over market fragmentation, with significant procurement expenditure still occurring outside the directive, and many contracts awarded nationally. Exclusion provisions under Article 346 TFEU could potentially hinder full implementation.
The European Parliament adopted by 425 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to improve Air Quality Directives (2004/107/EC and 2008/50/EC), addressing high pollution levels causing over 400,000 premature deaths annually. The directives, based on outdated standards, were deemed only partially effective in reducing air pollution and its health impacts. The European Green Deal commits to revising air quality standards.
The European Parliament adopted by 577 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to establish an EU strategy for sustainable tourism, aiming to support the tourism and transport industries severely impacted by COVID-19. The resolution calls for continued financial aid, integration of the industry into development plans, sustainability enhancements, digitalization, and modernization. It also emphasizes the need for common, coordinated criteria for safe travel and the deployment of the EU Passenger Locator Form, prioritizing data protection.
The European Parliament adopted by 483 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) evaluation, recognizing its success and global impact as a data protection standard. The European Parliament adopted by 529 v: The European Parliament passed, by 529 votes to 148, a resolution on the Rule-of-Law Conditionality Mechanism (Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2020/2092), applicable since January 2021. The regulation binds all Member States and EU institutions, with breaches triggering measures regardless of their pre-existing status. The resolution emphasizes the need for immediate attention to rule-of-law issues in certain Member States.
The European Parliament adopted by 571 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation (571 votes to 29, with 29 abstentions) on controlling exports of cyber-surveillance assets that interfere with human rights. The regulation covers hardware, software, and technology designed for covert intrusion into information systems. The Union will introduce controls on certain cyber surveillance technologies based on a unilateral list.
The European Parliament adopted by 462 v:

The Parliament also emphasized the need for increased funding for SMEs through various programs, particularly the Single Market Programme and InvestEU, to encourage entrepreneurship and provide capital support. The European Parliament adopted by 517 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation amending VAT-based own resources collection, simplifying and streamlining calculations with changes to the Council's draft, but rejected provisions for a rapid review procedure.
The European Parliament adopted by 474 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to amend the securitization framework in response to COVID-19, aiming to enhance institutional lending capacity and loss absorption. The European Parliament adopted by 572 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution emphasizing the crucial role of cohesion policy in combating climate change, aiming for climate neutrality by 2050. Local and regional authorities are encouraged to adopt climate strategies aligned with EU targets.
The European Parliament adopted by 540 v: The European Parliament approved, by a majority of 540 votes to 109, a regulation establishing rules for Member States to contribute a levy on non-recycled plastic packaging waste to the EU Commission. The European Parliament adopted by 646 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to improve marine litter governance, emphasizing the need for a revised integrated maritime policy and international cooperation against plastic pollution.
The European Parliament adopted by 474 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to amend the Securitization Regulation, aiming to facilitate the use of securitization during Europe's recovery from COVID-19. The amendments also address the expected increase in non-performing exposures due to COVID-19 by allowing institutions to trade these exposures through securitization, while separating risks from systemically important parts of the financial system.
The European Parliament adopted by 639 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution on enhancing digital education, emphasizing the need to address digital skill gaps among Europeans due to disparities in socio-economic status, age, gender, income, education, and employment. The European Parliament adopted by 494 v: The European Parliament voted (494-94) to strengthen the international role of the euro, recognizing its potential benefits but acknowledging that it currently lags behind the US dollar as a reserve and invoicing currency. The European Parliament adopted by 453 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to enhance and green maritime transport, aiming to reduce emissions in EU waters. The resolution aims to address the distortion of competition between fossil fuels and clean alternatives in maritime transport.
The European Parliament adopted by 602 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (602-8, 78 abstentions) for a European data strategy, aiming to strengthen EU businesses' competitiveness and advance AI, while ensuring respect for EU values and rights. The European Parliament adopted, by 645: The European Parliament approved a transparency register agreement (645-5, 49 abstentions), establishing guidelines for ethical interest representation among signatory institutions. The European Parliament adopted by 673 v: The European Parliament approved a Strategic Innovation Agenda for the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT) 2021-2027, aiming to boost innovation talent in Europe. The European Parliament decided by 627 v: The European Parliament postponed a vote on granting discharge for the implementation of the 2019 budget of the European Council and the Council, due to lack of cooperation from the Council and insufficient information.

The European Parliament decided by 635 v: The European Parliament approved, by a significant margin, the discharge of the European Data Protection Supervisor's 2019 budget implementation, with minimal errors noted and effective control systems in place. The European Parliament adopted by 682 v: The European Parliament approved the discharge for the European Ombudsman's 2019 budget, passing with a large majority and granting no significant issues were found in human resources and procurement management. The European Parliament decided by 606 v: The European Parliament approved, by a majority of 606 votes to 85, the budget for the European External Action Service (EEAS) for 2019, with no significant issues identified. The European Parliament decided by 604 v: The European Parliament approved, by 604 votes to 89, the discharge to the Executive Director of the SESAR Joint Undertaking for the implementation of the budget and closure of accounts for 2019. The European Parliament decided by 504 v: The European Parliament approved the 2019 budget implementation for the EU and related agencies by a vote of 504-178, with 16 abstentions. The European Parliament adopted by 533 t: The European Parliament passed a resolution (533 for, 37 against, 47 abstentions) enhancing rail passenger rights. The European Parliament adopted by 605 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution on soil protection, emphasizing its crucial role as a carbon store and vital ecosystem for human existence. The resolution identified several threats to soil health in the EU, including climate change, erosion, contamination, and desertification.
The European Parliament adopted by 632 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, passing by 632 votes to 23 with 38 abstentions, consenting to the EU-Honduras Voluntary Partnership Agreement on forest law enforcement and trade in timber products. The European Parliament adopted by 337 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to establish the European Defence Fund for 2021-2027, aiming to enhance competitiveness and innovation in Europe's defense industry. The vote was 337 in favor, 178 against, with 109 abstentions. The amended proposal will be renegotiated among institutions.
The European Parliament adopted par 643: The European Parliament approved a regulation for a multiannual management plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern Atlantic and Mediterranean, aligning with ICCAT recommendations. This aims to conserve and manage fisheries under ICCAT's jurisdiction.
The European Parliament adopted by 549 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (549 votes in favor, 70 against, 75 abstentions) to address challenges in taxing the digital economy. The European Parliament decided by 635 v: The European Parliament approved, by 635 votes to 56, the discharge of the Executive Director of CEPOL for the financial year 2019 and the closure of its accounts. The European Parliament decided by 582 v: The European Parliament approved the financial statements of the Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators (ACER) for 2019, granting discharge to the Director.
