The EIB was encouraged to strengthen its anti-tax avoidance measures, update policies according to the 5th Anti-Money Laundering Directive, and increase funding for technological transition.
The European Parliament adopted by 518 v: The European Parliament approved a General Union Environment Action Programme to 2030, aiming to transition towards a climate-neutral, sustainable economy while protecting and restoring the environment. The plan aligns with the European Green Deal and UN Sustainable Development Goals. The decision was passed with 518 votes in favor, 130 against, and 47 abstentions. Further negotiations are required.
The European Parliament decided by 353 v: The European Parliament passed amendments to its Rules of Procedure, clarifying budget discharge procedures, introducing a new rule for Union trust funds, deleting an inadmissibility rule, and promoting gender balance in committee bureaus and interparliamentary delegations.
The European Parliament adopted by 641 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to incorporate the 2020 surplus of €1.7 billion into the 2021 budget, primarily due to higher customs duty collections and under-spending. The funds are intended for rapid financial assistance to those affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. Member States were encouraged to allocate their reduced contributions towards pandemic-related actions.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 546: The European Parliament approved a legislative resolution, passing by 546 votes to 69, to expand the scope of the Fundamental Rights Agency, now encompassing police cooperation and judicial matters, aiming for improved efficiency and governance.
The European Parliament adopted by 600 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to strengthen the ECSC liquidation asset portfolio, enabling sales for annual €111 million allocations until 2027 and diversifying investments to improve risk-return performance.
The European Parliament adopted by 587 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation to strengthen the role of the European Medicines Agency in crisis preparedness and management for medicinal products and medical devices, learning from the COVID-19 pandemic. The regulation provides a framework for preparing, preventing, coordinating, and managing public health emergencies at EU level, as well as preventing shortages of essential medical supplies.
The European Parliament adopted by 497 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to establish the European Maritime and Fisheries Fund (2021-2027), focusing on sustainable fishing, aquaculture, food security, blue economy growth, and coastal community prosperity. The fund aims to protect marine life without increasing fishing capacity.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 627: The European Parliament approved a resolution to amend the Research Fund for Coal and Steel (RFCS) funding, allowing for annual allocations of €111 million from 2021-2027. This includes €40 billion for collaborative research in coal and steel sectors and €71 billion for breakthrough technologies towards zero-carbon steel making and just transition projects for coal mines.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 534: The European Parliament passed a resolution to combat fraud, reporting a decrease in both fraudulent and non-fraudulent irregularities by 2% overall and 34% in fraudulent cases in 2019. Concern was expressed over VAT fraud's impact on the EU budget, with a focus on combating Missing Trader Intra-Community (MTIC) fraud estimated to cost €40-60 billion annually.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 634: The European Parliament approved a resolution to complete the European Research Area, aiming to facilitate free movement of researchers and circulation of knowledge. The goal is to contribute to multiple EU strategies like SME, Digital, Green Deal, and UN Sustainable Development Goals. The Parliament endorsed plans to boost R&I investments, reach a 3% GDP goal, and improve access for EU researchers. Member States are urged to increase public spending on R&I to 1.25% of GDP by 2030, with a focus on joint programs and European partnerships.
The European Parliament adopted by 588 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (588-21, 79 abstentions) to establish Antarctic Marine Protected Areas covering over 3 million km², aiming to create one of history's largest marine protection zones. The areas, in the eastern Antarctic and Weddell Sea, are crucial for global ocean circulation and climate. These MPAs will contribute to EU and global commitments on marine biodiversity conservation, with negotiations ongoing in CCAMLR. The MPAs are proposed as a basis for discussions at the COP15 UN Biodiversity Conference in Kunming, China.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 470: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 470 votes in favor and 199 against, objecting to the approval of genetically modified soybean DAS-81419-2 for market placement. This decision was based on concerns about insufficient data regarding pest and disease pressure and potential ecological interactions with the environment.
The European Parliament adopted a legisl: The European Parliament approved a reform to enhance the Visa Information System (VIS), aiming to simplify visa applications, strengthen security checks, and improve information exchange between Member States on long-stay visa or residence permit holders. This includes updates to VIS, Entry/Exit System (EES), European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS), SIS Return, SIS Borders, and Border Interoperability regulations.
The European Parliament adopted by 473 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation for border management and visa funding from 2021-2027, aiming to strengthen integrated border control, facilitate legal crossings, prevent irregular immigration, combat cross-border crime, and support a harmonized common visa policy.
The European Parliament adopted by 470 v: The European Parliament rejected a decision to allow genetically modified soybean DAS-81419-2 x DAS-44406-6 in markets, due to concerns about insufficient monitoring tools for gene transfers and potential creation of genetic variability.

The European Parliament rejected a draft Commission decision to authorize genetically modified maize 1507 × MIR162 × MON810 × NK603 and related sub-combinations, due to concerns about herbicide assessment and Bt toxins.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 667: The European Parliament has approved a resolution to accelerate the deployment of the European Rail Traffic Management System (ERTMS), aiming to improve railway safety, infrastructure capacity, and align with the European Green Deal objectives. The resolution addresses challenges in governance and coordination between Member States to expedite ERTMS implementation.
The European Parliament adopted by 529 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 529-150, urging the Commission to immediately apply the Rule of Law conditionality regulation without delay, expressing concern over the Commission's delayed guidelines and calling for prompt investigation into potential breaches affecting the EU budget.
The European Parliament adopted by 509 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (509-63) to emphasize the need for fair, resilient, and green value chains in response to COVID-19's impact on international trade. They urged the Commission to focus on supply chain sustainability in its industrial strategy, particularly for critical raw materials and essential goods.
The European Parliament adopted by 434 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to establish the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF 2.0) for 2021-2027, focusing on transport, energy, and digital infrastructure. The objectives include increasing competitiveness, promoting smart, sustainable growth, and consolidating cohesion. Key amendments involve developing projects of common interest in efficient, interconnected networks and adapting transport infrastructure for dual civilian and defense mobility needs.
The European Parliament adopted by 470 v: The European Parliament rejected, by 470 votes to 200 with 22 abstentions, a decision to renew the authorization for genetically modified maize Bt11 (SYNBTØ11-1) in non-food and feed uses, citing concerns over literature search, monitoring reports, glufosinate residue levels, and ethical issues.
The European Parliament adopted by 584 v: The European Parliament approved the EU Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime (EU GHRSR), strengthening its global human rights role. They urged a broader, coherent strategy, calling for QMV in adopting sanctions and extending the regime to include corruption acts. Flexibility is needed to address emerging threats like COVID-19 restrictions or violence against human rights defenders.
The European Parliament adopted by 561 v: The European Parliament approved, with 561 votes in favor, 43 against, and 88 abstentions, a proposal to grant the Commission authority to define certain terms in the VAT Directive (2006/112/EC). This decision establishes a committee for overseeing implementing acts by the Commission in specific areas of VAT, while the Council retains its powers on matters not falling within the Commission's newly defined scope.
The European Parliament adopted, by 667: The European Parliament passed a resolution (667 votes to 11, with 14 abstentions) on the impact of offshore wind farms and other renewable energy systems on fishing sectors. The goal is to meet 30% of EU's electricity demand by 2050 through offshore wind energy, increasing current capacity from 12 GW to 300 GW. Long-term vision includes minimizing negative impacts on ecosystems, fish stocks, and biodiversity during the 25-30 year life cycle of offshore wind turbines.
The European Parliament adopted by 459 v: The European Parliament strongly condemned a Hungarian law passed on June 15, 2021, that restricts LGBTIQ rights and children's rights, violating EU values. The resolution was adopted with 459 votes in favor, 147 against, and 58 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 629 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 629 votes in favor and 19 against, condemning the deteriorating human rights situation in Nicaragua. The resolution was tabled by multiple groups, including EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens/EFA, and ECR, due to recent electoral law reforms, party dissolutions, and arbitrary arrests of opposition members.
The European Parliament adopted by 481 v: The European Parliament approved the establishment of the Internal Security Fund (ISF) for 2021-2027, aiming to enhance Union security through terrorism prevention, combating violent extremism, serious crime, cybercrime, and victim support. It also focuses on information exchange, cross-border coordination, and a common intelligence culture.
The European Parliament adopted by 603 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, by 603 votes to 2, expressing concern over repression of opposition parties in Turkey, particularly the Peoples' Democratic Party (HDP. The resolution condemned the targeting of HDP and urged the Turkish government to allow all political parties to operate freely. It also strongly condemned the killing of HDP member Deniz Poyraz and called for a thorough investigation.
The European Parliament adopted by 661 v: The European Parliament condemned the execution of child offenders in Saudi Arabia, particularly Mustafa Hashem al-Darwish and Abdullah al-Howaiti, despite Saudi Arabia's claim to have abolished such executions. The resolution was adopted unanimously, except for 3 votes and 23 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 522 v: The European Parliament passed an amendment to expand the Visa Information System (VIS), used for monitoring third-country nationals requiring visas to travel to the Schengen area. The VIS will now cover long-stay visas and residence permits, aiming to address security information gaps and optimize EU border management.
The European Parliament adopted by 666 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 666 votes in favor and 5 against, urging Iran to halt the execution of Swedish-Iranian academic Ahmadreza Djalali, condemning his torture and arbitrary detention, and calling for his immediate release.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 578: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 578 votes in favor and 29 against, condemning the forced closure of pro-opposition newspaper Apple Daily in Hong Kong. The text was tabled by multiple groups, including EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens/EFA, and ECR.
The European Parliament adopted by 387 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (387 votes to 161) emphasizing the need for LGBTIQ rights protection and progress in Europe. The resolution highlighted concerns over discrimination, violence, and obstacles faced by LGBTIQ individuals and families, urging the EU to take a unified approach to recognizing same-sex marriages and partnerships, and addressing discrimination within the EU.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 645: The European Parliament approved a resolution to allocate €4.2 billion for the Brexit Adjustment Reserve in the 2021 Union budget, exceeding the expenditure ceilings of the Multiannual Financial Framework. The vote passed with 645 votes in favor, 14 against, and 36 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 641 v: The European Parliament approved, with 641 votes in favor and 38 against, an extension of Community plant variety rights for asparagus, flower bulbs, woody small fruits, and woody ornamentals by five years. The amended text acknowledges that new varieties of these plants take more time to become profitable than others.
The European Parliament adopted by 561 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on enhancing tax information exchange, aiming to combat unfair practices and improve cooperation between Member States. The resolution encompasses updates to the Administrative Cooperation Directive (DAC), including provisions for automatic exchange of financial account information, advance tax rulings, country-by-country reports, beneficial ownership access, and cross-border tax planning arrangements.
The European Parliament adopted a legisl: The European Parliament approved a resolution to maintain employment guidelines for Member States in 2021, emphasizing inclusive labor markets, social protection, and focus on vulnerable groups. The decision includes prioritizing the European Child Guarantee and integrating the European Semester for comprehensive policy coordination.
The European Parliament adopted by 614 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen partnership with EU outermost regions, focusing on addressing their economic, social, climate, and cultural issues. They called for a systematic 'OR reflex' within EU institutions, a new strategy for the regions, and investment in jobs, solidarity, and youth.
The European Parliament adopted by 494 v: The European Parliament passed a recommendation (494 votes, 103 against) aimed at shaping EU-Russia political relations, distinguishing between the Russian people and Putin's authoritarian regime. The focus is on deterring Russia's security threat, combating human rights abuses, and developing a comprehensive strategy to engage with Russian citizens while addressing their concerns.
The European Parliament adopted by 641 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution aiming to boost sustainable inland waterway transport, currently accounting for 6.1% of EU freight, with a goal to increase it significantly to reduce road congestion and emissions. The Commission was urged to lead on green, efficient, and digital initiatives, harmonize regulations, promote best practices, and facilitate information exchange between Member States.
The European Parliament adopted by 594 v: The European Parliament passed, by 594 votes to 85, an amended regulation strengthening the EU's response to cross-border health threats, including pandemics. Proposals include a call for a WHO Framework Convention on Pandemic Preparedness and Response.
The European Parliament adopted by 664 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on a revised Atlantic maritime strategy, aiming to address regional challenges. Despite acknowledging initial efforts, concerns were raised about insufficient funding and governance complexity. Recommendations include utilizing funds from the 2021-2027 multi-annual financial framework for projects addressing Atlantic regions' multidimensional issues.
The European Parliament decided, by 659: The European Parliament voted to reconsider inter-institutional negotiations on aligning Directive 2014/41/EU with EU data protection rules, passing with a large majority (659-7) and 22 abstentions.
The European Parliament decided, by 638: The European Parliament voted to reconsider inter-institutional negotiations on aligning Council Framework Decision 2002/465/JHA with EU data protection rules, passing with 638 votes in favor and 29 against, with 21 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 566 v: The European Parliament approved, with 566 votes in favor, the proposal for an Overseas Association Decision, focusing on Greenland and Denmark. The decision aims to support sustainable development objectives, address educational challenges, strengthen resilience, improve competitiveness, and promote cooperation among the overseas countries and territories (OCTs). Special consideration is given to the least developed OCTs to help them overcome structural constraints.
The European Parliament adopted by 652 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to establish the Brexit Adjustment Reserve, providing support for Member States affected by the UK's withdrawal. The maximum resources amount to €5.47 billion, with provisional allocations in 2021 and 2022.
The European Parliament adopted by 664 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 664 votes in favor and 4 against, aiming to accelerate the transition to animal-free research, testing, and education. The text was proposed by multiple groups, including EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens/EFA, ECR, and The Left. Despite EU encouragement for non-animal methods, challenges persist due to bureaucratic hurdles, insufficient funding, and varying national implementation.
The European Parliament adopted by 650 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to support the fishing industry and generate employment in coastal communities, addressing concerns exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Recommendations include improving statistical representation of jobs in the sector and promoting generational renewal through better data collection for the social pillar under the Common Fisheries Policy (CFP).
The European Parliament\nadopted by 556: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 556 votes in favor and 105 against, on the conditions for highly skilled employment of non-EU workers. The revised Blue Card Directive sets admission criteria, including a salary threshold of at least 1.0 times the average gross annual salary in the member state, but not exceeding 1.6 times. Member states can offer lower thresholds to recent graduates for a specified period.
The European Parliament adopted by 377 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to establish an independent EU ethics body for enhanced transparency and integrity. The new body will advise on ethical rules for Commission, MEPs, and staff across EU institutions.
The European Parliament adopted by 427 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (427 votes in favor, 119 against) to designate gender-based violence as a new crime area under EU law, aiming to address and protect LGBTIQ+ individuals from online and offline abuse. This action comes in response to rising gender-based violence during the COVID-19 crisis, with surveys showing one in three women in the EU have experienced physical or sexual violence since age 15.
The European Parliament adopted by 570 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (570-61, 40 abstentions) for a stronger, values-focused EU-China strategy. The strategy aims to shape relations comprehensively, prioritizing EU values and promoting a rules-based multilateral order. It recognizes China as both a partner and competitor, with a focus on dialogue on global challenges, including human rights, environment, and COVID-19 recovery.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 679: The European Parliament approved, with minor exceptions, an agreement on air services between the EU and South Korea, enhancing opportunities for EU airlines and promoting legal certainty in commercial operations.
The European Parliament adopted by 598 v: The European Parliament approved, with 598 votes in favor and 84 against, amendments to strengthen the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). The ECDC's mandate will now extend beyond communicable diseases to include major non-communicable ones like cardiovascular and respiratory diseases. EU Member States are required to develop national plans and provide data for rapid risk assessment.
The European Parliament adopted by 502 v: The European Parliament, on August 11, 2021, passed a resolution expressing concern over media freedom deterioration and rule of law issues in Poland. The resolution opposed the 'Lex TVN' draft bill that restricts broadcast licences to companies majority-owned by European Economic Area entities. The Polish Senate rejected this bill on September 9, but the legislative process continues. The Parliament condemned efforts to silence critical content and reduce media diversity in Poland.
The European Parliament adopted by 426 v: The European Parliament strongly condemned the Cuban government's violent response to July protests over shortages and human rights issues, calling for an end to repression, release of political prisoners, and compliance with international human rights recommendations.
The European Parliament adopted by 383 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 383 votes in favor and 47 against, condemning the conviction of human rights defender Ahmed Mansoor in the UAE for his advocacy work. The resolution strongly criticizes the violation of Mansoor's rights and calls for his immediate release, as well as an end to the imprisonment of other human rights defenders in the UAE.
The European Parliament adopted by 377 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 377 votes in favor, condemning the violent conditions in Kenya's Kakuma refugee camp, particularly affecting LGBTIQ+ individuals. The EU urges Kenyan authorities to investigate and bring justice for a recent arson attack on LGBTIQ+ refugees.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 533: The European Parliament approved, with 533 votes in favor and 107 against, an agreement amending the visa facilitation deal between the EU and Cape Verde, aiming to simplify short-stay visa procedures for citizens of both parties.
The European Parliament adopted by 575 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 575 votes in favor and 71 against, expressing concern over the critical situation in Lebanon due to political, economic, social, and health crises, among others. The resolution emphasizes the need for a transparent investigation into the Beirut port explosion and urges the EU to support Lebanon's efforts to combat corruption and preserve its stability.
The European Parliament adopted by 536 v: The European Parliament condemned the Taliban takeover in Afghanistan and refused to recognize their current government. They expressed deep concerns about the future of Afghanistan under Taliban rule, particularly the imposition of radical sharia law and violation of basic rights and freedoms. A call for an end to violence was issued.
The European Parliament has adopted by 5: The European Parliament passed a resolution (524-39) to improve working conditions and social protection for platform workers, recognizing the need for equal rights regardless of employment status. A proposed European framework aims to ensure decent working conditions while addressing precarious forms of platform work.
The European Parliament adopted by 506 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (506-81) to combat tax evasion and reform EU policies on harmful tax practices, addressing emerging issues like aggressive general regimes. The Council's Code of Conduct Group has been ineffective in eradicating unfair tax advantages for large companies, leading to the need for stronger measures due to tax scandals and pandemic-related revenue losses.

The European Parliament passed a resolution (506-36) emphasizing international cooperation in the Arctic, focusing on sustainable development, climate change response, and multilateral governance. The EU is urged to engage with new actors like China, prioritize peaceful cooperation, and address security concerns while respecting Arctic states' sovereignty.
The European Parliament adopted by 495 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on the Banking Union Annual Report 2020 (495-100), emphasizing the need for completion of the European Deposit Insurance Scheme. Members welcomed new members Bulgaria and Croatia, and discussed Denmark and Sweden's potential entry. Despite banks' resilience during the crisis, structural inefficiencies persist, particularly high non-performing loans. A fully operational Banking Union is seen as crucial for a robust European economy and strong capital markets union.
The European Parliament adopted by 493 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on the EU Trust Fund and Refugees in Turkey, with 493 votes in favor, 88 against, and 103 abstentions. The resolution expressed concerns over limited parliamentary involvement in decision-making, supervision, and control of EU contributions to these funds. It called for detailed information from the Commission on operational committee decisions and emphasized that extensions should primarily be technical, facilitating a smooth transition to the new multi-annual financial framework (MFF).
The European Parliament adopted by 686 v: The European Parliament approved, with minor exceptions, the establishment of a 35-member delegation to the EU-UK Parliamentary Partnership Assembly, aimed at overseeing the implementation of the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement. This delegation can request information, be informed of decisions, and make recommendations regarding the agreement.
The European Parliament adopted by 407 v: The European Parliament rejected an extension of the approval period for the toxic pesticide chlorotoluron, citing safety concerns and lack of urgent need. The Commission is urged to reconsider its decision and submit a new proposal based on scientific evidence.
The European Parliament adopted by 582 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to rebuild overfished Mediterranean fish stocks, reducing them from 88% in 2014 to 75% in 2018. The parliament urged the Commission to identify obstacles and take action to rebuild fish stocks, strengthen marine protected areas, and expand recovery zones.
The European Parliament adopted by 377 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution on AI in criminal law, emphasizing respect for fundamental rights. The EU's data protection framework should form the basis for future regulation, prohibiting AI use when it infringes upon these rights, and categorizing high-risk uses that significantly impact individuals.
The European Parliament adopted by 513 v: The European Parliament approved IPA III, a regulation for pre-accession assistance, with 513 votes in favor, 97 against, and 45 abstentions. The adopted version aims to support beneficiary countries in adopting reforms aligned with EU values, focusing on rule of law, democracy, human rights, migration management, public administration effectiveness, and good governance.
The European Parliament adopted by 351 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (351-31, 304 abstentions) calling for policy coherence in addressing biodiversity loss in developing countries within the 2030 Agenda. The EU was urged to integrate conservation, sustainable resource use, and ecosystem restoration into its development cooperation policy and partnerships, with a focus on science-based biodiversity targets and the introduction of a right to a safe environment in the EU Charter. The Commission's commitment to propose a binding human rights and environmental due diligence for companies was welcomed.
The European Parliament adopted by 591 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen EU cyber defense capabilities, emphasizing the importance of a common policy and increased cooperation. Measures include developing shared support capabilities, enhancing cyber security, and improving information sharing among Member States. The Parliament also called for closer collaboration with CERT-EU and the development of a rapid response network against cyberattacks.
The European Parliament adopted by 550 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (550 votes to 83) affirming support for a new transatlantic partnership with the US, emphasizing shared values and strategic autonomy. The partnership aims to strengthen global democracy, combat disinformation, shape digital future, coordinate on Russia and China, and invest in infrastructure.
The European Parliament adopted by 615 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, 615-24, to strengthen EU road safety policy for 2021-2030, aiming for 'Vision Zero' with zero deaths and serious injuries. The new framework includes targets, a 'safe system' approach, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and increased funding for safer infrastructure.
The European Parliament adopted by 510 v: The European Parliament strongly condemns domestic violence, particularly during COVID-19, and calls for immediate action. They urge Member States to address the rise in domestic violence, exchange best practices, and request the Commission to develop an EU protocol on women's crisis protection, establish an emergency alert system, and consider essential services for victims. Regrettably, the Istanbul Convention has not been ratified by the European Union.
The European Parliament adopted by 624 v: The European Parliament approved a new Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreement with Greenland and Denmark, replacing the 2007 agreement. The consent allows for a six-year agreement (2021-2026) and a four-year protocol (2021-2024), aiming to align with the reformed Common Fisheries Policy's external dimension.
The European Parliament adopted by 618 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 618 votes in favor and 4 against, urging an end to hostilities in Tigray, Ethiopia, due to the humanitarian crisis affecting millions. The resolution was tabled by multiple political groups, expressing concern over reports of human rights violations and limited access to aid.
The European Parliament adopted by 603 v: The European Parliament approved a Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreement with Greenland and Denmark, aiming to benefit both fisheries sectors. However, concerns were raised about exceeding scientific advice in the previous agreement. A new agreement was adopted, acknowledging complex negotiations and internal political challenges in Greenland.
The European Parliament adopted by 506 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 506 votes in favor and 29 against, condemning the ongoing repression in Belarus following a year of protests. The resolution calls out the Belarusian authorities for detaining thousands, holding over 700 political prisoners, and failing to investigate violence against protesters. The Parliament stands in solidarity with the people of Belarus and does not recognize Alexander Lukashenka as president.
The European Parliament adopted by 381 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution condemning Texas' SB8 abortion law, which effectively bans most abortions as early as six weeks into pregnancy. The resolution calls for the swift repeal of SB8 to uphold women's reproductive rights and ensure accessible abortion services in Texas.
The European Parliament adopted by 647 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with only two votes against and 31 abstentions, condemning the February 2021 coup in Myanmar and expressing concern over human rights violations against religious and ethnic groups. The resolution was tabled by multiple political groups.
The European Parliament adopted by 660 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 660 votes in favor and 2 against, condemning the illegal arrest, detention, and conviction of Paul Rusesabagina in Rwanda. They called for his immediate release on humanitarian grounds. The resolution also urged the Rwandan Government to ensure Rusesabagina's well-being and allow him access to medication.
The European Parliament adopted by 677 v: The European Parliament approved, with minimal opposition, a resolution to extend the suspension of certain customs duties on industrial products imported into the Canary Islands. This move aims to support local economic operators and secure stable employment on these islands, as the current measures are set to expire at year's end. The extension was requested by the Spanish Government due to the region's structural market limitations.
The European Parliament adopted by 579 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (579-12) focusing on enhancing disability rights, addressing barriers in areas like public transport, education, and sign languages. The resolution emphasizes the need for Member States to implement UN Convention on Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), consult disabled people's organizations, and ratify the Optional Protocol to CRPD without delay.
The European Parliament adopted by 563 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to reduce methane emissions, focusing on human-induced sources in fossil fuels, waste, and agriculture. They called for binding targets and a global agreement at COP26 to significantly decrease EU methane emissions by 2030, emphasizing the potential for low-cost mitigation measures.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament approved changes to the EU budget for 2021, updating revenue following the implementation of Council Decision (EU, Euratom) 2020/2053. These changes include an increase in own resources ceilings, a higher rate for customs duty collection costs, a uniform VAT call rate, and a new plastic waste-based resource.

The European Parliament approved a resolution for a sustainable, fair, and animal-friendly "Farm to Fork" strategy, aiming to create a resilient food system aligned with the European Green Deal and SDGs. The Parliament encouraged immediate action from the Commission, including legislative measures and financial support for transition. They also supported the development of strategic food policy plans and a cross-cutting governance approach for coherence between related EU policies.
The European Parliament adopted by 580 v: The European Parliament approved a recommendation to strengthen EU-Taiwan political relations and cooperation, aiming to foster dialogue and cooperation amidst China's military threats towards Taiwan. Taiwan is the EU's 5th largest trading partner in Asia and 15th globally.
The European Parliament adopted by 675 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution urging the Commission to protect workers from asbestos, which causes thousands of deaths annually. They emphasized the need for a comprehensive strategy, ESRAA, to ensure safe removal of asbestos in EU, prioritizing worker safety and utilizing EU funds for improved diagnostics and waste management.
The European Parliament adopted by 543 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 543 votes in favor, urging support for artists and cultural recovery in the EU. Recognizing the significant value of culture and its industries, they called for immediate aid during the COVID-19 pandemic and long-term structural support to revitalize the sector, including education opportunities for future generations.
The European Parliament adopted by 562 v: The European Parliament passed an amendment (562 votes to 36, with 19 abstentions) to a Directive on motor vehicle liability insurance, expanding coverage exclusions for e-bikes, segways, electric scooters, and vehicles used exclusively for motorsports. The Directive aims to ensure equal protection for traffic accident victims across the EU, insolvency protection, and fair claims processing for cross-border policy holders.
The European Parliament adopted by 347 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution aimed at improving employment and social policies in the Eurozone post-COVID-19. The focus is on promoting sustainable well-being for all Europeans through solidarity, social justice, gender equality, high-quality public services, and quality employment.
The European Parliament adopted by 458 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution calling for increased transparency in EU's handling of COVID-19 vaccine contracts with pharmaceutical companies. The Commission is urged to work openly and share information with citizens, but currently refuses to disclose expert names or the identities of seven member states involved in negotiations. Accountability is emphasized as crucial for the EU's vaccine strategy's global credibility, with Parliament needing full access to budgetary details for scrutiny.
The European Parliament adopted a legisl: The European Parliament approved a directive aimed at harmonizing rules for credit servicers and purchasers dealing with non-performing loans from EU banks. The directive establishes a designated authority for authorization and supervision of these entities, requiring applicants to be legal entities based in their home Member State. The directive aims to support the development of secondary markets for non-performing loans while safeguarding borrowers' rights.
The European Parliament adopted by 527 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution urging strong climate action at COP26 in Glasgow, emphasizing the need for a new consensus on global climate neutrality by mid-century. The EU was urged to phase out fossil fuel subsidies by 2025 and accelerate climate action with a five-year timeframe for all countries. The Parliament also called for inclusive attendance at COP26, considering COVID-19 restrictions.
The European Parliament adopted by 577 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 577 votes in favor, aiming to support Europe's media industries during the Digital Decade. The resolution emphasizes the need for comprehensive industrial strategies and increased funding for news media, audiovisual sectors, and cultural SMEs, particularly in response to the financial impact of COVID-19 on these industries.
The European Parliament adopted by 624 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation establishing nine EU joint undertakings for strengthening and integrating scientific, technological, and innovation capacities. The vote passed with 624 in favor, 3 against, and 33 abstentions. The joint undertakings aim to address global challenges, ensure EU competitiveness, focus on sustainability and resilience, develop innovative solutions, and contribute to Union strategic priorities.
The European Parliament adopted by 675 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, with 675 votes in favor, 14 against, and 11 abstentions, regarding the effective use of EU Solidarity Fund resources for natural disasters, including COVID-19. The resolution emphasizes the need to address both immediate crises and long-term impacts of climate change on disaster recovery.
The European Parliament adopted by 578 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (578-28, 79 abstentions) on the Pandora Papers, a massive data leak revealing tax evasion and avoidance by politicians and public officials. The text was tabled by multiple groups, calling for action against secrecy jurisdictions and offshore professional service providers.
The European Parliament adopted by 502 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (502-153) condemning the Polish Constitutional Tribunal's decision challenging EU law primacy, viewing it as a threat to shared values and laws. The resolution was tabled by multiple groups.
The European Parliament adopted by 415 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution (415-220) to align State aid rules for climate, energy, and environmental projects with the EU's sustainability goals, updating the expiring 2014-2020 guidelines. The Commission's draft communication on these updated guidelines was welcomed, aiming for a more environmentally protective state aid system, including decarbonization of the energy sector. Flexibility in rules is emphasized to accommodate technological changes during the transition to a less carbon-intensive model.
The European Parliament adopted by 534 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution on Tunisia's situation by 534 votes to 45, expressing concern over economic stagnation, high COVID-19 deaths, and a presidential decree concentrating power. They called for a restoration of democratic institutions and parliamentary activity.
The European Parliament adopted by 470 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to allow member states, upon Europol's proposal, to enter alerts on third-country nationals involved in serious crime or terrorism into the Schengen Information System. This aims to share information more effectively, particularly on foreign terrorist fighters.
The European Parliament adopted by 480 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to strengthen Europol's role in research and innovation for combating evolving crimes, focusing on transparency, explainability, fairness, and accountability.

The European Parliament adopted by 451 v: The European Parliament approved, with 451 votes in favor and 53 against, an agreement modification between the EU and Australia regarding tariffs, following the International Trade Committee's recommendation. The European Parliament adopted by 597 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (597 votes, 36 nays) to strengthen EU sports policy, focusing on integration and international cooperation. The European Parliament adopted by 659 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to enhance digital oversight of EU fund management, aiming for transparency and updated financial regulations to monitor new mechanisms like Next Generation EU. The European Parliament adopted by 398 v: The European Parliament approved a Directive amendment to phase out time-based tolls and introduce distance-based charging for heavy goods vehicles by 2023, with full implementation by 2027. The European Parliament adopted by 551 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to enhance the EU's post-2020 health and safety at work strategy, aiming for better protection against harmful substances, stress, and repetitive motion injuries. The European Parliament adopted by 552 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (552 votes, 81 against) addressing the need for a unified EU strategy against foreign interference, particularly from Russia and China. The resolution emphasizes concerns over growing attempts at manipulation of information and the weaponization of disinformation.
The European Parliament adopted by 479 v: The European Parliament adopted a resolution supporting the EU Gender Action Plan III (2021-2025) for global gender equality, despite objections from four Member States that hindered formal endorsement due to their opposition to the term 'gender'. The resolution emphasized the need for full implementation of GAP III in all external actions and for gender to be a significant or principal objective in 85% of new programs.
The European Parliament adopted by 357 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (357-119) to strengthen EU citizens' rights, emphasizing the need for a comprehensive assessment and concrete actions over the next three years. The European Parliament adopted by 476 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (476-78) for a fair and simple taxation strategy, supporting measures against tax fraud, evasion, and simplifying tax processes. A harmonized approach to corporate taxation across the EU is also advocated to combat unfair competition.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 642: The European Parliament approved a decision to establish a 38-member special committee investigating lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic and offering future recommendations. The committee will focus on the EU's response in health, democracy, economy, society, and global relations, addressing issues such as crisis preparedness, healthcare provision, digital health advancements, and vaccine strategies.
The European Parliament adopted by 614 v: The European Parliament passed, with majority support, the establishment of a special committee to combat foreign interference and disinformation within the EU, recognizing Russia's ongoing campaign as a serious threat to democratic processes. The committee aims to address gaps in current legislation and policies.
The European Parliament adopted by 482 v: The European Parliament rejected a decision to allow genetically modified cotton GHB811 on the market due to concerns about herbicide residue levels. This vote was passed by 482 votes against 198, with 14 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 635 v: The European Parliament approved a decision to establish a 38-member committee investigating the use of Pegasus and similar spyware, focusing on potential violations of EU rights and freedoms in Hungary, Poland, and other countries. The committee will examine if these tools were misused for political, economic, or unjustified purposes against journalists, politicians, and others.
The European Parliament adopted by 478 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (478-155) to strengthen the Rule of Law Conditionality Regulation, aiming to safeguard the EU budget from breaches of rule-of-law principles. The resolution emphasizes addressing democracy and human rights violations across the Union, including media freedom, migrant rights, women's rights, LGBTIQ rights, and freedom of association. The Court of Justice dismissed challenges by Poland and Hungary against the regulation on February 16, 2022. However, the Commission has yet to apply it.
The European Parliament adopted by 474 v: The European Parliament rejected a decision to allow genetically modified oilseed rape 73496 on the market, citing concerns about increased herbicide residues and metabolites.
The European Parliament adopted by 635 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (635 votes, 2 against, 42 abstentions) condemning Azerbaijan for damaging Armenian cultural heritage in Nagorno-Karabakh. The Parliament urged all states to protect cultural sites and denounced the destruction as part of a wider pattern of Armenophobia.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 625: The European Parliament passed a resolution to integrate Regional Economic Accounts for Agriculture (REAA) into the existing framework, amending Regulation (EC) No 138/2004. This move aims to improve regional statistical data for agriculture policy implementation and evaluation. The new regulation sets deadlines for data transmission.
The European Parliament adopted by 607 v: The European Parliament condemned the violence, human rights violations, and attacks against journalists and human rights defenders in Mexico, particularly the high number of murders going unpunished. They called on authorities to investigate killings promptly, ensure protection, and create a safe environment for journalists.
The European Parliament adopted by 688 v: The European Parliament approved a proposal to establish tax-free shops in the French terminal of the Channel Tunnel, following the UK's withdrawal from the EU, providing comparable facilities for travelers using the link from France to the UK. The proposal was adopted without amendments.
The European Parliament adopted by 646 v: The European Parliament strongly condemned the February 2021 Myanmar coup, calling for an end to violence, respect for election results, and civilian government reinstatement. The resolution was passed with overwhelming support.
The European Parliament adopted by 625 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to establish a unified withholding tax framework, aiming to curb profit shifting practices and reduce tax revenue losses due to corporate avoidance. The Council is urged to swiftly adopt the proposed reforms for implementation in 2023.
The European Parliament adopted by 409 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (409-61, 42 abstentions) to combat oligarch structures and prevent fraud in EU funds for the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) 2021-2027. This package, worth €1800 billion, aims to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic and address long-term priorities across various policy areas. The resolution emphasizes the importance of upholding EU values in managing these funds.
The European Parliament adopted by 584: The European Parliament passed, by 584 votes to 67, amendments to the proposal for a regulation on batteries and waste batteries. The regulation now covers all types of batteries, including those used in electric vehicles, and requires a carbon footprint declaration and labeling. The matter was referred back for further negotiations.
The European Parliament adopted a legisl: The European Parliament approved a vote (536-87) to amend the Value Added Tax (VAT) Directive, allowing Member States more flexibility in applying reduced or zero rates. The amendment sets a maximum of two reduced rates at a minimum of 5%, and permits additional rates below 5% and exemptions with VAT deductibility. Parliament approved the proposal, emphasizing the need for VAT rate convergence while maintaining a standard rate between 15% and 25%.
The European Parliament adopted by 413 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (413-120) urging an immediate EU action plan for food security within and outside the EU, due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The plan aims to address global food vulnerabilities, safeguard rights of developing countries, and support family farming to ensure affordable and accessible food. Additionally, it emphasizes the need to restore stability in Ukraine's agricultural sector.
The European Parliament adopted by 546 v: The European Parliament approved a draft decision to authorize Italy to exchange vehicle registration data, following data protection implementation in national laws. This vote passed with 546 yes votes, 36 no, and 6 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 556 v: The European Parliament approved a decision to mobilize €4,074,296 from the Union budget for workers made redundant in the wholesale trade sector (excluding automobiles and motorbikes) due to COVID-19 impacts on vending machine sales. The funding, representing 85% of total costs, is for France's Selecta company.
The European Parliament adopted by 546 v: The European Parliament approved a draft decision to authorize Greece to exchange vehicle registration data for automated consultations, following data protection implementation in national laws. This was concluded after a Council evaluation report confirmed Greece's compliance with the general data protection provisions of Decision 2008/615/JHA.
The European Parliament adopted by 585 v: The European Parliament approved an agreement with Brazil, allowing visa-free travel for up to 90 days within a 180-day period for EU and Brazilian passport holders. However, Ireland is not participating or bound by this decision due to its non-participation in the Schengen acquis.
The European Parliament adopted by 558 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to provide up to €150 million in macro-financial assistance to Moldova, aimed at economic stabilization and major reforms. The aid is subject to Moldova's adherence to democratic principles, rule of law, human rights, and successful implementation of adjustment and structural reform measures.
The European Parliament adopted by 581 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation aimed at preventing excessive roaming charges within the Union, setting conditions for wholesale access and applying to both wholesale and retail levels. It also aims to increase transparency for users of roaming services.
The European Parliament adopted by 571 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation for establishing an e-Justice Communication via Online Data Exchange (e-CODEX) system, enhancing cross-border data exchange in civil and criminal proceedings. The regulation outlines the system's structure, management, security, and responsibilities of EU agencies, Member States, and authorized access points.
The European Parliament adopted by 527 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation for a DLT pilot scheme to operate market infrastructures, passing with 527 votes, 28 against, and 31 abstentions. This move aims to provide legal certainty for market participants using distributed ledger technology (DLT) by establishing uniform requirements. The pilot regime will test the development of a European infrastructure for trading, clearing, and settling DLT-based financial instruments, including crypto-assets.
The European Parliament adopted by 529 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (529 votes in favor, 49 against) emphasizing the importance of child-friendly justice. Member States were urged to prioritize children's rights and best interests in proceedings affecting their well-being and future living conditions, with an emphasis on giving children the right to be heard and participate in such proceedings. The Commission was invited to develop common guidelines for this purpose.
The European Parliament adopted by 460 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 460-130, advocating for renewed emphasis on citizenship education to bridge knowledge gaps, foster participation, and combat Euroscepticism. They emphasized the need for a common definition, pedagogical renewal, and increased focus on EU and global aspects in national curricula.
The European Parliament adopted by 549 v: The European Parliament approved a decision to extend seed equivalence recognition for Bolivia's sorghum, maize, and sunflower crops until 2029, adopting the Commission's proposal. This move aims to maintain uninterrupted seed imports from Bolivia.
The European Parliament adopted by 587 v: The European Parliament approved an agreement with Brazil, allowing visa-free travel for EU diplomatic and service passport holders and reciprocally for Brazilians. This decision does not apply to Ireland as they did not participate in the adoption.
The European Parliament adopted by 596 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on the Council's position for adjusting the 2021-2027 Multiannual Financial Framework, allowing for the transfer of unspent funds from 2021 to certain programs. Specifically, the draft amending budget aims to redistribute 25% of the unused 2021 commitments for eight funds, as only one fund was fully adopted in 2021.
The European Parliament adopted by 548 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (548-15) to improve nitrate measuring systems and combat water pollution from agriculture and wastewater treatment plants, as current efforts fall short of meeting objectives set by the Water Framework Directive. The Commission is urged to propose ambitious measures in its 2022 integrated nutrient management plan.
The European Parliament adopted by 609 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 609 votes in favor and 12 against, emphasizing the importance of continued cooperation between the EU and UK on fisheries management in the Channel, North Sea, Irish Sea, and Atlantic Ocean post-Brexit. The resolution called for maintaining reciprocal access to waters and resources beyond June 2026, with no further quota reductions for EU fishers.
The European Union adopted by 463 votes: The European Parliament approved a resolution for the 2023 budget, focusing on maintaining recovery and addressing uncertainties due to economic factors and ongoing crises. The budget aims to strengthen the Health Union, promote green and digital transitions, uphold rule of law, create opportunities for youth, and enhance the Union's global standing. Cohesion policy is expected to receive a significant increase in funding as it enters the final year of implementation for the 2014-2020 Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), while also preparing for the start of new programs.
The European Parliament adopted by 420 v: The European Parliament rejected a decision to approve genetically modified soybean MON 87769 × MON 89788 for market use, due to insufficient data on its safety and potential environmental impact. Concerns were raised about increased herbicide usage with this GM crop.
The European Parliament adopted by 337 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution increasing its budget for 2023 by 6.24%, primarily focusing on cybersecurity and safety, with a net decrease of €33.96 million from initial estimates. The budget also anticipates additional spending of €62 million due to the international crisis's impact on inflation and Parliament's resilience.
The European Parliament adopted by 509 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (509 votes, 3 no, 47 abstentions) to protect children and young people fleeing Ukraine's war. The text was proposed by multiple groups, focusing on the increased risk of violence, abuse, and exploitation for unaccompanied children, and emphasizing the need for existing EU strategies and legal instruments to address their specific needs.
The European Parliament adopted by 501 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation on European data governance (Data Governance Act), aiming to increase trust in data sharing and establish common European data spaces. The act facilitates the re-use of certain public sector data, sets rules for data intermediation services, and establishes a European Data Innovation Board. However, it does not obligate public sector bodies to share data or release them from confidentiality obligations under EU or national law.
The European Parliament adopted by 509 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution promoting the right to repair digital devices for a more sustainable Circular Economy. The majority of EU citizens support easier device repairs and prefer fixing over replacing.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution expressing concern over the Taliban's restrictions on women's rights in Afghanistan, particularly denying secondary education to over one million girls and limiting their travel.
The European Parliament adopted by 410 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation on trans-European energy infrastructure, aiming to enhance interconnections, energy security, market integration, and affordable prices while promoting climate neutrality by 2050. The regulation also supports projects related to hydrogen infrastructure and carbon capture and storage.
The European Parliament adopted by 623 v: The European Parliament approved, with minimal opposition, a directive aimed at harmonizing EU rules on seafarer training with international standards set by the International Maritime Organization (IMO). The adopted proposal aligns with revisions made in 2010, 2015, and 2016 to the STCW Convention, ensuring consistent implementation of international commitments.
The European Parliament adopted amendmen: The European Parliament approved amendments to maintain the current parameters of the market stability reserve within the EU Emissions Trading Scheme until 2030. This aims to prevent a surplus of allowances and ensure market predictability, crucial for meeting climate targets. Changes were made to emphasize the importance of the reserve rate not falling below 24% and the minimum number of allowances not dropping below 200 million.
The European Parliament adopted by 427 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to strengthen the Schengen evaluation and control mechanism, focusing on all aspects of the Schengen acquis and fundamental rights. The decision was made by 427 votes in favor, 102 against, with 24 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution condemning Russia's escalating repression, particularly against Alexei Navalny and anti-war protesters. The resolution calls for Navalny's immediate release, along with hundreds of other detained Russians, and urges the EU to use global human rights sanctions against Russia.
The European Parliament adopted by 513 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (513-22) emphasizing the human toll of Russia's war against Ukraine, including displacement and loss of life. The resolution also highlighted ongoing energy dependence on Russia, with EU fossil fuel purchases still funding the conflict. Academic studies suggest that banning these imports could have minimal impact on EU economic growth.
The European Parliament to grant dischar: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Director of the Fusion Energy Joint Undertaking for their 2020 budget implementation and accounts closure. The ITER Council's decision to maintain its baseline plan with First Plasma set in December 2025 was noted despite forecasted delays.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the Translation Centre's financial year 2020 accounts and granted discharge to its Director. The Court of Auditors confirmed the reliability and legality of the transactions.

The resolution requires member states to establish gender-neutral job evaluation systems and encourages pay transparency before employment.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of CEPOL for financial year 2020, endorsing the agency's reliable annual accounts and legal transactions. The European Parliament approved the discharge of the European Agency for Safety and Health at Work's Interim Executive Director, following assurance from the Court of Auditors that the agency's 2020 financial statements are reliable. The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of the European Fisheries Control Agency for 2020, endorsing the closure of their accounts for that year. The decision was based on the Court of Auditors' assurance that the agency's financial statements were reliable and legal.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of the European Environment Agency for the financial year 2020, endorsing the closure of accounts for that period. The decision was based on the Court of Auditors' assurance that the agency's financial statements were reliable and legal.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) for financial year 2019, endorsing their annual accounts. Parliament made recommendations on performance, financial management, and control of EU agencies.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the European Agency for Large-scale IT Systems (eu-LISA) for the financial year 2020, and endorsed its annual accounts. Despite a budget implementation rate below target, concerns about carry-overs were noted due to underlying structural issues.
The European Parliament decided by 636 v: The European Parliament approved the discharge for the EMCDDA's financial year 2020, with a budget decrease of 0.71%. Other observations were made regarding performance, staff, procurement, and Covid-19 response.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of CEDEFOP for the 2020 budget implementation and account closure, with a majority vote of 542 to 74, following assurances from the Court of Auditors about the reliability and legality of the annual accounts. Recommendations were made on the Centre's financial statements, budget management, and other areas including performance, staff policy, internal control, and Covid-19 response.
The European Parliament adopted by 568 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (568 votes for, 21 against, 43 abstentions) to promote an EU strategy for children's education during the COVID-19 pandemic. The strategy aims to mitigate the impact of school closures on over 168 million children who have lost a year of education due to lockdowns. The EU is urged to adopt a child rights-based approach, prioritize non-discrimination, and encourage global efforts in ensuring access to education for all children.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge for the Innovative Health Initiative Joint Undertaking's 2020 budget and closed its accounts, with a majority vote of 572 to 37. The Court of Auditors confirmed the accuracy of the Joint Undertaking's 2020 financial situation and operations.
The European Parliament adopted by 611 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to boost organic farming, aiming to increase EU agricultural land under organic production by 2030. The resolution emphasizes the role of organic farming in climate change mitigation, biodiversity, and soil protection, contributing to sustainable food systems. Parliament also called for flexible legislation to accommodate differences among Member States.
The European Parliament adopted by 542 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to promote women's economic independence through entrepreneurship and self-employment. The resolution aims to increase the number of women entrepreneurs and CEOs, strengthen networks for women's entrepreneurship, and implement programs to encourage innovation and creativity among women.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of Europe's Rail Joint Undertaking for the 2020 budget implementation and closed its accounts, with 557 votes in favor, 47 against, and 35 abstentions. In 2020, cooperation with Member States and international parties increased.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Key Digital Technologies Joint Undertaking for their 2020 budget implementation and closed their accounts. The Court of Auditors confirmed the accuracy of the Joint Undertaking's 2020 financial situation and operations.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Single European Sky ATM Research 3 Joint Undertaking for the financial year 2020 and closed its accounts, with a majority vote of 547 to 84. This decision followed the Court of Auditors' confirmation that the accounts presented an accurate financial situation and results for the year.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Clean Hydrogen Joint Undertaking's Executive Director for the 2020 budget implementation and closed its accounts. The decision was passed by 574 votes to 22 with 40 abstentions, following a positive audit report from the Court of Auditors.

The European Parliament approved the Director of ACER's discharge for the financial year 2020 and endorsed the closure of accounts, following assurance from the Court of Auditors that the annual accounts are reliable. The European Parliament approved the discharge for the European Banking Authority's financial year 2020, endorsing reliable annual accounts. The Authority's budget increased by 3.06% compared to 2019, with a high implementation rate of 99.17%. The UK premises were successfully closed in December 2020.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) for the financial year 2020, endorsing their reliable annual accounts. The vote was 558 in favor, 50 against, with 35 abstentions. The Authority's budget for 2020 was €56,246,722, primarily funded by Union funds, Member States' supervisory authorities, and fees from supervised entities.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to ENISA's Executive Director for the implementation of the agency's budget for 2020 and the closure of accounts for that year. The decision was passed with 560 votes in favor, 47 against, and 34 abstentions. The Parliament adopted a resolution containing recommendations to improve ENISA's financial management and control.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority's financial year 2020, with a resolution containing recommendations for improved performance and financial management. The Authority's budget for 2020 was €28,386,398, primarily funded by the Union (36.59%) and national supervisory authorities of Member States (61.63%).

The European Parliament approved the discharge for the Executive Director of the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA) for the financial year 2020, endorsing their reliable annual accounts. The resolution included recommendations on budgetary management and performance, with a slight decrease in budget implementation and payment appropriations execution rates compared to 2019. Parliament also made observations regarding staff policy, conflicts of interest, and Covid-19 impacts on planned activities.

The European Parliament approved the discharge for the Executive Director of the European Space Programme Agency's financial year 2020, with a budget of €35.4 million, following assurance from the Court of Auditors that the accounts are reliable and legal.

The European Parliament approved the discharge for the Executive Director of the European Union Agency for Railways, allowing the closure of accounts for the year 2020. The budget for this year was EUR 30,764,883, with a high implementation rate of 99.98%. Despite having the smallest budget among transport agencies, concerns about funding persist due to its exceptional environmental and climate performance in rail transport.

The European Parliament approved the discharge for the Euratom Supply Agency's financial year 2020, and endorsed its reliable annual accounts. The Agency's final budget for 2020 was €230,000, with a commitment appropriations implementation rate of 99.54% and a payment execution rate of 22.33%.

The European Parliament approved the Agency for Support for BEREC's financial statements for the 2020 fiscal year, granting discharge to its Director. The decision was supported by 561 votes, with 71 votes against and 10 abstentions. The budget increased by 27.96% compared to 2019, primarily due to higher staff and operational expenses.
The European Parliament adopted by 495 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 495 votes in favor, aiming to establish the EU as a global leader in AI development. Recognizing the economic potential of AI by 2030 and the need for human-centered, trustworthy, and sustainable standards, they emphasized the urgency for a unified European approach to AI regulation.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge of the European Aviation Safety Agency's Director for financial year 2020, following assurance from the Court of Auditors about the reliability of the agency's accounts. The agency's budget decreased by 6.81% compared to 2019, with a significant reduction in revenue due to the Covid-19 crisis. Budget implementation and payment appropriations execution rates increased during the year.
The European Parliament adopted by 494 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution for a comprehensive approach to the EU Blue Economy, advocating for a broad definition that includes fisheries and aquaculture. They emphasized the need for an integrated strategy, financial support, and potential partnerships in maritime transport.
The European Parliament decided by 589 v: The European Parliament approved, by a large majority, the budget for the European Data Protection Supervisor for 2020, with no significant issues found by the Court of Auditors. The budget increased due to new tasks under the General Data Protection Regulation and supervisory responsibilities for enforcement agencies like the European Prosecutor's Office and Eurojust. However, the COVID-19 pandemic affected budget implementation.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge of its President for the 2020 budget implementation. The resolution, passed by a majority, highlighted the successful management of parliamentary finances, with 95.7% of appropriations committed and a high level of budget implementation achieved.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Court of Auditors' Secretary-General for the 2020 budget implementation. Despite growth in the budget to €152 million, the Parliament requested simplification and detailed explanations on implementing recommendations in future reports. The resolution also noted increased costs for IT, medical service, and security due to COVID-19.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Circular Bio-based Europe Joint Undertaking Director for the 2020 budget implementation and closed their accounts, with a majority vote of 569 to 67. This decision was based on the Court of Auditors' opinion that the annual accounts presented an accurate financial situation and results for the same year.
The European Parliament decided by 429 v: The European Parliament postponed a decision on discharging the Secretary General of the Economic and Social Committee's 2020 budget, passing with 429 votes to 158, due to budget management issues affected by the pandemic.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the financial statements of Eurofound for 2020, granting discharge with 544 votes in favor, 78 against, and 8 abstentions. The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Clean Aviation Joint Undertaking's budget for 2020 and closed its accounts. The vote passed with 572 in favor, 53 against, and 14 abstentions. The Court of Auditors confirmed the accuracy of the Joint Undertaking's financial situation and operations for the year 2020.

The European Parliament approved the discharge of the European Medicines Agency's financial year 2020 accounts, with a majority vote. The decision includes recommendations to enhance the agency's performance and financial management. Notably, the agency waived fees for COVID-19 therapeutics and vaccine developers since March 2020.
The European Parliament decided by 612 v: The European Parliament approved, by a large margin, the discharge of the European Ombudsman's budget for 2020, acknowledging no significant issues found by the Court of Auditors. The Ombudsman's budget increased in 2020 despite COVID-19 challenges, with a reduction in carried-over appropriations.
The European Parliament decided by 555 v: The European Parliament approved, by a majority of 555 votes to 83, the discharge of the High Representative for the implementation of the European External Action Service (EEAS) budget for 2020. No significant weaknesses were found in the EEAS's human resources and procurement during an audit, and payments were deemed free from material error. The EEAS budget for 2020 was €731 million, with 95% of funds committed and 79% paid out.
The European Parliament decided by 548 v: The European Parliament approved, by a majority of 573 votes to 45 with abstentions, the budget implementation of the Court of Justice of the EU for 2020, totaling €436.6 million. The Court was found to have managed human resources and public procurement effectively, with no significant issues identified.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Executive Director of the European Asylum Support Office, ending a four-year streak of budget concerns. The decision includes recommendations for the Office's financial management and control, with a final budget of €130,986,611 for 2020.
The European Parliament adopted by 506 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation amendment aimed at aligning with international obligations on persistent organic pollutants. The proposal now returns to inter-institutional negotiations, focusing on clarifying concentration limits underpinned by the precautionary principle and aiming for a toxic-free environment.
The European Parliament decided by 555 v: The European Parliament postponed its decision on discharging funds to the Council for the 2020 budget due to lack of cooperation and undermining democratic control, with 555 votes in favor, 60 against, and 13 abstentions. Parliament called on the Council to resume negotiations promptly to reach an agreement within the discharge procedure framework.
The European Parliament decided by 558 v: The European Parliament approved, by 558 votes to 42, the discharge of the Secretary General of the Committee of the Regions for the implementation of their 2020 budget, following a clean audit report on human resources and public procurement. The Parliament's resolution also highlighted the need for better management of uncommitted appropriations due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The European Parliament adopted by 436 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution on Competition policy for 2021, emphasizing the need to consider COVID-19 challenges and phase out support measures progressively. The goal is to prevent an asymmetric recovery and reduce EU dependence on global supply chains, particularly in strategic sectors. The resolution calls for a robust competition policy to aid economic recovery and promote a green and digital transition in a sustainable and inclusive manner. It also highlights the importance of addressing SME financing issues, removing barriers in service development, and reviewing existing competition instruments, with a focus on digital market investigations.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Director of the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, allowing the closure of accounts for the 2020 financial year. The decision includes recommendations on budgetary management and other areas, such as performance, staff policy, public procurement, conflicts of interest, internal control, and Covid-19 response.

The European Parliament approved the discharge for the Executive Director of the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking, allowing the closure of its accounts for 2020, following a positive audit report. This decision was made with 554 votes in favor, 18 against, and 62 abstentions. The Parliament also adopted a resolution containing observations regarding the Joint Undertaking's operations.
The European Parliament adopted by 403 v: The European Parliament approved a proposal to allow the Council to set the date for applying Schengen Information System provisions to Cyprus, enabling data transfer and verification of correct application. Restrictions on use will remain until full Schengen acquis application and border checks are lifted in Cyprus.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the Institute of Innovation and Technology's financial statements for 2020, granting discharge and closing accounts. The budget increased by 12.04% compared to 2019, with a high implementation rate of 99.85%.
The European Parliament adopted by 496 t: The European Parliament passed a resolution (496-28, 113 abstentions) condemning global persecution of religious and belief minorities.
