It affirmed commitment to protect their rights, including freedom of religion, and strongly denounced violence against any minority based on belief.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved Europol's financial statements for 2020, granting discharge and closing accounts. Despite a late payment rate of 33%, the Court of Auditors found the annual accounts reliable and legal.
The European Parliament adopted by 605 v: The European Parliament approved a proposal to extend until December 31, 2025, the use of anti-fraud measures in value-added tax (VAT) for certain susceptible goods and services, without amendments. This was passed with a large majority, and aims to combat existing fraud via the reverse charge mechanism.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the financial discharge for the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) for the year 2020, acknowledging the reliability of their annual accounts. The resolution included recommendations for improved budgetary management, with a decrease in the total budget from €109,362,158 in 2020 compared to 2019.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament approved a resolution advocating for a more active EU role in addressing climate change, biodiversity protection, and sustainability. They also emphasized the need for increased cooperation between national parliaments and the EU, as well as continued citizen participation in decision-making processes. The resolution also highlighted the necessity of a stronger geopolitical Union, particularly in response to global issues like the Russian aggression against Ukraine.
The European Parliament adopted by 499 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on EU agency budget discharge for 2020, passing with 499 votes in favor, 67 against, and 5 abstentions. The resolution commends agencies' resilience amid COVID-19, recognizing their crucial role in EU policy implementation, including infection control, vaccine authorization, and guidelines on remote work. Despite low risks to regularity and budget management identified by the Court of Auditors, challenges related to COVID-19 were acknowledged.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved discharge to the Commission for implementing the budget of the 8th-11th European Development Funds (EDF) in 2020. The vote was 546 to 79, with 11 abstentions. The Parliament acknowledged surpassed commitments and payments due to COVID-19 response efforts, appreciated efforts to reduce old pre-financing and old unspent commitments, and welcomed the closure of the 8th EDF and the Commission's intention to close the 9th EDF soon. Members also confirmed the reliability of accounts and transactions.

The European Parliament approved Eurojust's financial statements for 2020, granting discharge and closing the accounts. The Court of Auditors confirmed the reliability and legality of the transactions. The budget increased by 7.05% compared to 2019, with a budget implementation rate of 99.99%. Parliament made observations on performance, staff policy, procurement, internal controls, and Covid-19.

The European Parliament approved the discharge to the Director of the European Institute for Gender Equality (EIGE) for the financial year 2020, endorsing their reliable annual accounts. Despite a decrease in budget implementation and payment appropriations execution rates, the resolution was passed with recommendations on performance, financial management, and control of EU agencies.
The European Parliament adopted by 526 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, by 526 votes to 5 with 63 abstentions, condemning the ongoing suppression of political opposition in Cambodia. The resolution criticizes the government's crackdown on opposition members, independent media, and civil society organizations since 2017, leading many into exile due to fear of arrest or retaliation. The resolution was tabled by multiple groups, including the EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens/EFA, expressing concern over the deteriorating human rights situation ahead of Cambodia's upcoming elections in 2022 and 2023.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge of the European Training Foundation's financial year 2020 accounts, with a vote of 550 to 54, and granted recommendations for improved transparency and accountability. The Foundation's budget for 2020 was €20,957,000, with a high implementation rate of 99.88%.

The European Parliament approved the implementation of the EU general budget for 2020 and closed the accounts for the same year. The budget was emphasized as a crucial tool for achieving political priorities, particularly during crises like COVID-19. Members also stressed the importance of implementing rule of law conditionality to prevent budget losses in certain Member States.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution, condemning Russian attacks on Ukraine's transport infrastructure and calling for further sanctions in the transport sector against Russia. They also welcomed various initiatives offering free transportation for Ukrainian citizens and humanitarian aid.
The European Parliament decided to grant: The European Parliament approved the discharge of the Executive Director of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency for the 2020 budget, following assurances from the Court of Auditors about the reliability and legality of the financial statements. The final budget was €364 million, with a commitment rate of 98.9% but a low payment execution rate of 43.8%.
The European Parliament adopted by 426 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 426 votes in favor and 133 against, expressing concern over the deteriorating rule of law, democracy, and fundamental rights in Poland and Hungary. The Council was urged to make progress in ongoing procedures and swiftly implement concrete recommendations. The Parliament also requested regular updates from the Council during each presidency.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution condemning threats to stability, security, and democracy in Western and Sahelian Africa. The resolution addresses escalating violence, terrorism, and instability in the region, particularly due to the proliferation of small arms and the presence of groups like Boko Haram and ISWAP.
The European Parliament adopted by 462 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, by 462 votes to 19 with 89 abstentions, addressing the impact of the Ukraine-Russia conflict on women. The resolution focuses on the plight of approximately 5 million refugees, primarily women and children, who have fled to the EU, as well as internally displaced women and children in need of aid within Ukraine. Additionally, it acknowledges the efforts of Ukrainian women involved in combat and support roles during the conflict. The resolution also emphasizes the urgent need for sexual and reproductive health care access for both women still in Ukraine and those seeking refuge in the EU, particularly in Poland.
The European Parliament adopted by 454 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to extend the EU Digital COVID Certificate for third-country nationals, facilitating their movement during the pandemic. The vote passed with 454 in favor, 112 against, and 20 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution condemning persistent organ harvesting in China, particularly from Falun Gong practitioners and other minorities like Uyghurs, Tibetans, and Christians. The resolution expressed serious concerns about state-sanctioned practices.
The European Parliament resolution on th: The European Parliament strongly condemns the life sentence given to Osman Kavala, a human rights defender in Turkey, and demands his immediate release, as per a 2019 ruling by the European Court of Human Rights. Concerns about government interference in the judicial process persist.
The European Parliament adopted by 453 v: The European Parliament approved an extension of the EU Digital COVID Certificate scheme until June 2023, allowing for recovery certificates following positive test results. The extension was passed with 453 votes in favor, 119 against, and 19 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution calling for increased aid to Moldova, recognizing the financial burden of hosting Ukrainian refugees and the economic challenges due to COVID-19 and gas price hikes. The Commission is urged to provide grants, humanitarian assistance, border management support, and relocation aid to Moldova.
The European Parliament adopted by 519 v: The European Parliament urged the Council to swiftly initiate EU accession talks with Albania and North Macedonia, emphasizing the need for Albania to focus on rule of law reforms, judicial system consolidation, democracy strengthening, anti-corruption measures, media freedom, minority rights, and civil society empowerment.
The European Parliament adopted by 627 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation aimed at investigating foreign subsidies distorting the internal market, with key amendments clarifying the threshold for such subsidies (€4 million over three years) and allowing consideration of equivalent control systems in third countries. The Commission is required to publish guidelines within two years.
The European Parliament adopted by 368 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 368 votes in favor, supporting North Macedonia's commitment to democracy and EU integration. Members urged accelerated accession negotiations for Albania and North Macedonia, particularly amid geopolitical tensions with Russia. Bilateral issues between Bulgaria and North Macedonia were highlighted for swift resolution to avoid delays in accession progress. The Parliament also commended North Macedonia's efforts towards rule of law, minority rights, and media freedom, encouraging continued intensification.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament approved a resolution to establish the European Education Area by 2025, focusing on micro-credentials, individual learning accounts, and environmental sustainability education. This move aims to provide flexible learning opportunities and strengthen higher education and vocational institutions' role in lifelong learning.
The European Parliament adopted by 512 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, with 512 votes in favor, 43 against, and 39 abstentions, supporting Moldova's EU membership application. They urged the EU to grant candidate status to Moldova, alongside Ukraine and Georgia, and called for intensified dialogue and support to accelerate integration into the EU single market. The Commission was also asked to help develop a pre-accession strategy and assess reform progress using the same methodology as for Western Balkan countries. Parliament welcomed Moldova's new economic reform program approved by the IMF.
The European Parliament adopted by 429 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on the 2021 Rule of Law Report, calling for the Commission to address additional rule of law elements and clarify its assessment indicators. The report was criticized for failing to acknowledge deliberate backsliding in countries under Article 7(1) TEU procedures, notably Poland and Hungary.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution condemning war crimes in Ukraine, demanding an end to Russia's aggression and withdrawal of forces. Reports detail indiscriminate attacks against civilians, including summary executions, torture, rape, and use of banned weapons.
The European Parliament adopted by 503 v: The European Parliament passed, with 503 votes in favor and 46 against, a Directive aimed at establishing a minimum corporate tax rate of 15% for multinational groups operating within the EU. This Directive transposes the OECD and G20's December 2021 international tax reform into EU law. The Directive applies to large groups with combined annual revenues exceeding €750 million, and Parliament approved the main elements of the Commission's proposal, including the proposed timetable and implementation deadline of December 31, 2022. Some changes were made to the Commission's proposal, such as clarifying that a constituent entity is considered resident in the jurisdiction where it is tax-resident based on specific criteria.
The European Parliament adopted by 356 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 356 votes in favor, 159 against, and 114 abstentions, to accelerate military capability development and make technology independent from fossil fuels, addressing both security threats from Russia's aggression against Ukraine and climate change. The aim is to contribute to the Union's carbon neutrality targets without compromising mission security or operational capabilities of the armed forces.
The European Parliament adopted by 448 v: The European Parliament expressed concern over Turkey's rule of law and fundamental rights issues, reiterating that progress is necessary for resumed accession negotiations, which have been halted since 2018. The Parliament emphasized the strategic importance of Turkey and called for action to match recent commitments to EU membership.
The European Parliament adopted by 490 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 490 votes in favor, 59 against, and 38 abstentions, to strengthen security in the Eastern Partnership area. The resolution calls for an end to Russia's aggression against Ukraine, withdrawal of troops from occupied territories, and closer defense cooperation with some Eastern Partnership countries.
The European Parliament adopted by 515 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 515 votes in favor, to expedite economic ties with Ukraine, temporarily waiving customs and import duties on Ukrainian goods, aiming to alleviate economic hardships caused by Russia's aggression.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution strengthening the EU's response to the economic and social impacts of the Russian war in Ukraine, emphasizing the need for increased union solidarity.
The European Parliament adopted by 577 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (577 votes for, 38 against, 10 abstentions) addressing challenges faced by EU islands due to their unique characteristics, such as small size, remote location, and vulnerability to climate change. The resolution emphasizes the need for integration strategies to overcome these obstacles in areas like labor market, transport, economy, education, energy supply, and waste management.
The European Parliament adopted by 532 v: The European Parliament approved a new sustainable fisheries partnership agreement with Mauritania, enhancing cooperation for sustainable fishing and combating illegal activities. The agreement offers significant opportunities for the EU fleet and establishes a framework for collaboration.
The European Parliament adopted by 438 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 438 votes in favor, 65 against, and 94 abstentions, supporting Ukraine's territorial integrity and providing assistance post-conflict. Recommendations include confiscating frozen Russian assets for Ukraine's reconstruction, strengthening defense cooperation, and intensifying collaboration with NATO allies to uphold the rules-based international order. The EU aims to establish strategic autonomy as a guiding principle in foreign, security, and defense policy.
The European Parliament adopted by 557 v: The European Parliament approved an agreement with Mauritania, allowing EU vessels from France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, and Spain to fish in Mauritanian waters in exchange for €57.5 million annually. The agreement lasts six years and can be renewed tacitly. A new protocol is also valid for five years with an EU financial contribution of €16.5 million. The parties may renegotiate the terms from the third year, and a new management plan for small pelagic species is required for part of the EU's funding.
The European Parliament adopted by 482 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 482-103, urging Member States to use transparent and objective criteria when allocating fishing opportunities under the Common Fisheries Policy (CFP). The resolution emphasizes the need for transparency in these criteria and encourages infringement proceedings against non-compliant states.
The European Parliament adopted by 420 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to establish its right of initiative for direct legislation, lamenting the lack of progress in special legislative procedures. Members condemned the Council's inaction on rule-of-law safeguards and called for immediate negotiations on an interinstitutional agreement. Additionally, they expressed concern over three Member States yet to ratify the amended EU electoral law.
The European Parliament adopted by 556 v: The European Parliament approved, by a large majority, an extension of the agreement on Galileo and GPS satellite navigation systems cooperation between the EU and the US, aiming to enhance civilian, commercial, and scientific uses.
The European Parliament adopted by 547 v: The European Parliament approved changes to EU aviation rules under the Emissions Trading System, implementing the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA). The amendments reference the Paris Agreement and COP26 resolutions, aiming to address slow progress in reducing international aviation emissions.
The European Parliament adopted by 474 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to strengthen EU presence and influence in the Indo-Pacific region, focusing on strategic ties and security cooperation with like-minded countries. The resolution also emphasized the need for consolidated international commitments due to Russia's aggression against Ukraine.
The European Parliament adopted by 524 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 524 votes in favor and 17 against, condemning the repressive actions by Nicaragua's Ortega-Murillo regime against political opponents, human rights defenders, media, and journalists. The resolution calls out the regime for violating international human rights obligations and undermining democracy.
The European Parliament adopted by 503,: The European Parliament passed a resolution to ban products made by forced labor, aiming to combat this issue in global supply chains. The EU also emphasized the need for dialogue, technical assistance, capacity building, and awareness-raising with non-EU countries.
The European Parliament adopted by 355 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution calling for a Convention to revise EU Treaties, aiming to enhance decision-making processes, adapt powers in health, energy, defense, and social/economic policies, and reform voting procedures for sanctions and emergencies. The vote was 355-154 with 48 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution condemning the systematic oppression of the Uyghur community in Xinjiang, including evidence of crimes against humanity and potential genocide. They called on China to halt forced labor, mass sterilization, family separations, and birth prevention measures.
The European Parliament adopted by 364 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (364-154) expressing concern over potential US Supreme Court actions that could restrict abortion rights. The text was proposed by multiple groups, including EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens/EFA, and others. The resolution highlights the importance of abortion as essential healthcare and the high number of unsafe abortions in developing countries.
The European Parliament adopted by 411 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 411 votes in favor and 129 against, urging the Commission and Council to delay approval of Poland's recovery plan due to concerns over rule of law violations and non-compliance with EU court judgments.
The European Parliament adopted by 437 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation to set binding annual greenhouse gas emission reductions for Member States from 2021 to 2030, aiming to meet commitments under the Paris Agreement. The amended regulation sets annual emissions allowances for the period 2023-2030 and changes the linear trajectory definition, differing from the initial plan to readjust them in 2025.
The European Parliament adopted by 506 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 506 votes in favor and 50 against, expressing concern over political tensions and slow progress on EU reforms in Montenegro, particularly judicial reform and the need for inclusive dialogue. They also called for improved coordination between executive and legislative powers to advance EU accession efforts.
The European Parliament adopted by 339 v: The European Parliament approved stricter CO2 emission standards for new cars and vans to reach zero emissions by 2035 as part of the 'Fit for 55' package. By 2030, emissions from new passenger cars should be 55% lower, and from new vans, 50% lower. The Commission is also tasked with proposing targeted funding to ensure a just transition in the automotive sector by December 2023.
The European Parliament adopted by 479 v: The European Parliament approved, with 479 votes in favor, 130 against, and 32 abstentions, amendments to extend the EU Emissions Trading Scheme (EU ETS) to aviation emissions, including those from flights to non-EEA countries. This is part of the 'Fit for 55 in 2030 package' aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030. The amendments also include a derogation for certain regional flights within the EU.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen EU-Africa trade relations, emphasizing the need for a more equitable partnership beyond traditional donor-recipient dynamics. Key focuses include developing Africa's industrial base, protecting infant industries, and prioritizing environmental protection in cooperation policies. A new basis for partnership is envisioned, centered on equality, mutual respect, and understanding.
The European Parliament adopted by 436 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (436-69) to further modernize and strengthen the EU's international investment policy, emphasizing its role in promoting sustainable economic growth, job creation, and development aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals.
The European Parliament adopted by 413 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen the EU's greenhouse gas emission trading system, aiming for a 62% reduction in emissions by 2030 compared to 2005 levels. The reform includes maritime shipping emissions within the system.
The European Parliament adopted by 519 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to renew the scientific and technological cooperation agreement with Brazil for five years, aiming to strengthen partnerships and address shared societal challenges.
The European Parliament adopted by 472 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation aimed at strengthening climate neutrality targets, focusing on land use, forestry, and agriculture sectors by 2035. The proposal is part of the 'Fit for 55 in 2030 package', an EU plan to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55%. Parliament supports increasing the CO2 emission reduction target for land use, land-use change, and forestry (LULUCF) sector by 2030. The target will be enhanced further through additional measures and initiatives at EU and Member State levels to support carbon storage in agricultural soils.
The European Parliament adopted by 576 v: The European Parliament approved, with minor exceptions, the EU's accession to the Convention on Foreign Judgments Enforcement, aimed at simplifying cross-border litigation and promoting global justice. This convention applies to civil and commercial matters, excluding revenue, customs, or administrative issues.
The European Parliament adopted by 420 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to support the implementation of the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), the EU's main pandemic response tool, by 420 votes to 90. The RRF is crucial for economic growth as it contributes to recovery and resilience, employment, productivity, and more within the EU. Parliament emphasized the importance of effective implementation and timely reforms for the RRF grants to provide continued budgetary support to Member States.
The European Parliament adopted by 402 v: The European Parliament rejected a decision to approve genetically modified maize NK603 × T25 × DAS-40278-9 for market placement, citing concerns over herbicide residues and potential health risks associated with glyphosate exposure.
The European Parliament\nadopted by 479: The European Parliament passed, by a significant margin, amendments to establish a Social Climate Fund for addressing the social impacts of ETS expansion on vulnerable households from 2025-2032. The amendments focus on benefiting energy and mobility poverty-stricken citizens, particularly those in rural, remote, or less developed areas. A definition for 'mobility poverty' was also introduced.
The European Parliament adopted by 576 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to provide €400 million from the EU budget to support refugees fleeing Ukraine, following Russia's invasion. The vote passed with 576 in favor, 3 against, and 13 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 564 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to mobilize €17.7 million from the European Globalisation Adjustment Fund (EGF) for displaced workers in France's air transport sector, following an application by Air France. The contribution represents 85% of the total cost.

The European Parliament approved a decision to mobilize €1.49 million from the European Globalisation Adjustment Fund (EGF) to support displaced workers in Greece's electrical equipment manufacturing sector, following an application from Attica. This contribution covers 85% of the total cost, with the remaining funds allocated for personalized services and EGF implementation.
The European Parliament adopted by 450 v: The European Parliament approved a carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM) expansion, covering organic chemicals, plastics, hydrogen, ammonia, and indirect emissions. The CBAM is set to commence from 2023, with free allowances in the EU ETS phased out by 2032.
The European Parliament adopted by 471 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to enhance inclusivity in Erasmus+ (2014-2020), emphasizing equal opportunities for all participants. Despite the lack of a harmonized inclusion strategy, the resolution calls for improvements to address existing education inequalities and align with green and digital transitions.
The European Parliament adopted by 398 v: The European Parliament rejected, by a majority of 398 votes to 173, a decision to approve genetically modified maize DP4114 × MON 810 × MIR604 × NK603 for market placement. This rejection was due to concerns about increased glyphosate exposure and potential carcinogenic risks associated with the maize.
The European Parliament adopted the reso: The European Parliament passed a resolution aiming to combat illegal logging within the EU, urging Member States to enforce stricter controls on timber used by companies and calling for an expansion of the EU Timber Regulation. Additionally, the Commission was asked to lead global efforts against illegal logging, standardize definitions, and utilize technology for compliance.
The European Parliament adopted by 470 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 470 votes in favor and 56 against, reaffirming commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). They emphasized the need for a 'whole-of-government' approach, leadership at the highest level, and stakeholder engagement to achieve SDGs. The resolution also called for more coordinated EU action globally, with SDGs serving as the foundation for European policy.
The European Parliament adopted by 529 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (529-45) supporting Ukraine, Moldova, and Georgia's EU candidacy amid Russia's aggression. Accession will follow established procedures and criteria, including democratic reforms and market economy implementation. Georgia's candidate status is pending government action on priority areas.
The European Parliament adopted by 469 v: The European Parliament approved, with 469 votes in favor and 96 against, a resolution endorsing Kosovo's commitment to EU-related reforms and its intention to apply for EU membership in 2022. The parliament also urged swift implementation of a visa-free regime for Kosovo citizens and emphasized the importance of normalizing relations with Serbia for both countries' progress towards the EU.
The European Parliament adopted by 437 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on combating fraud and protecting the EU's financial interests in 2020, emphasizing the need for increased control over emergency expenditure due to COVID-19 risks. With an unprecedented EUR 1.8 trillion in funds allocated under the new Multiannual Financial Framework and NextGenerationEU recovery plan, Parliament stressed the importance of preventing fraudulent irregularities totaling approximately EUR 1.46 billion in 2020.
The European Parliament adopted by 454 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (454-73) to strengthen the EU's commitment to multilateralism, emphasizing the need for autonomous instruments to act as a global actor and preserve multilateralism amidst global forces like fragmentation and protectionism. A European Diplomatic Academy was also proposed. The EU is encouraged to continue defending multilateralism while addressing challenges such as climate change and promoting stability.
The European Parliament adopted by 607 v: The European Parliament approved a recommendation (607-13, 11 abstentions) for EU-INTERPOL cooperation agreement negotiations. The aim is to strengthen EU response to global terrorism and organized crime by enhancing data access and operational cooperation with INTERPOL, while ensuring compliance with EU data protection principles and fundamental rights.
The European Parliament adopted by 523 v: The European Parliament endorsed a resolution supporting Serbia's future EU membership, emphasizing the need for sustained reforms in rule of law, human rights, and alignment with EU foreign policy. They welcomed increased voter turnout in recent elections but condemned political tensions and attacks on opposition, journalists, and civil society. The Parliament urged the new government to respect previous decisions and accelerate Serbia's alignment with European policies.
The European Parliament adopted by 458 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, supported by 458 votes and opposed by 51, emphasizing the EU's strategy for sustainable and fair trade in the Indo-Pacific region. The focus is on inclusiveness, cooperation, and respect for democracy, human rights, and rule of law. The EU aims to establish a multilateral approach based on open trade environments, level playing fields, reciprocity, and mutual benefit. The resolution also highlights the importance of maintaining a free Indo-Pacific, preserving maritime supply routes, and strengthening partnerships with relevant actors in the region.
The European Parliament adopted by 482 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to strengthen EU-India trade ties, aiming for a deeper partnership based on shared values and mutual benefits. Both sides are encouraged to work towards comprehensive, value-based agreements in trade, investment protection, and geographical indications.
The European Parliament adopted by 501 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 501 votes in favor and 47 against, focusing on mental health in the digital work environment post-COVID-19. The resolution calls for increased attention to work-related mental health issues, the development of a supportive digital working environment, and stronger social protection rights at work. An EU strategy is proposed to integrate mental and physical health, provide effective care, increase access to treatment, and support employment.
The European Parliament adopted by 436 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution for a comprehensive European care strategy, focusing on quality care, choice, and accessibility throughout life, particularly in remote areas. The strategy should be data-driven, ambitious, and address the needs of both care recipients and carers across the lifespan.
The European Parliament adopted by 492 v: European Parliament approves resolution on EIB's financial operations, emphasizing a focus on less developed regions and sustainable development goals. The EIB's loan signatures in 2020 totaled €66.1 billion, with significant investments in Italy, Spain, France, and sectors like transport, global loans, and energy. The COVID-19 pandemic influenced disbursement patterns, with over half of the target reached by mid-year. The EIB's role as a leading issuer of green and social bonds was acknowledged, along with a good loan portfolio performance.
The European Parliament adopted by 493 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to strengthen EU and national actions for the development of the social economy, aiming to foster social entrepreneurship, create quality jobs, and integrate it into green and digital transitions. Member States are encouraged to support social innovation programs for vulnerable groups.
The European Parliament adopted by 535 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution aimed at combating women's poverty in Europe, calling for an ambitious EU anti-poverty strategy by 2030 with a focus on ending women's poverty and addressing labor market barriers. Additionally, efforts were emphasized to eradicate precarious work and improve the situation of women in the labor market.
The European Parliament adopted by 539 v: The European Parliament approved the adoption of the euro by Croatia on 1 January 2023, supporting the Commission's proposal despite challenges from COVID-19 and energy price increases. Parliament commended Croatia's efforts to strengthen its economy and welcomed their Recovery and Resilience Plan.
The European Parliament adopted by 453 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (453-26) to improve EU regulation, focusing on maximizing benefits for citizens, businesses, especially SMEs. The resolution encourages better impact analysis, gender equality, and compliance with the EU's climate neutrality objective.
The European Parliament adopted by 494 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution (494-100) on the progress of the Banking Union, acknowledging the operational status of the first two pillars but emphasizing the need for an established European deposit insurance scheme. Progress towards completing the banking union is supported, with parallel advancements urged in all areas. The Parliament expressed concern about the impact of the Russian invasion of Ukraine on the EU banking sector and called for close monitoring by relevant authorities.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament approved a resolution, passing by a majority of 484 votes to 52, focusing on the financial activities of the European Investment Bank (EIB). The resolution emphasizes the EIB's role as the EU's public bank, highlights its record investment of nearly €95 billion in 2021, and encourages focus on climate change, social cohesion, and digital transformation. Parliament also called for increased EIB support for Ukraine in response to Russia's invasion, welcoming emergency measures providing €668 million in immediate financial aid and a commitment to disburse an additional €1.3 billion.
The European Parliament adopted by 438 v: European Parliament passes resolution on combating intersectional discrimination, emphasizing the need for EU policies addressing multiple forms of discrimination against women of diverse ethnicities. Calls for a mainstreaming mechanism, EU framework, and guidelines to promote an intersectional approach in policy-making.
The European Parliament adopted by 479 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 479 votes in favor and 81 against, urging Bosnia and Herzegovina to advance on EU membership requirements, focusing on democratic institution function, rule of law, anti-corruption efforts, media freedom, civil society support, and protection of vulnerable groups. The Parliament expressed concern over ongoing divisions, secessionist tendencies, and corruption in the country, while reiterating support for Bosnia and Herzegovina's democratic transformation through European integration. The resolution emphasized respect for the Dayton Peace Agreement and condemned statements threatening Bosnia and Herzegovina's statehood and constitutional values.
The European Parliament adopted by 572 v: The European Parliament approved temporary trade liberalization measures for seven agricultural products from Moldova, aiming to increase EU market access. The affected products include tomatoes, garlic, table grapes, apples, cherries, plums, and grape juice. The regulation provides additional duty-free quotas to redirect trade towards the EU.
The European Parliament adopted by 602 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution aimed at improving food security in developing countries, particularly those affected by conflicts and pandemics. The EU was urged to prioritize the right to food, promote self-sufficiency, and support sustainable food systems, with a focus on vulnerable groups like women and family farmers. The crisis exacerbated by Russia's aggression in Ukraine is highlighted as a significant threat to global food security.
The European Parliament decided by 555 v: The European Parliament approved, with 555 votes in favor and 20 against, an amendment to its Rules of Procedure allowing for remote attendance at committee meetings under certain conditions, excluding those held in camera. The amendment ensures members can exercise their mandate, uses technology-neutral solutions, employs secure Parliament services, provides adequate audio/video quality, and requires appropriate locations for intervention.
The European Parliament adopted by 477 v: The European Parliament approved the extension and renewal of the Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreement between the EU and Cook Islands, allowing EU vessels to fish tuna in Cook Islands waters for three years. The agreement is worth approximately €2.1 million over three years.
The European Parliament adopted by 620 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution, passing with 620 votes in favor, 10 against, and 9 abstentions. This vote amends Regulation 508/2014 to help EU member states mitigate the impact of Russia's military aggression on Ukraine, particularly on fishing activities and market disruptions in fishery and aquaculture products. The approved measures allow for financial compensation to recognized producers affected by these disruptions.
The European Parliament adopted by 450 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (450-132) to challenge national vetoes undermining the global tax deal, aiming to reform the international tax system through a two-pillar solution addressing digital economy challenges. However, Hungary and initially Poland opposed the EU law implementing this agreement.
The European Parliament adopted by 520 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 520 votes in favor and 24 against, addressing economic hardships and civil rights issues in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Province. The resolution condemns the suppression of local leaders, civil society, and journalists under President Emomali Rahmon. Protests erupted in May 2022 due to abuses against the community, which were met with violent crackdowns by law enforcement agencies.
The European Parliament adopted by 362 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 362 votes in favor and 16 against, condemning the violence against indigenous and environmental defenders in Brazil, particularly the killing of Dom Phillips and Bruno Pereira. The resolution calls attention to the ongoing conflicts in the Javari Valley, caused by organized crime and illegal activities like deforestation for agricultural land used for commodities such as beef, soy, and palm oil.
The European Parliament adopted by 324 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (324-155) safeguarding abortion rights and women's health in the EU, following the US Supreme Court decision overturning Roe v Wade. The text was tabled by several groups, including S&D, Renew, Greens/EFA, and Left, condemning the potential complete bans on abortion in the US.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution condemning the arrests of Cardinal Joseph Zen and trustees of the 612 Humanitarian Relief Fund in Hong Kong. They called for targeted sanctions against officials responsible for the ongoing human rights crackdown.
The European Parliament adopted by 417 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution for a new EU Forest Strategy by 2030, aiming to enhance sustainable forest management in Europe, contributing to the Green Deal and Biodiversity Strategy goals. The strategy focuses on creating green growth, jobs, and achieving carbon neutrality by 2050.
The European Parliament has adopted by 5: The European Parliament passed a resolution (522-49) to focus on EU border regions as key drivers for integration, emphasizing the need for targeted funding, local involvement, and tailored strategies. A proposed 'borderland billion' aims to allocate 0.26% of the EU's cohesion policy budget for border region development from 2028-2034.
The European Parliament adopted by 488 v: The European Parliament approved a recommendation, with 488 votes in favor, 37 against, and 106 abstentions, to prioritize EU investment in its Southern Neighborhood. This partnership aims to enhance EU security, stability, prosperity, and climate resilience amid COVID-19 and the Ukraine crisis, focusing on diversifying and decarbonizing energy supplies and strengthening cooperation for mutual benefit.
The European Parliament adopted by 448 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on EU economic cohesion, with 448 votes in favor, 61 against, and 75 abstentions. Members emphasized the need for solid funding for cohesion policy, including resources from the Just Transition Fund, to address new challenges and continue its role. Cohesion policy should not be used to compensate budgetary flexibility issues or face cuts during the crisis. The Parliament also suggested considering two separate parts within the Common Provisions Regulation post-2027 for faster negotiations on future funding.
The European Parliament adopted by 589 v: The European Parliament approved new fishing regulations for Union vessels in the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Organisation's Regulatory Area, endorsing measures adopted by the organisation in 2021. This includes changes to cod and Greenland halibut port inspections, mesh size usage, and serious infringement procedures.
The European Parliament adopted by 497 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution calling for a comprehensive revision of the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), with a focus on securing fresh funds for new policy commitments. They also advocated for incorporating the Social Climate Fund into the EU budget and urged immediate action by Q1 2023. Additionally, Parliament suggested modifications to the MFF, including reflecting the revised financial envelope of the Social Climate Fund throughout the regulation.
The European Parliament adopted by 334 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation aimed at increasing the use of sustainable fuels in EU air transport, setting a target of 85% renewable fuels by 2050 (previously proposed as 63% by 2050). The vote was 334 to 95 with 153 abstentions. The regulation applies to aircraft operators, airports, and aviation fuel suppliers.
The European Parliament adopted by 449 v: The European Parliament approved, with 449 votes in favor and 25 against, a resolution to modernize the International Sugar Agreement of 1992. The changes aim to address discrepancies in voting rights and financial contributions among member countries and rules for the Executive Director appointment.
The European Parliament adopted by 410 v:
The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 410 votes in favor, 131 against, and 42 abstentions, addressing the impact of COVID-19 measures on fundamental rights in the EU during 2020 and 2021. The resolution highlighted concerns over infringements on rights such as movement, privacy, education, work, and social security, increased inequalities, and a rise in racist incidents.

The Parliament also expressed concern about ongoing violations of rule-of-law principles in some Member States, threatening the fair distribution of EU funds. It urged the Commission to use available tools, including the rule of law conditionality mechanism, to address these issues. The resolution strongly condemned severe and systemic violations of rule-of-law principles in certain Member States, posing a danger to fundamental rights and freedoms.
The European Parliament adopted by 565 v: The European Parliament approved entering a €3.2 billion surplus from 2021 into the 2022 budget, emphasizing the need for sound financial management and urging the Commission to allocate funds for Ukraine support and address COVID-19 vaccine procurement issues.
The European Parliament adopted by 581 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation aimed at implementing conservation and management measures for fisheries in the Western and Central Pacific Ocean, as adopted by the Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission (WCPFC). The regulation applies to EU fishing vessels operating within the Convention area.
The European Parliament adopted by 433 v: Parliament passed a resolution, with 433 votes in favor, 123 against, and 28 abstentions, expressing concern over a serious breach of EU values in Hungary due to issues in rule of law, democracy, and fundamental rights. Areas of concern include constitutional and electoral system, judicial independence, corruption, privacy, freedom of expression, academic freedom, religious freedom, association rights, equal treatment, minority rights, migrant rights, and economic and social rights.
The European Parliament adopted by 465 v: The European Parliament approved, with 465 votes in favor and 42 against, a regulation aimed at enhancing the resolvability of banks. Known as the 'Daisy Chain' proposal, it amends rules within the Banking Union to improve the prudential treatment of global systemically important institutions.
The European Parliament adopted by 598 v: The European Parliament passed, with minimal opposition, a directive establishing a uniform system for checking dangerous goods transported by road. The new law aims to ensure safety across Europe and applies to vehicles traveling within or entering member states from third countries, excluding military transports. The directive requires member states to conduct checks throughout their territories while minimizing redundancy and uses a common list of items applicable to the transport of dangerous goods in the Union.
The European Parliament adopted by 392 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation on the statute and funding of European political parties and foundations (recast), allowing parties from outside the EU27 to participate. The regulation also mandates transparency obligations, including publishing political programs and logos on websites, and ensuring gender balance.
The European Parliament adopted by 522 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (522-12, 79 abstentions) addressing the mental health crisis among EU youth due to COVID-19 closures of educational, cultural, and recreational facilities. The resolution emphasizes the need for comprehensive European action to promote mental health in children and young people, including increased funding for education institutions and recruitment of qualified teachers.
The European Parliament adopted by 504 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 504-57, recommending the Commission to establish minimum EU standards for third-party litigation funding (TPLF). This practice, used in various types of litigation, could be utilized more often to support justice access, particularly in high-cost countries and marginalized groups. Regulation of TPLF should align with policies enhancing access to justice, such as lowering legal costs or promoting legal aid.
The European Parliament adopted by 538 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 538 votes in favor and 16 against, condemning the arrest of Bishop Rolando Álvarez in Nicaragua. The text was tabled by multiple groups, including EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens/EFA, ECR, expressing concern over human rights violations and state repression in Nicaragua since 2018.
The European Parliament adopted by 503 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (503-40) to strengthen Europe's industrial competitiveness, focusing on an ambitious industrial policy for a green economy and net-zero emissions. The crisis and Russia's aggression against Ukraine have heightened this need, with a focus on a single market, R&D, SMEs, and securing essential supply chains.
The European Parliament adopted by 555 v: The European Parliament approved an extension of the Fisheries Partnership Agreement between the EU and Mauritius, passing by a large margin (555 votes to 25). This move aims to continue fishing activities amidst ongoing negotiations for a new agreement due to the country's economic reliance on tuna vessels during the pandemic.
The European Parliament adopted by 466 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to establish the New European Bauhaus, a cultural movement promoting sustainable, inclusive, and enjoyable living environments. The project aims to improve quality of life by creating healthy and affordable living spaces, with Member States encouraged to implement it in their national policies.
The European Parliament adopted by 424 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (424 votes, 14 nays, 46 abstentions) on the escalating tension between Taiwan and China, emphasizing their shared values. The resolution condemns China's military exercises and cyber-attacks following US Speaker Nancy Pelosi's visit to Taiwan, which it deems a virtual blockade of Taiwan's air and sea space.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution condemning human rights violations, including forced deportation of civilians and adoption of children, in the context of Russia's aggression against Ukraine. The resolution was tabled by multiple groups, highlighting grave abuses such as 'filtration' processes leading to numerous human rights violations.

The European Parliament passed a resolution condemning human rights violations linked to fossil fuel projects in Uganda and Tanzania, particularly the East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP). The resolution highlighted concerns over displacement, imprisonment of activists, and land seizures.
The European Parliament adopted by 469 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (469 votes in favor, 34 against) aimed at strengthening the EU's efforts against climate change due to extreme weather events like drought and fires. The text was proposed by multiple groups, emphasizing the need for increased ambition on mitigation and adaptation strategies, particularly in water management and food security. The Commission is urged to enhance climate action, focusing on limiting global warming to 1.5°C and fostering resilience against extreme weather conditions.
The European Parliament adopted by 566 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on using new technologies like blockchain for taxation, aiming to enhance transparency, combat tax evasion, and improve administrative procedures. The resolution emphasizes the potential of emerging technologies in fostering intelligent tax practices and improving traceability of transactions.
The European Parliament adopted by 486 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to foster sustainable and competitive EU aquaculture, aiming to increase self-sufficiency and meet global demand for aquatic products. The growth potential should be developed sustainably, considering economic, social, and environmental factors. Aquaculture's contribution to the European Green Deal was emphasized.
The European Parliament adopted by 457 v: The European Parliament approved a strategic partnership with the Horn of Africa (Somalia, Ethiopia, Sudan, Kenya, Uganda, Eritrea, South Sudan, Djibouti) to address common challenges like climate change, terrorism, ethnic tensions, and governance issues. In response to Russia's aggression against Ukraine, the EU is urged to reevaluate its engagement in the region due to the negative impact of Russia's actions on regional security.
The European Parliament adopted by 611 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to establish the AccessibleEU Centre, supporting accessibility policies within the EU internal market by 611 votes to 3. The Centre aims to improve the implementation of existing legislation for people with disabilities in areas such as health, education, and mobility.
The European Parliament adopted by 549 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (549 votes to 28, with 50 abstentions) to strengthen wildlife conservation efforts under CITES. The goal is to eliminate illegal trade in CITES-listed species by 2025, focusing on exotic pets and ensuring sustainable trade within the EU.
The European Parliament adopted by 453 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation aimed at preventing commodities linked to deforestation from entering the EU market. Key additions include expanding the scope to include swine, sheep, goats, poultry, maize, rubber, charcoal, and printed paper products. The regulation also defines 'zero deforestation' as goods produced after December 2019, and requires an impact assessment for potential expansion to other natural ecosystems within a year of implementation.
The European Parliament adopted by 486 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (486 votes to 109, with 38 abstentions) addressing the poor living conditions of Roma people in EU settlements. The resolution calls for immediate action at the national level to improve housing, education, employment, healthcare, and social inclusion for Roma communities, who represent a significant part of the EU population.
The European Parliament adopted by 550 v: The European Parliament affirmed that the right to clean drinking water and sanitation is a human right, emphasizing its importance for public health and human development. The resolution calls for increased prioritization, improved implementation, efficient funding, and public participation to ensure access in developing countries, as well as protection mechanisms at international, regional, and national levels to make this right enforceable.
The European Parliament adopted by 618 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation establishing an EU Single Window for Customs, aiming to streamline cross-border trade and reduce administrative burden on traders. The new system will facilitate information sharing and digital cooperation between customs authorities.
The European Parliament adopted by 469 v: The European Parliament approved a Directive on energy efficiency, aiming to reduce energy consumption by at least 40% in 2030. Member States are required to set binding national contributions to meet these targets and contribute to the Paris Agreement and energy security.
The European Parliament adopted by 596 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation to implement tuna conservation measures in the Indian Ocean, amending three existing regulations. The regulation covers fishing practices, marine species protection, control measures, and vessel requirements.
The European Parliament adopted by 592 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to amend ESI Funds and EFAH rules (CARE), providing flexibility to address migration challenges due to Russian aggression and COVID-19 impact.
The European Parliament adopted by 468 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 468 votes in favor, urging action to strengthen ocean governance and combat biodiversity loss. The text was proposed by multiple groups, including EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens/EFA, and ECR, declaring a climate and environmental emergency. The EU is called upon to lead in protecting the ocean and restoring marine ecosystems.
The European Parliament adopted by 555 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation (555 votes, 42 nays) establishing a unified framework for agricultural statistics. The amended text emphasizes the need for transparent, comprehensive data for agriculture, environment, climate, health, food safety, and UN Sustainable Development Goals.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament approved a resolution on managing space traffic, addressing a global challenge. The resolution emphasizes the need for preventive measures, advanced collision avoidance, increased sensor data, robust data sharing, and debris advancements to ensure safe, secure, and sustainable space operations.
The European Parliament adopted by 418 v: The European Parliament approved a directive aimed at increasing the EU's renewable energy target to at least 45% by 2030. The proposal also includes indicative targets for storage technologies and demand flexibility to enhance integration of renewable energy sources.
The European Parliament adopted by 602 v: The European Parliament has approved a plan to require universal USB-C chargers for mobile devices by 2024, with an extension to laptops by 2026. By 2024, the Commission will also harmonize interoperability requirements for wireless charging to promote technological innovation.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution calling for an immediate end to hostilities in Tigray, Ethiopia, particularly focusing on humanitarian aid for children and displaced people. The resolution also demanded a return to constitutional order, ceasefire monitoring, restoration of basic services, and an end to civilian targeting by all parties involved.

The European Parliament passed a resolution, led by multiple groups, condemning escalating violence and human rights abuses in Haiti due to gang control. The resolution addresses the worsening humanitarian crisis affecting over 1.5 million people.

The European Parliament passed a resolution calling for collective action to address soaring energy prices, exacerbated by Russia's aggression against Ukraine, which is causing hardship for millions of Europeans and Ukrainians. Member States are urged to mitigate the impact on vulnerable citizens and businesses.
The European Parliament adopted resoluti: The European Parliament passed a resolution condemning the death of Mahsa Amini, a woman in Iran arrested by morality police, and called for an impartial investigation into her death and allegations of torture.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution strongly condemning the military junta's violent rule in Myanmar and calling for an end to the state of emergency, restoration of the civilian government, and respect for media freedom. The resolution also urged the release of President Win Myint, Aung San Suu Kyi, and other arrested individuals, as well as the cessation of military attacks and violence against the population, and the dropping of politically motivated charges against journalists.
The European Parliament adopted by 504 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (504 votes, 26 nays) condemning Russia's aggression against Ukraine, emphasizing human rights violations and war crimes. The EU reaffirmed its support for Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
The European Parliament adopted by 363 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to strengthen employment policies, emphasizing investment in quality job creation, inclusive digital and ecological transitions, and support for disadvantaged groups. They called for equal involvement in setting Union-level guidelines and requested adaptations to crisis measures.
The European Parliament adopted by 349 v: The European Parliament rejected a Commission Implementing Regulation extending approval periods for certain pesticides (8-hydroxyquinoline, chlorotoluron, difenoconazole) due to concerns over exceeding implementing powers and disregard of the precautionary principle. The substances were deemed potentially harmful to human health and aquatic life.
The European Parliament adopted by 547 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (547-49) urging the Council to allow Romania and Bulgaria to join the Schengen area, citing discrimination and harm to EU's single market due to continued internal border controls.
The European Parliament adopted by 593 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution updating the EU's 2022 budget, incorporating changes in revenue such as UK contributions and fines, and making adjustments for REPowerEU and Eurojust's mandate extension. Parliament urged faster introduction of new own resources to cover Recovery Instrument costs. Despite parliamentary insistence, the Commission combined revenue updates with ongoing negotiations.
The European Parliament adopted by 564 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution on the rule of law in Malta, five years after the assassination of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. The text was tabled by multiple groups following her murder in 2017.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution calling for urgent transformation of the global energy system, prioritizing investments in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and zero-emissions technologies to combat climate change. Despite increased climate pledges, the UN's emissions gap report predicts a 2.7°C temperature rise if current targets are met, exceeding Paris Agreement goals.
The European Parliament adopted by 447 v: The European Parliament strongly condemned the terrorist attack against LGBTIQ+ individuals in Slovakia, passing a resolution with 447 votes for, 78 against, and 45 abstentions. The resolution calls on the Slovak Government to take significant action against hate crimes towards the LGBTIQ+ community following the murder of two young men.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament condemned the September 30, 2022 coup in Burkina Faso and called for an immediate return to civilian rule. They urged the future government to honor international commitments, particularly on human rights, and to establish a timeline for constitutional order and elections by July 2024.
The European Parliament adopted by 442 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (442 votes to 114) advocating for racial justice, non-discrimination, and anti-racism in the EU. The resolution emphasizes the need for a comprehensive approach to combat all forms of racism and discrimination, including structural and institutional racism, across the EU. The Parliament also reiterated its call for the adoption of a horizontal anti-discrimination directive that has been stalled since 2008.
The European Parliament adopted by 503 v: The European Parliament approved an agreement to modify trade service commitments, incorporating Annex 1 from the Services Domestic Regulation Declaration (December 2021). The parliament consented to this agreement, aiming to reduce unnecessary barriers in trade services.
The European Parliament adopted by 451 v: The European Parliament passed an amendment to regulate the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels in maritime transport, aiming for climate neutrality by 2050. The regulation applies to ships over 5000 gross tonnage, covering 100% of their intra-EU voyages and 50% of voyages between EU and third-country ports. The amendments were referred back for further negotiations.
The European Parliament adopted by 560 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to develop a comprehensive European strategy for the video game industry, aiming to foster growth, innovation, and fair benefits for all actors, particularly focusing on esports and co-productions by EU creators. Funding is provided through the Creative Europe and Horizon Europe programs.
The European Parliament adopted by 596 v: The European Parliament approved an agreement to liberalize road freight transport between the EU and Moldova, replacing existing bilateral agreements.
The European Parliament adopted by 485 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation on alternative fuels infrastructure, setting minimum national targets for deploying charging stations for light-duty vehicles by 2024. The targets include public charging stations in residential areas and those capable of smart and bi-directional charging.
The European Parliament adopted by 534 v: The European Parliament approved, with amendments, the Council's plan to abolish internal border controls between the Schengen area and Croatia. The Parliament also called for evaluations of Croatia's border management, including visits to address allegations of mistreatment and pushbacks of migrants at the borders.
The European Parliament adopted by 577 v: The European Parliament passed a cybersecurity directive aimed at strengthening EU-wide resilience. The directive requires member states to adopt national strategies and establish competent authorities for incident response. It applies to critical sectors like energy, finance, and digital infrastructure.
The European Parliament adopted by 586 v: The European Parliament approved an agreement on road freight transport between the EU and Ukraine, replacing existing bilateral agreements to facilitate transit and liberalize operations. This move aims to address issues faced by Ukrainian drivers due to the ongoing conflict with Russia.
The European Parliament adopted by 421 v: The European Parliament rejected the Council's proposed cuts to the draft EU budget for 2023, opting instead to restore funding levels for various programs and maintain allocations for special reserves. Members emphasized the importance of addressing challenges such as the COVID-19 pandemic, rising inflation, and energy insecurity, with a focus on green investments.
The European Parliament adopted by 553 v: The European Parliament approved a Directive aimed at updating EU financial services directives to align with digital operational resilience requirements. This amendment clarifies ICT risks and ensures consistency across financial entities. The changes aim for legal clarity, adaptability to market developments, and proportionality.
The European Parliament adopted by 556 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with majority support, on the Digital Operational Resilience Regulation (DORA). DORA aims to enhance digital operational resilience for financial entities like banks and insurers by establishing a framework for IT security. It includes uniform requirements for ICT risk management, reporting of major incidents, and voluntary cyber threat reporting.
The European Parliament adopted by 469 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (469-67) to promote regional stability and security in the Middle East. The vote aims to address ongoing conflicts and rivalries in the region, including those in Yemen, Libya, and Syria, involving external actors like Iran, Russia, and Turkey.
The European Parliament adopted by 592 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution on the European Innovation Council's implementation, highlighting concerns about delays in financing for SMEs and changes to the EIC Fund structure. Parliament emphasized the need for a single process for blended finance awards and adequate staffing at the EIC Fund.
The European Parliament adopted by 525 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution to enhance corporate sustainability reporting, requiring large companies and those listed on EU markets to disclose details on environmental, social, human rights, and governance matters. This applies to all large undertakings, listed SMEs (until 2028), and third-country companies with significant operations in the EU.
The European Parliament adopted by 454 v: The European Parliament approved a recommendation, 454-130, to strengthen support for Libya's national reconciliation and border management. Funding of €37 million per year from 2021-2024 is allocated for state-building, human development, and basic health services. The EU aims to prevent migrant deaths in the Mediterranean and supports a UN-led, inclusive Libyan reconciliation process for long-term stability.
The European Parliament adopted by 572 v: The European Parliament approved, by a large margin, an agreement to modify trade concessions with New Zealand following Brexit, ensuring continuity in trade flows. The agreement was finalized in December 2021.
The European Parliament adopted by 631 v: The European Parliament passed a Directive on driver training for goods and passenger vehicles, aiming to improve road safety and driver safety during operations. This codified Directive applies to drivers of Member States and third countries employed by EU-based undertakings in road transport. Exemptions apply when all drivers are locally hired or the vehicle is not used within the Union.
The European Parliament adopted by 474 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to implement the borrowing strategy for NextGenerationEU, the EU's recovery instrument, with 474 votes in favor, 80 against, and 78 abstentions. This program, the largest common EU borrowing initiative, provides loans to Member States and direct Union budget expenditure, making the EU a significant player on financial markets. The Commission's swift development and implementation of this extensive funding program has been commended.
The European Parliament adopted by 471 v: The European Parliament approved amendments to integrate REPowerEU chapters into recovery and resilience plans, prioritizing energy poverty reduction and fuel diversification from Russia. The plan should outline reforms and investments from February 2022 with milestones, targets, and quantified energy savings.
The European Parliament adopted by 461 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 461 votes in favor, aiming to strengthen Europe's financial architecture for development due to increased funding gaps for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and other global challenges. Recognizing insufficient EU efforts, they called for international cooperation to address these issues effectively.
The European Parliament adopted by 595 v: The European Parliament approved a Directive aimed at enhancing resilience of critical entities in the EU market by 595 votes, with 24 abstentions. The Directive sets harmonized minimum rules for critical entities, requires Member States to identify and support them, establishes common cooperation procedures, and harmonizes the definition of critical infrastructure across the EU.
The European Parliament adopted by 519 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to consent to the Protocol for the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) to participate in certain Union programs, with 519 votes in favor, 23 against, and 92 abstentions. This Protocol sets financial and technical rules for the Palestinian Authority's involvement, with contributions to the EU budget and adherence to Union program conditions.
The European Parliament adopted by 502 v: The European Parliament approved a strategy update for EU enlargement by 502 votes to 75, aiming to strengthen its geopolitical stance against growing Russian threats. In response to Russia's aggression towards Ukraine, Ukraine and Moldova were granted candidate status, while Georgia's European perspective was recognized. The updated policy aims for flexibility, dynamism, and rewards in the enlargement process while maintaining merit-based accession.
The European Parliament adopted by 609 v: The European Parliament approved the extension of cultural cooperation provisions within the EU-South Korea Free Trade Agreement. The decision was passed with 609 votes in favor, 6 against, and 18 abstentions.
The European Parliament adopted by 608 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation extending fishing access restrictions in Union waters, passing by 608 votes to 13 with 9 abstentions. This aims to preserve sensitive coastal communities and local economies of outermost regions.
The European Parliament adopted a resolu: The European Parliament passed a resolution to improve prevention, management, and care for diabetes in the EU, aiming to address widespread discrimination against those living with the condition. The resolution emphasized the need for an EU legal framework against such discrimination.
The European Parliament adopted by 626 v: The European Parliament passed a regulation to strengthen national standardization bodies' roles in European Standardization Organizations (ESOs) decision-making processes regarding European standards and deliverables. The amended proposal ensures that decisions on accepting/refusing standardization requests, new work items, and adopting/revising/withdrawing European standards are made exclusively by representatives of national standardization bodies within the relevant ESO decision-making body.
The European Parliament adopted by 540 v: The European Parliament passed a decision (540 votes to 6, with 36 abstentions) to reject Russian passports issued from occupied regions, specifically Crimea, Sevastopol, Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, Zaporizhzhia in Ukraine, Abkhazia and South Ossetia in Georgia. The Commission is tasked with creating a list of these unacceptable travel documents per region or territory.
The European Parliament adopted by 440 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to increase the carbon border adjustment mechanism revenue to 100% of its sale value and consider it as an own resource for the EU budget. If the OECD/G20 Pillar 1 Agreement ratification process isn't underway in a significant number of countries by 2023, the Commission will propose a new digital levy or similar measure to generate revenue by 2026.
The Committee on Budgets adopted by 539: The European Parliament adopted a resolution, passing it by a large margin, to strengthen the Union Civil Protection Mechanism and provide additional measures in response to the consequences of the Russian war in Ukraine. This draft budget also includes revenue adjustments and technical updates.
The European Parliament adopted by 416 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, with 416 votes in favor, 124 against, and 33 abstentions, urging action to address Hungary's rule of law issues under the Conditionality Regulation. The Council is called upon to implement proposed measures, and the Commission should act on other rule of law breaches, particularly those concerning judicial independence.
The European Parliament adopted by 494 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (494-58) recognizing Russia as a state sponsor of terrorism, due to alleged attacks against civilians in Ukraine. The resolution demands an end to military actions, withdrawal of forces, and respect for Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
The European Parliament adopted by 490 v: The European Parliament approved a resolution to extend EU budget guarantees for financial assistance to Ukraine in 2023 and 2024, providing continued support amidst Russia's aggression.
The European Parliament adopted by 500 v: The European Parliament approved a regulation to establish a unified borrowing method for financial assistance programs, aiming to simplify financing and better address urgent needs like Ukraine's.
The European Parliament adopted by 522 v: The European Parliament approved the 2030 Digital Decade Policy Programme, aiming to create a favorable environment for innovation and investment, with a focus on human-centered digital transformation across the EU. The program establishes a cooperation mechanism among the Parliament, Council, Commission, and Member States.
The European Parliament has adopted a re: The European Parliament has passed a resolution, collectively tabled by multiple groups, condemning the repression of democratic opposition and civil society in Belarus. The resolution calls for an end to violence, release of political prisoners including Nobel Peace Prize laureate Ales Bialiatski, and cessation of Belarus' involvement in Russia's war against Ukraine.
The European Parliament adopted by 507 v: The European Parliament approved a Regulation to provide financial aid to Ukraine for 2023, passing with 507 votes in favor, 38 against, and 26 abstentions. This aid includes loans, non-repayable support, and interest rate subsidies. The aim is to offer short-term relief, fund post-war reconstruction (where necessary), and support Ukraine's path towards European integration, focusing on macro-financial stability, reforms, and good governance.
The European Parliament decided not to o: The European Parliament approved changes to the Commission's Delegated Regulation on OTC derivative contracts, aiming to ease liquidity strains for energy companies amid rising commodity prices and volatility. This decision follows a request from the Commission to temporarily amend the regulation to alleviate burdens on energy firms.
The European Parliament adopted by 306 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution (306-225) to protect livestock farming and large carnivores in Europe, emphasizing the need for balanced coexistence. The text calls for preventing animal suffering due to attacks by large carnivores, and encourages cross-border collaboration with harmonized monitoring methods.
The European Parliament adopted by 326 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 326-46, condemning Egypt's ongoing human rights violations, particularly during COP27. The resolution called for the release of detained journalists, closure of case 173/2011, and an end to arrests for consensual sexual relations.
The European Parliament adopted by 303 v: The European Parliament passed a resolution, 303-209, modernizing the Energy Charter Treaty (ECT) to improve investment protection standards, limit fossil fuel protection, and promote sustainable development. The agreement was reached in principle on June 24, 2022.
The European Parliament adopted by 532 v: The European Parliament condemned the deterioration of human rights, particularly women's rights in Afghanistan, including the ban on girls' education. They called for an end to gender-based restrictions, respect for women's participation in public life, and upholding Taliban promises on education. The resolution also denounced attacks on activists, journalists, minorities, and peaceful protests.
